		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p>Graduates of the Health Educator Program have put their HED experience to use in many ways. &nbsp;We are very proud of the accomplishments of our alumni and feel that each person who enters the program has unlimited potential.&nbsp;</p> <h3 class="s7">Class of Fall 2011</h3> <p><em><strong>Jacqueline Pascual</strong></em>, Union City, CA <br> I am starting a raw vegan Mexican delivery service in Las Vegas, NV.</p> <p><em><strong>Rosie Tait</strong></em>, Gateshead, UK<br> I completed the Health Educators course in the Fall of 2011. Since then I have done some further training and I am now in the process of setting up a business called Living High. I hope to offer detox packages in a variety of formats. I am also in the process of arranging a raw food stall at a local farmers market. The Hippocrates Program will form the basis of my detox packages. I have also done some coaching based on the program. In addition I teach yoga and I am a Thai Yoga Massage Therapist.</p> <p><em><strong>Marty Hall Landau</strong></em>, Palm Beach, FL<br> The day I graduated I was hired to be part of the Guest Service Tearn. I worked with Kathryn for almost a year and while I was working at HHI I realized there was a missing piece for the Life Transformation Program. I prepared a business plan, which I shared with Anna Maria and she gave it to Brian. He called me in to his office and I now am managing the salon on campus. I love that I can support the program with the knowledge from the Health Educator Program and all the experience in the Guest Service Department along with my passion of 40 some years in the beauty industry. I am so grateful for this opportunity.</p> <h3 class="s7">Class of Winter 2012</h3> <p><strong><em>Alida Lopez Parada,</em></strong> Mexico City, Mexico<br> I give lectures about enzymes and detox and nutritional programs (consulting). I teach raw food kitchen classes, sell Life Give products from HHI and raw vegan desserts. I am starting to create a Raw Vegan Ice Cream to sell it in super markets, so I can have my own brand of Ice Cream since we don't have that in Mexico in the whole country.</p> <p><strong><em>Kent Lawrence,</em></strong> New Hampshire, USA<br> I am living mostly raw, growing shoots and sprouts and wheatgrass, and teaching community classes at my local library. Then as the topic comes up in conversation I bring up the living plant diet as HHI practices. Aylin Filliba, Santa Monica, California I am living in Santa Monica, after the HED program I started a raw food chef certification in Matthew Kenney's school will be taking the level 2 soon. Currently I am in the process of writing a blog about health and raw food prep. I am also working with someone who has been to HHI, he found me through the institute and it has been great. I am hoping for more customers.</p> <h3>Class of Summer 2012</h3> <p><strong>Marisa Silverstein,</strong> New Jersey, USA <br> I have started a heath coaching practice, www.reclaimyourcenter.com, and am a member of Luz Delia's Dream Team working on expanding Well-Being world wide­ http://www.bodysystemsdesign.com/page.aspx?ID=566</p> <p><em><strong>Laura A. Bushey, M.A.,</strong></em> Ponte Vedra Beach, FL<br> I am a certified Raw Food chef and health coach, helping people transform their lives, this is my website where you can get more information on my business: www.kitchenoflife.com</p> <p><em><strong>Lolita Skripko,</strong></em> Oceanside, NY <br> Since the Summer 2012 Program I have been an HHI Referral Agent, LifeGive Wholesaler, Assistant Manager at Juice Press &amp; most importantly: role model to friends and family.</p> <p><em><strong>Constanza Vergara,</strong></em> Colombia<br> I'm producing wheatgrass and sprouts for people and a restaurant. I have given three work shops about living food</p> <h3>Class of Fall 2012</h3> <p><em><strong>Cisem Cakir</strong></em>, Turkey <br> I am now directing Gardens of Babylon's Health Center, setting up anew Raw Food Detox program. I am teaching the chefs the new techniques and how to set up a raw food kitchen. We also have a detox specialist here, and we are working together, she is promoting Master Detox(fasting with liquids). So we offer two different kinds of detox and it is going well so far. Still we need a lot of advertising, which we will be working more on that this year.</p> <p><em><strong>Betsy Sheehy</strong></em>, West Palm Beach, FL<br> Right now I am working on the beginning stages of opening the raw food restaurant, which will be a long time in the making- lucky to have it opened and running by this June 2013</p> <p><em><strong>Maya Yasur</strong></em>, Boca Raton, FL<br> Following the Health Educator program I decided that I wanted to stay involved and continue evolving as a part of the Hippocrates Wellness. I am currently working at the front desk at the Oasis therapy center in Hippocrates and am honored to continue being a part of this organization as I experience first hand how it changes lives on a daily basis.</p> <p><em><strong>Jack Cross,</strong></em> Australia<br> I am currently working on the Oasis cruise line as a nutritionist and fitness instructor, helping people transform their bodies and health"</p> <p><em><strong>Dianna Castillo</strong></em>, Vashon, Washington<br> I have continues my work as a an Energy Healer, and now incorporate the knowledge I gained form the Health Educator program about the healing powers of raw and living foods.</p>

		<title><![CDATA[Hippocrates Wellness: Food Is Medicine Conference]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/hippocrates-wellness-food-is-medicine-conference/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p>Brian Clement and Anna Maria Clement of the Hippocrates Wellness, West Palm Beach, Florida have joined forces with the George W. Yu Foundation to host a working meeting of multi-disciplinary experts focused on the metabolic common denominators underlying cancers, Alzheimer's and Diabetes. In addition to scientists, clinical doctors, health experts, Hippocrates Wellness has invited nutrition journalists, writers, public relations and social media experts to build momentum for the public awareness and empowerment regarding the present state of the fight against cancer and the prevention of disease. Working together, there is a unique and genuine opportunity to shift the paradigm in the direction of a universally recognized acceptance to the metabolic approach of cancer. Not only will it have impact on people afflicted with cancer now, but also in the long-range implications of prevention. Though so much evidence points to a defective energy metabolism or bioenergetics in so many diseases and simple nutritional manipulations can play such an important role in reversing poor health and chronic diseases, there is little attention, nor awareness, among the lay public and professionals. The discoveries of new molecules that selectively injure cancer cell energy are too critical to ignore, yet there is no funding to expand the research and development. So the initiative of this meeting is to unite and form the consortium needed to bring these concepts to a broad audience -- the world. Located on a lush 50 acre campus in West Palm Beach, Florida, Hippocrates Wellness is the leader in the field of natural and alternative health care. For over 60 years, we have dedicated our complementary health care and educational programs to "helping people help themselves."</p><div class="k2_video"><div class="ratio-16by9 mb-15 mb-lg-20"><iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/6XZn6ChvkbY" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowfullscreen=""></iframe></div> </div>

		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/from-the-garden-firespike/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p>The showy firespike ornamental bush is a wonderful addition to any garden. Butterflies and hummingbirds cannot resist its bright scarlet red tubular blossoms!&nbsp; This tropical perineal plant can grow up to four feet tall and will grow year-round in zones 10 and higher (South Florida.)&nbsp; Even gardeners in zones 8 and 9 will find them growing back from the ground in the Spring after a typical winter. While it will tolerate partial shade this plant will produce more vibrant red blossoms when in full sun. When planting firespike prepare the soil with lots of rich organic compost and space the bushes two to three feet apart to give them room to grow.&nbsp; Here at Wheatgrass Central we have firespike growing all over our beautiful 50 acre campus. This adds to the serene ambiance of the World’s Premier Health Encounter for the benefit of our guests. Come to Hippocrates and visit our Organic Garden to learn more about plants and enjoy a rejuvenating stay here by surrounding yourself with nature in our immaculately manicured tropical oasis!</p>

		<title><![CDATA[Malabar Spinach]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/malabar-spinach/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p>Malabar spinach is a tropical dark leafy green plant with a sweet, juicy taste much like that of its’ more conventional English cousin. It grows well in hot, humid climates such as south Asia, India as well as here in South Florida. In fact, it gets its’ name from the Malabar Coast of India. Malabar spinach prefers fertile, well-drained soil that is kept moist. Malabar spinach is a creeping vine and is best when trellised.</p>

<p>Malabar spinach is a rich source of vitamins and minerals. It is even more nutritious than conventional (English) spinach. For example, 100 grams of Malabar spinach offers:</p>

<p><strong>• 8000 IU vitamin A which is 267% of the RDA.</strong></p>
<p><strong>• 102 mg vitamin C which is 102% of the RDA.</strong></p>
<p><strong>• 140 mg vitamin B6 (folate) which is 35% of the RDA.</strong></p>
<p><strong>• 100 g manganese, 32% of the RDA.</strong></p>
<p><strong>• 1.2 mg iron which is 15% of the recommended daily allowance (RDA)</strong></p>
<p><strong>• 100 g potassium, 11% of the RDA.</strong></p>
<p><strong>• Calcium, magnesium, copper, beta carotene, antioxidants, phytonutrients, and many more!</strong></p>

<p>Here at Hippocrates Wellness we grow Malabar Spinach in the Organic Garden for the benefit of our guests.</p>

		<title><![CDATA[How to Make Your Own Nut Milk]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/how-to-make-your-own-nut-milk/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p><strong>Nut Milk</strong></p>

<p>This Nut Milk is protein packed and delicious, try it after your next workout!</p>
<p>Yield 7-8 Cups</p>
<p><strong>Ingredients:</strong></p>
<p>2 Cups Raw Almonds (or nuts/seeds of your choice) Soaked Overnight</p>
<p>5 Cups Filtered Water</p>

<p>Optional: Cinnamon</p>

<p><strong>Technique:</strong></p>
<p>1. Rinse the soaked almonds well and place in a high speed blender.</p>
<p>2. Add water.</p>
<p>3. Blend on high for 20 seconds.</p>
<p>4. Remove the pulp by straining through a nut milk bag.</p>
<p>5. Optional: Garnish with cinnamon.</p>
<p>Stir if separation occurs. Keeps in a refrigerator for 3 days.</p>

		<title><![CDATA[Santa Fe Spinach Salad]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/santa-fe-spinach-salad/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p>A delicious summer recipe reminiscent of a warm summer night in Santa Fe. Enjoy!</p>

<p><strong>Taco “Meat”</strong></p>
<p>3 C. Walnuts (soaked and dehydrated)</p>
<p>1-2 Cloves Garlic</p>
<p>2 T. Chili Powder</p>
<p>¼ Tsp. Cayenne</p>
<p>1 Tsp. Braggs Aminos (optional)</p>
<p>1. In a food processor, combine all ingredients</p>
<p>2. Process by pulsing until desired texture is achieved</p>
<p>3. Season to Taste</p>
<p>4. Dehydrate overnight for salad</p>
<p><strong>Red Pepper Tahini Dressing</strong></p>
<p>2 Red Bell Peppers, Roughly Chopped</p>
<p>1 C. Raw Sesame Tahini</p>
<p>1 C. Water</p>
<p>1-2 Cloves Garlic</p>
<p>1 T. Frontier Pizza Seasoning</p>
<p>1 T. Fresh Lemon Juice</p>
<p>2-3 Drops Liquid Stevia Extract</p>
<p>Braggs Aminos, Dulse, or Kelp Granules to Taste</p>
<p>1. In a blender, combine all ingredients</p>
<p>2. Blend well and season to taste</p>
<p>3. Add more water to adjust consistency</p>

<p><strong>To Make the Salad:</strong></p>
<p>Combine Spinach and chopped onions in a bowl, dress with the Red Pepper Tahini Dressing. Sprinkle dehydrated Taco “Meat” on top! Remember it is always important that your ingredients be organic, especially spinach!</p>

		<title><![CDATA[From the Garden - Yes, We Have Some Bananas!]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/from-the-garden-yes-we-have-some-bananas/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p>Here at Wheatgrass Central we are also growing hundreds of fruiting trees of over thirty different varieties spread out all over our beautiful fifty acre tropical campus. We harvest our fruit when it is ripe and in season throughout the year which is delivered to the kitchen for the benefit of our guests. The kitchen puts this fruit out twice a week for breakfast for those guests who are currently in the program.</p>

<img src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/bananas-225x300.jpg" alt="" class="mb-15 mb-lg-20">

<p style="text-align: center;">Hippocrates Wellness's Bananas!</p>
<p>Fruit can be up to 15% of a healthy diet as long as it is picked when it is ripe, it is whole, it is fresh, and organic. Although fruit is not a critical component for a healthy body it can help with the transition from the Standard American Diet (SAD) to the Hippocrates lifestyle. Furthermore, some of our guests may be advised to abstain from fruit for a season depending upon their situation in order to allow the program to be more effective.</p>

<p>The issue with most fruit that is commercially grown for wide spread distribution in large chain supermarkets is that it is often picked weeks or months before it is ripe so that it will have a long shelf life. This allows suppliers to ship the fruit over a larger geographical area for broader distribution which allows them to increase their profits. As the fruit is growing it draws minerals from the tree in the form of sap. If the fruit is picked before it is ripe and then eaten by you it then thinks you are the tree and it begins to draw minerals from you!</p>

<p>This is an excellent reason for you to grow your own food so you can control how it is grown and how it is harvested. When purchasing produce buy locally whenever possible and get to know the growers personally so you can become more aware of their growing and harvesting practices. Come to Hippocrates to get the full download on all the amazing benefits of food when it is properly grown, harvested, and served fresh!</p>

<img src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/mangos1-225x300.jpg" alt="" class="mb-15 mb-lg-20">

<p style="text-align: center;">Hippocrates Wellness's Mangoes!</p>

					<item>
		<title><![CDATA[Hippocrates House Dressing (1)]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/hippocrates-house-dressing-1/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p>This delicious recipe is a&nbsp;favorite among Hippocrates Wellness guests. It is rich in omega 3's and rich in flavor!</p>

<p><strong>Hippocrates House Dressing</strong></p>

<p>Blend at a high speed:</p>

<p>1/4 cup plus 1 Tbsp. lemon juice</p>

<p>1/8 cup Braggs</p>

<p>1 Tbsp. water</p>

<p>3 cloves garlic</p>

<p>2 Tsp. ground yellow mustard seeds</p>

<p>1/8 Tsp. cayenne</p>

<p>While blending slowly add:</p>

<p>3/4 cup of oil blend: olive, flax, hemp</p>



<p>This dressing is thick and creamy and will last in the fridge for 2 weeks. (Double the recipe for easier blending)</p>

<p>Sever over greens or use as mustard!</p>

		<title><![CDATA[What is Glutathione?]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/what-is-glutathione/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p>Dr. Tim Guilford is a practitioner of functional medicine and homeopathy.</p>
<p>A long standing interest in nutrition, detoxification, and oxidative stress led Dr. Guilford to recognition of the important role of Glutathione in human physiology.</p>
<p>Dr. Guilford recently lectured to our guests here at Hippocrates Wellness, and had this to say about GLUTATHIONE; the Body’s Master Antioxidant:</p>
<p>Glutathione (GSH) is a deceptively simple string of 3 amino acids, glutamine, cysteine and glycine. GSH also has a sulfur molecule which binds with toxins and gives it a distinct aroma. &nbsp;Toxic exposure and oxidative stress can deplete glutathione levels resulting in an array of both chronic and acute conditions.</p>

<p><a href="http://hippocratesinst.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/blog5.jpg"><img class="alignnone size-full wp-image-3668" src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/blog5.jpg" alt="blog5" width="375" height="250"></a></p>

<p>I first became aware of glutathione (GSH) while researching the toxicity of mercury. Articles show mercury is removed from cells by binding to GSH. It turns out that GSH plays an important role in detoxifying mercury as well as many other toxins.</p>
<p>Certain enzymes facilitate the binding of GSH to toxins. &nbsp;They work like “match-makers” because they facilitate the introduction of glutathione to materials that could be toxic to cell function. These enzymes are needed to make glutathione in an efficient manner, and they are present in almost every cell in the body. When these enzymes are not formed properly, glutathione production becomes inadequate.</p>

<p>Glutathione is also a very powerful antioxidant. &nbsp;The mitochondria in our cells produce energy, and mitochondria don’t function well without glutathione. GSH prevents the formation of free radicals that can occur during energy production. Fundamental to its role as an antioxidant, GSH converts biochemical free radicals to harmless water. GSH is the primary defense against oxidative stress that can lead to mitochondrial impairment and cellular damage. &nbsp;Without optimal cellular GSH levels, cells are not able to function efficiently.</p>

<p>It has been shown that the amounts of glutathione an individual makes may be a product of heredity. Genetic inefficiency can occur in both the production of glutathione and in the enzymes that facilitate glutathione’s function. Thus heredity and genetic variation may explain why some of us become deficient in glutathione while others don’t.</p>

<p>In addition, toxins like mercury, persistent organic pollutants and mold mycotoxins can also deplete glutathione. The differences in production of glutathione make it understandable why one person in a household may be affected by toxins while others are not. In these situations, my clinical experience has shown that increasing the number of glutathione molecules available for cells, especially immune cells, to function may be helpful.</p>

<p><a href="http://hippocratesinst.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/blog6.jpg"><img class="alignnone size-full wp-image-3667" src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/blog6.jpg" alt="blog6" width="116" height="344"></a></p>
        ]]></content:encoded>

		<title><![CDATA[How to Kick the Coffee Habit]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/how-to-kick-the-coffee-habit/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p></p><ul><p></p>
<p>	</p><li>Caffeine is toxic. Drinking coffee every day is like constantly drinking slow poison. Here is why:<p></p>
<p></p><ul><p></p>
<p>	</p><li>Caffeine is a natural insecticide that the coffee plant produces in order to avoid being eaten by the bugs.</li><p></p>
<p>	</p><li>Caffeine is a neurotoxin and wears away the myelin sheath on your nerves which will lead to nervousness, headaches, sleeplessness, anxiety and other neurological disorders.</li><p></p>
<p>	</p><li>Drinking coffee is acid forming which is a potential carcinogenic challenge to the body.</li><p></p>
<p>	</p><li>Coffee has a diuretic effect on the body which ultimately dehydrates you as your body desperately tries to flush this poison you just drank in an effort to minimize tissue and organ damage.</li><p></p>
<p>	</p><li>Caffeine creates free radicals.</li><p></p>
<p>	</p><li>Drinking coffee causes wrinkles and prematurely ages you.</li><p></p>
<p></p></ul><p></p>
<p><a href="http://hippocratesinst.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/blog3.jpg"><img class="alignnone size-full wp-image-3670" src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/blog3.jpg" alt="blog3" width="318" height="318"></a></p>
<p>A healthy alternative to coffee is Teeccino which is a naturally caffeine free, non-acidic, non-bitter herbal coffee substitute. It's made from organic carob, organic barley, organic chicory, organic Ramon seeds, and natural coffee flavor. Teeccino is good for:</p>
<p></p><ul><p></p>
<p>	</p><li>Natural energy boost - from nutrients, not stimulants.</li><p></p>
<p>	</p><li>Heart healthy potassium and soluble fiber.</li><p></p>
<p>	</p><li>Inulin – naturally from chicory root, supports beneficial microflora that improves digestion, elimination, and intestinal health.</li><p></p>
<p>	</p><li>Add almond milk and stevia if desired.</li><p></p>
<p>	</p><li>Available as an all-purpose grind or in single serving bags.</li><p></p>
<p></p></ul><p></p>
<p>Another excellent alternative to coffee is Dandy Blend which is also a naturally caffeine free, non-acidic, non-bitter herbal coffee substitute. It's made from the roots of dandelion, chicory and beets, and the grains of barley and rye.</p>
<p><a href="http://hippocratesinst.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/blog4.jpg"><img class="alignnone size-full wp-image-3669" src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/blog4.jpg" alt="blog4" width="225" height="300"></a></p>
<p></p><ul><p></p>
<p>	</p><li>Dandy Blend contains over 50 trace minerals in each cup, most of which the body uses to help synthesize compounds needed in metabolism.</li><p></p>
<p>	</p><li>Dandy Blend is the only instant coffee alternative in the United States that contains dandelion root. To Americans, dandelion may be considered a weed, but to people all over the world it is a valued vegetable and highly respected herbal medicine. It is one of the top six herbs in the Chinese medicine chest.</li><p></p>
<p>	</p><li>Dandy Blend is gluten free. Gluten, which is comprised of proteins that are not water-soluble, is left behind in the grounds to be composted during the extracting process, leaving Dandy Blend gluten-free.</li><p></p>
<p></p></ul><p></p>
<p>Coffee is highly addictive and you may experience some discomfort if you try to quit cold turkey. It is a good idea to wean yourself off of coffee slowly in order to minimize the discomfort of the withdrawal effect. You can easily kick the Caffeine Habit in just Two Weeks! Begin brewing ¾ coffee to ¼ Teeccino or Dandy Blend. Gradually decrease coffee and increase Teeccino or Dandy Blend over a two week period until you are caffeine free! You can find Teeccino at The Hippocrates store, and Dandy Blend at Whole Foods, and some natural health food stores.</p>

<p>Come to Hippocrates to get the full download on all our healthy natural alternative protocols</p></li><p></p>
<p></p></ul><p></p>

		<title><![CDATA[How to Grow Asparagus]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/how-to-grow-asparagus/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <h2>How to Grow Asparagus</h2>
<p>By Brian Hetrich Greenhouse Manager</p>

<p>Asparagus has the highest glutathione levels of any food. Glutathione is the master phytochemical and is unmatched in its ability to remove poisons from the body. Asparagus is one of the best cancer-fighting foods. It is also rich in B vitamins, vitamin C, calcium, and iron.</p>

<p>Asparagus is a cool weather perennial crop that thrives in any area having winter ground freezes. If properly planted and cared for it will keep coming back and producing for 20 years or more! Here is how to grow asparagus:</p>

<p>•Choose an area of your yard that is well drained and receives full sun. Prepare a planting bed 5 feet wide by 10 feet deep by removing all grass and roots and then turning in at least 50% well aged compost 12 inches deep into the existing soil. The richer the better.</p>
<p>•Purchase twenty 1-year old ‘Jersey Knight’ or Jersey Giant’ crowns. This should produce enough be adequate for a family of three.</p>
<p>•Soak the crowns in compost tea for 20 minutes prior to planting.</p>
<p>•Make 4 rows 12 inches apart. Plant the crowns 6 inches deep with 24 inch spacing.</p>
<p>•Cover the crowns with 3 inches of soil. After two weeks cover again with another 3 inches of soil. After another two weeks add more soil until the soil is slightly mounded above ground level to allow for settling.</p>
<p>•Cover with mulch so your tender young spears do not have to compete so much with weeds.</p>
<p>•Water regularly. At least once every three days if it is not raining.</p>
<p>•Fertilize three times a year with compost tea or side dress with compost.</p>
<p>•Spray once a week during the growing season with insecticidal soap or pepper spray.</p>
<p>•During the winter months cover with 6 inches of straw or light mulch to provide protection from the cold.</p>
<p>•Don’t harvest any spears in the first two years so that all their energy can be used for establishing deep roots.</p>
<p>•In the third year, harvest one-fourth your crop every week over a four week period. Use a sharp knife to cut the spears at the ground level.</p>
<p>•In the fourth year harvest one-eighth of your crop over an eight week period.</p>

<p>Fresh-picked spears are far more tasty and tender than store-bought ones. Enjoy!</p>

		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/how-reflexology-works/</link>

		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>

            <h2>FOOT REFLEXOLOGY FOR SYSTEM BALANCE AND INCREASED HEALTH</h2>
<p>The origin of reflexology reaches back into ancient Egypt during 2,330 B.C. where inscriptions were discovered in a physician’s tomb (mastaba).</p>

<p>Reflexology is a science and holistic therapy . It is an ancient healing modality that works on the concept that there are reflexes or points on the feet and hands that relate to every organ, gland, and part of the body. A compression technique using the thumb and forefinger is used in reflexology to connect to these points on energy zones in the body. Reflexology works with all the systems of the body.</p>
<h3>How reflexology works:</h3>
<p>1. Chi-energy zones; pressing on points that relate to other parts.</p>
<p>2. Circulation-breaking up congestion in capillaries improving blood flow in the body.</p>
<p>3. Nervous System-relieving tension in the body so that body can respond to in a healthy normal way to stimuli and stress. There is a proven neurological relationship between the skin and organs.</p>
<p>4. Foot problems and tension in the foot relieved.</p>
<h3>What reflexology does:</h3>
<p>1. Relieves stress and tension, produces a “deep” relaxation.</p>
<p>2. Improves circulation and lymph flow.</p>
<p>3. Creates homeostasis that helps a body calm down or wake up.</p>
<p>4. Reduces pain in a foot and create better flexibility.</p>

<img src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/iStock_000052617016_XXXLarge.jpg" alt="" class="mb-15 mb-lg-20">
<p>The feet and hands are used in reflexology because they are a perfect pictures of the body-like a reflex camera shows a small picture of the larger one. There are a wealth of nerve endings in the feet and hands. They are the perfect place to work - a person feels safe. The work is not invasive.</p>

<p>In a reflexology session, deposits (made up of inorganic calcium or phosphorus, uric acid, lactic acid or even pollutants from the air, water, or foods that were not taken care of by lungs, liver kidneys, or skin) that is in the small blood vessels of the extremity. These deposits are pushed against nerve endings during a reflexology session and broken up. There are 7,200 nerve endings in each foot. Nerve endings in the feet have extensive interconnections through the spinal cord and brain with all areas of the body.</p>

<p>Eunice D. Ingham, The founder of the Ingham Method of Reflexology, wrote in an excerpt from “Stories The Feet Can Tell” , 1938. She states “…reflexology is a means of equaling the circulation. We all know circulation is life. Stagnation is death. Everything around us that is alive is in motion.”</p>
<p>Wishing all much balance and healing,</p>

<p>Tricia Martin, LMT</p>

		<title><![CDATA[Psoriatic Arthritis – A Recovery Story]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/psoriatic-arthritis-a-recovery-story/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <h1><strong>Psoriatic Arthritis – A Recovery Story</strong>
<p><em>Psoriatic arthritis: Symptom free without medications</em></p></h1><p></p>
<h3>By Jens Krause, Scharbeutz (Schleswig-Holstein), Germany</h3>
<img src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/jens3-150x150.jpg" alt="" class="mb-15 mb-lg-20">
<p>I recently graduated from the three-week Life Transformation Program at Hippocrates Wellness (HHI) in West Palm Beach, Florida. My journey to health, however, started about one and a half years earlier. At that time I purchased a book entitled LifeForce (in German: WunderLebensMittel) by Brian Clement, PhD, LN. From among all my resources, this one turned out to be one of the most important readings.</p>

<p>For two decades I have been struggling with severe rheumatic symptoms (arthritis, inflammation, agonizing pain) at irregular intervals. One doctor after another was unable to find the cause for my disease and the only diagnosis I was ever given was some issue with a spine disc in my lower back. As a result, I underwent two surgeries in that region in the ‘90s. Unfortunately, these major invasive operations did not alleviate any symptoms. Subsequently, a specialist recommended an artificial disc replacement, a surgery I decided against.</p>

<p>Four years ago, I finally received a diagnosis: psoriatic arthritis. I was prescribed several rheumatic medications (MTX, Remicade and Prednisone), which for the first time in my life, eliminated my symptoms for an extended period. The cost for this relief, however, was high since the combination of drugs produced severe side effects (weak immune system, strong nausea, etc.) Thus, every time I visited my rheumatologist I asked him about lowering the various dosages. Due to a year and a half of repeated requests, the only medication I continued to take was Prednisone. Even with this, I felt something was still off, and my inner voice urged me to do something else. So I decided to go my own way without any help. I slowly reduced my remaining medication to zero and embarked on researching holistic solutions.</p>

<p>I love sports. After reading The China Study by Dr. T. Colin Campbell and watching videos on YouTube about Frank Medrano, a vegan and master of Calisthenics (exercises by using body weight only), I knew that becoming vegan was the first step in the right direction. I read stacks of books and articles to obtain comprehensive information to cover every possible avenue.</p>

<p>In other words, I left no stone unturned to improve my health and changed almost everything in my life. With these changes, my whole world changed as well. I became a vegan with a food intake of 70 – 80% raw. I grew my own sprouts and wheatgrass and started to exercise regularly (calisthenics, mostly outdoors). Additionally, I made sure to avoid any kind of negativity and trained myself to focus on the nicer things in life. Today I no longer watch TV, stopped reading newspapers and ended some toxic relationships. Now I am 43 years old, symptom free and no longer taking any medications. But I was still not satisfied. My inner voice piped up again to ratchet up my efforts. So I decided to go to Hippocrates Wellness (HHI) to learn anything I could about self-recovery.</p>
<p style="text-align: center;"><img src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/jens4-300x225.jpg" alt="" class="mb-15 mb-lg-20">
</p>
<p>Hippocrates is a very peaceful place full of incredible and powerful people. I had a wonderful time and received a thorough education about self-recovery. It will take me some time to understand and digest the whole value of my stay. However, what I know already is that this was one of the best decisions of my life. To paraphrase David Wolfe in the documentary The Healing Effect (you can watch it on FMTV); today you have the choice to go the “best” or the “worst” way (based on A Tale of Two Cities by Charles Dickens). If you choose the “best” way, you will encounter hope and love in the world and get optimal food, water and herbal medicine. This will accelerate you to a destination you could not have imagined before. After staying just three weeks at HHI, I can say with certainty that this place is choosing the “best” way.</p>

<p>PS Many thanks to Maya for editing my article.</p>

            <h2>RE-ENERGIZE WITH ESSENTIAL OILS</h2>
<p><strong>By Maryna Dager</strong></p>
<p>Have you been feeling mentally, emotionally, or physically drained? Here at&nbsp;Hippocrates we learn to fill our everyday life with good vibrations and practice a positive optimistic attitude. Organic food, exercising, yoga, qigong and meditation help us to stay upbeat, strong and full of high frequency energies. Even though many people enjoy the benefits of this lifestyle, from time to time we all can be brought down by stress. Any negative experience can cause loss of energy balance and make us vulnerable to everyday pressure. Practicing meditation and balancing your charkas can alleviate the stress and restore the balance. Aromatherapy can bring your meditation practice to a higher, more intense level where you can listen to your inner self and bring back the inner harmony. Even if you do not practice meditation you can apply essential oils on your skin and activate your body energy centers (chakras) with essential oils. Inhaling the oils or adding them to bath are also efficient ways of using the oils.</p>

<p>Hippocrates has carefully selected for you 7 essential oils for strengthening your energy.&nbsp;To learn how to re-energize with essential oils keep reading!</p>

<img src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/red-150x150.jpg" alt="" class="mb-15 mb-lg-20">
<p><span style="color: #ff0000;">Root chakra, or base chakra is boosted by <strong>Patchouli</strong> oil and associated with full acceptance of life on earth, survival, power to achieve goals, vitality, grounding, satisfaction, material security, stability, primal trust and courage. A dreamy person may become more grounded through healing this chakra, someone who feels weak, lost and powerless may feel more connected to vigor of life. It is important to meditate on the ground while working on this chakra. Rub a few drops of <strong>Patchouli</strong> oil into your feet before meditation to restore the balance. </span>[divider type="blank-spacer" position="hr-circle-left" size="padding-medium" /]</p>

<img src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/orange-150x150.jpg" alt="" class="mb-15 mb-lg-20">
<p><span style="color: #ff6600;">Navel chakra, or sacral chakra relates to primal feelings, sexuality, desire, sensuality, procreation, enthusiasm, relationships, union with nature, openness to others and personal creativity. If you feel you do not enjoy life or your creativity is in stagnation you may need to correct energy imbalance in this chakra. We recommend to put a few drops of sensual <strong>Sandalwood</strong> to lower abdomen where the charka is located.</span>[divider type="blank-spacer" position="hr-circle-left" size="padding-medium" /]</p>
<img src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/yellow-150x150.jpg" alt="" class="mb-15 mb-lg-20">
<p><span style="color: #ffcc00;">When your Solar plexus chakra is weak you may feel you lack control of your life, you may become angry, aggressive or domineering. This chakra is linked to personal power, social identity, influence, authority, self-control, energy, peace, radiance, joy, inner harmony, acceptance of self, action and vitality. Solar plexus chakra is bolstered by purifying <strong>Lemon </strong>oil. Massage some lemon oil into your solar plexus area and let <strong>Lemon</strong> oil restore your peace and personal power.</span>[divider type="blank-spacer" position="hr-circle-left" size="padding-medium" /]</p>

<p><span style="color: #339966;"><img src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/yellow_green-150x150.jpg" alt="" class="mb-15 mb-lg-20"></span></p>
<p>Heart chakra represents unconditional love, forgiveness, compassion, understanding, warmth, sharing, sincerity, devotion, selflessness and love of God or spiritual and divine love. You will know that your heart chakra needs strengthening when you notice that do not allow yourself to open up to others for the fear of being rejected or hurt or when your relationships become clingy and needy. To strengthen weak heart chakra, use <strong>Bergamot</strong> oil at the center of your chest. It will activate this energy center and boost energy circulation.&nbsp;[divider type="blank-spacer" position="hr-circle-left" size="padding-medium" /]</p>

<img src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/blue-150x150.jpg" alt="" class="mb-15 mb-lg-20">
<p><span style="color: #0000ff;">When you are afraid to speak up or stop yourself from asking what you want it may be a sign that your Throat chakra is weak. It is located in throat area and represents free self-expression, communication, inspiration, confidence, freedom, truth and independence. You may reinforce your Throat chakra with invigorating <strong>Peppermint</strong> oil applying a few drops on the base of your throat.</span></p>
<p>[divider type="blank-spacer" position="hr-circle-left" size="padding-medium" /]</p>
<img src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/blue_green-150x150.jpg" alt="" class="mb-15 mb-lg-20">
<p><span style="color: #000080;">The Third eye chakra is concerned with intuition, clairvoyance, imagination, idealism, concentration, peace of mind, projection of will and manifestation. It is located in the middle of forehead between the eyebrows and can be strengthened by clarifying <strong>Rosemary</strong> or <strong>Lavender</strong> oil.</span></p>
<p>[divider type="blank-spacer" position="hr-circle-left" size="padding-medium" /]</p>
<img src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/purple-150x150.jpg" alt="" class="mb-15 mb-lg-20">
<p><span style="color: #800080;">The Crown chakra is located on the top of your head and related to integration with omnipresent being, divine wisdom, bliss, understanding and enlightenment. If you lost the meaning of life, your life may benefit from healing Crown chakra. Apply a few drops of <strong>Frankincense</strong> oil at the base of the skull and behind the ears to fortify your seventh chakra.</span>&nbsp;[divider type="blank-spacer" position="hr-circle-left" size="padding-medium" /]</p>
<p>If you have any questions about essential oils you can always call us to Oasis at 541-471-5867 and we will be happy to share our knowledge of the wonderful world of aromatherapy and consult you about using oils for the best possible results.</p>

            <h3 style="text-align: center;"></h3>
<h1 style="text-align: center;">Spotlight on our 2015 RawFest Sponsors</h1>
<p style="text-align: center;">Join us in the next 4 weeks getting to know the Sponsors for our Annual RawFest, who have graciously stepped up to make this annual event a possibility.&nbsp; We are honored to have them as part of the Hippocrates Community, and appreciate not only what they do, but who they are.</p>

<h3 style="text-align: center;">Join us on October 31, 2015 from 10 AM-4 PM at Hippocrates Annual RawFest</h3>
<h3><strong>Grow Good Health with The Tower Garden</strong></h3>
<p>Tower Garden® simplifies traditional gardening, using a unique vertical garden system that makes it easy to grow your own fresh fruits and vegetables at home.</p>
<p><strong>The vertical garden, powered by aeroponics</strong></p>
<p>Tower Garden gives you more control of your and your family’s health by making it easy to grow nutritious, great-tasting vegetables and fruits at home. And it’s a smart choice, both environmentally and economically.</p>
<p>Because of its unique aeroponic technology and vertical design, Tower Garden uses less than 10% of the water and land required by traditional, soil-based agriculture. And a recent study by the University of Mississippi found it also generates 30% more produce than soil-based growing methods.</p>
<p><strong>Eat local: from Tower to table</strong></p>
<p>It’s tough to get more local than your own backyard! With Tower Garden, eating local has never been easier. Our aeroponic vertical garden system cuts your carbon footprint by recycling natural resources, potentially reducing pesticide use, and virtually eliminating the need to ship and store produce.</p>
<p>For more information on The Tower Garden visit <a href="http://www.JPFL4U.com">http://www.JPFL4U.com </a>click on Tower Garden tab at top of page or contact Christina Daugirdas at (561) 719-1394</p>


<h3><strong>Pure Choice Skin Care</strong></h3>
<p>At <strong>Pure Choice Holistic SkINside-OUT Studio</strong>, we believe every little thing matters that comes into direct contact with your face &amp; body. In today’s stressful &amp; toxic filled world, consumers are hard pressed to find the time in educating themselves about common toxic practices of the cosmetic manufacturing industry today. In contrast, this precise reason is why it is our passion at to take the time to really educate our clients in recognizing what is truly safe for their family’s daily use, both at home and in the treatment room.</p>

<p>Lisa Johnson-Stuart, founder and Master Clinical Esthetician has carefully designed an extraordinarily pure skin care program, setting the standard way above and beyond the competition. This program promotes outstanding results without the need for injecting toxic substances, paying for highly priced treatments or even going under the knife to obtain the benefits of beautiful and radiant skin. ALL our treatments are not only 100% Pure, Organic, Wild-Harvested &amp; Natural but also include an array of methodically selected professional tools and equipment that further enhance each individual’s results. With Lisa’s proper guidance and client’s commitment, the relationships she holds with her clients have proven to be nothing short of highly regarded &amp; respectful. She has established an honest reputation for holistically nurturing all her client’s needs and concerns in the most healing and relaxing environment possible.</p>


<h3><strong>Chunkie Dunkies</strong></h3>
<p>Chunkie Dunkies was an inspiration that came to me after I was fortunate enough to work in the Hippocrates Kitchen and then complete their 9 week Health Educator Course in 2010. Because of my amazing education and new experience with Raw Foods I only wanted to eat food that was simple, clean and pure. But... I still loved my sweeter foods and began experimenting with raw nuts and sprouted buckwheat groats (a Hippocrates staple). Within a short period of time, I created my first raw chocolate chip cookie and I was in heaven! It tasted so good and it only had a few ingredients.</p>

<p>Thought there had to be others out there that craved the same, so I went for it. Within one month I developed 5 new flavors (Carrot Cake, Oatmeal Raisin Walnut, Almond Butter Crunch, Mint Chocolate Chip and Cashew Lemon Cream) and began selling them at the local green market in Palm Beach Gardens, FL.</p>
<p>Now four years later, we offer 13 different products, sold in over 100 locations (which can be found on our website) and sell online at <a href="http://www.chunkiedunkies.com">www.chunkiedunkies.com </a>Our Cookies, Brownies and Biscotti are Raw, Vegan, Gluten-Free, Dairy-Free, Non-GMO, Paleo-Friendly and Kosher, handmade in our<strong> 100% plant-based, gluten-free facility</strong> in Riviera Beach, FL. They are either sweetened with organic maple syrup, organic raw blue agave or liquid stevia (Stevita brand). We currently sell two biscotti flavors in the Hippocrates Store and on their website. <strong>Almond Lemon Cream</strong> and our <strong>Newest Flavor - Vanilla Almond Crunch</strong>. We will continue to grow our stevia line of treats because we know how important it is to have this option available for our health.</p>

<p>I love food, especially when it’s pure and delicious. Our main goal is to continuously educate those that healthy food can be Gourmet and Satisfying. And now, when we are out and about, demonstrating Chunkie Dunkies, nothing puts a smile on my face more than when a new, unsuspecting customer tries a bite for the first time and is WOWED by our flavors. :)</p>

<p>Health &amp; Happiness, Dina Lauro, Founder/Raw Vegan Chef</p>

            <h2>Guarding Yourself From Chemicals</h2>
<h3>By Tina Discepola MD</h3>
<p>It’s not easy to maneuver through the maze of chemical overload in today’s society. There are toxins everywhere! Everything we eat, use on our person or in household has a laundry list of ingredients we know nothing about. The chemical names are foreign to us. We assume they must be safe because they are FDA-approved. Wrong!</p>
<p>Unfortunately, it has become a personal responsibility to become savvy the products we eat and the products that we use. Many of the ingredients below are serious hormonal disrupters, distillates of petroleum (yup, gasoline!), and have significant links to cancers, autoimmune disease, and degenerative neurological problems. Use the following guidelines as a way to keep you and your family as toxin-free as possible.</p>
<h3>Ingredients to Avoid</h3>
<p><strong>BISPHENOL A (BPA):</strong> This is not listed on labels. Found in most canned foods, plastic baby bottles, sippy cups, receipts and thermal paper. Cause severe hormonal disruption and cancer.</p>
<p><strong>PVC and VINYL:</strong>&nbsp;Found in soft plastic toys, shower curtains, flooring.</p>
<p><strong>FORMALDEHYDE:</strong>&nbsp;As known as&nbsp;DMDM hydantoin or diazolidinyl urea.</p>
<p><strong>TRICLOSAN:</strong>&nbsp;Found in antibacterial soaps and products.</p>
<p><strong>PHTHALATES:</strong>&nbsp;May appear as fragrance or parfum. These are serious endocrine disrupting agents and can damage a child’s brain development.</p>
<p><strong>1,4-DIOXANE:</strong>&nbsp;Labeled as sodium laureth sulfate, and polyethylene glycol/PEG.</p>
<p><strong>PFOA:</strong>&nbsp;Found in non-stick pans and stain resistant fabrics or treated fabrics.</p>
<p><strong>PARABENS:</strong>&nbsp;Found in personal care products, including shampoos and lotions.</p>

<img src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/09/iStock_000003150653_Large.jpg" alt="" class="mb-15 mb-lg-20">

<h3>How to To Protect Yourself from Toxins</h3>
<p>1. Don’t use chemical pesticides, period.</p>
<p>2. Use steel or cast-iron cookware. Please avoid NON-stick.</p>
<p>3. Avoid plastics when possible, especially those labeled No 3, 6 or 7. NEVER heat plastic in the microwave, dishwasher, or sun. Find a stainless steel reusable water bottle to carry. Store your food in glass; it’s so much safer. Heat can cause the endocrine disrupting chemicals to leach into food and drink.</p>
<p>4. Avoid handling cash-register receipts and certainly don’t place them in your mouth. BPA transfers easily to the skin and mucosal surfaces. Many stores offer that receipts be emailed to you, a much safer option.</p>
<p>5. Avoid plug-in fragrances at home or work. Keep windows of a new car open until that “new-car smell” (phthalates) is completely gone.</p>
<p>6. Choose household products that do not have warnings of CAUTION, DANGER, or CAUSTIC.</p>
<p>7. Always read the ingredient list. Compare cleaning agents and their ingredients. Choose products that use essential oils for scent.</p>

		<title><![CDATA[The Perfect Fall Dish: Mexicali Quinoa]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/the-perfect-fall-dish-mexicali-quinoa/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>

		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p><strong>Hearty and&nbsp;delicious with a fresh zip, this dish is sure to be a crowd favorite!</strong></p>
<h2>Mexicali Quinoa</h2>
<p><em>Yield: 4 Cups</em></p>

<p>3 C. Sprouted Quinoa</p>

<p>1 C. Corn</p>

<p>1/2&nbsp;Finely Diced Red Onion</p>

<p>1/2&nbsp;C. Thinly Sliced Scallion</p>

<p>1/2&nbsp;C. Finely Diced Red Bell Pepper</p>

<p>1/2&nbsp;C. Chopped Fresh Cilantro</p>

<p>Dressing:</p>

<p>1.5 T. Chopped Scallion</p>

<p>1 Clove Garlic</p>

<p>1 Tsp. Kelp Powder</p>

<p>1 Pinch Cayenne</p>

<p>1/2&nbsp;C. Extra Virgin Olive Oil</p>

<p>3 T. Fresh Lemon Juice</p>
<p></p><ol><p></p>
<p>	</p><li>In a mixing bowl, combine the quinoa, corn, red onion, scallion, red bell pepper, and cilantro.</li><p></p>
<p>	</p><li>In a blender, combine the remaining ingredients. Blend well and season to taste. Add the dressing to the mixing bowl and toss to combine.</li><p></p>
<p></p></ol><p></p>

		<title><![CDATA[Cultivating Compassion]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/cultivating-compassion/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <h2>Cultivating Compassion</h2>
<p><strong>by Brian Clement PhD, LN</strong></p>

<p>When psychologist Carl Jung, on one of his perennial quests, visited Chief Mountain Lake of the Taos Pueblo, the tribal elder told him he judged the whites to be quite mad. “Why is that?” Jung asked. “They say they think with their heads,” the chief replied. “Of course” said Jung, “What do you think with?” Mountain Lake pointed to his heart, “We think here.” (See reference at end of article)</p>

<p>Most of us believe that wisdom of the heart is learned by experience and employed with charm, but cultures the world over have forever thought and spoken from a place of compassion rather than calculated intellect. The “civilized” have often diminished the importance of the so-called “uncultured” by placing a wedge between them. In common thought, they are looked down upon as naïve and ignorant. When people express themselves clearly and openly, they are often perceived as childlike, which should be a compliment but unfortunately is seen as a detriment.</p>

<img src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/09/iStock_000004133340_Large-200x300.jpg" alt="" class="mb-15 mb-lg-20">
<p>All of humanity’s self-imposed problems bubble up from our addiction to and admiration of cerebral activity. All greatness and resolution from the beginning of time has poured out of the heart. When you consciously peruse the past, our most beloved figures have employed their hearts in the utmost way to raise humanity. In the Eastern Orthodox tradition, “the heart is not only the core of a human being, but is identified with the mind itself.” In biblical terms, “As a man thinks in his heart, so is he.” (Proverbs 23:7) Similarly, the Japanese have two words for heart: shinzu, the physical organ and kokoro, the mind of the heart. Marc Ian Barasch in his landmark book Field Notes on the Compassionate Life poses the question, “Does the heart have a mind of its own?” He goes on to describe how neuroscience has long known: that the two hemispheres of the brain think somewhat independently – the right side being, in a sense, more heartful, specializing in emotional-intuitive functions; the left leaning more toward rationality and logic. The idea of heartfulness as an independent form, a cognition, was illustrated, in a widely reported 1986 experiment. A test group of college students was first shown a documentary about Mother Teresa. Immediately afterward, their saliva revealed increased levels of S-IgA, an immune system boosting hormone. The conclusion reached in the popular press was, “Compassion makes you feel good and it’s good for you.” But the media reports overlooked an intriguing fact: Most of the students said they’d found the film depressing. After seeing it, they reported a decrease in feelings of love and contentment and an increase in “overall negative mood.” They found the plight of the poorest of the poor, the sick and the dying of Calcutta’s slums, deeply dispiriting. Mother Teresa’s rigid religiosity made some uncomfortable. The surprise was this: Both the students who had negative reactions and those who had positive ones showed the same immune system enhancement.</p>



<p>In the rolling hills of Northern California sits the Institute of HeartMath. Its mission statement: “to illumine the mind with the heart’s knowing.” The organization’s enigmatic founder, Doc Childre, often says that love is not enough – it is the care that makes it real. The Institute’s teachings are backed by some hard research reported in such periodicals as the American Journal of Cardiology. Cardiologists have for years been studying subtle beat-to-beat irregularities in heart rhythms called heart-rate variability (HRV), mostly as a diagnostic tool to measure nervous system aging and emotional stress. Doc added a key insight to this already well-established methodology: Different HRV patterns seem to correlate with specific emotional states, in particular those that psychologists call the qualia, such as compassion, love, and forgiveness. Measuring inner states with instrumentation is nothing new. EEGs have shown that alpha and theta rhythms in the brain are associated with the calming effects of meditation, yoga and prayer, commonly known as the “relaxation response” named by Harvard Medical School’s, Herbert Benson, M.D.&nbsp; HeartMath’s research added a new dimension. Measures of HRV show that the patterns generated by altruism and compassion are distinctly different from relaxed meditative states. Researchers claim that states of mind (or better yet, states of heart) have more to do with caring about others than with seeking inner peace. These feelings also generate far greater health-promoting effects on the immune system and autonomic nervous system. Rollin McCraty, one of HeartMath’s researchers, states “love and caring drive the entire bodily system to oscillate at its resonant frequency, a purported state of harmony between brain and body that can be scientifically measured.” He further asserts that emotion is faster than thought. This rings with truth, since there are many examples in daily life that display this reality. Primate researcher Frans de Waals “perception-action model” suggests that it is both apes’ and humans’ emotions, including empathy, that trigger a physical response before any conscious decision has been reached. Psychologist Jonathan Haidt also reflects on this by calling it a “heart-over-head hypothesis.” He describes this as a social intuitionalist model, and believes that we first have an emotionally colored intuition followed by intellectual justification. In effect, the heart has already decided what feeling, course or action is to be taken. The heart apparently is the viewing side of the binoculars which leads us to intellectually paint the picture and consciously manifest the already concluded reaction.</p>

<p>As stated in Compassion: A Reflection on the Christian Life by Nouwen, McNeill, and Morrison, “Patience is the discipline of compassion.” Christian patriarch St. Markious of Egypt stated that the heart’s greatest potentials lie dormant. For the uncultivated, he wrote in the The Philokalia, “The heart is a tomb and there our thought and intellect are buried.” One Buddhist analogy states:</p>

<p><em>Your beliefs become your thoughts</em></p>

<p><em>Your thoughts become your words</em></p>

<p><em>Your words become your actions</em></p>

<p><em>Your actions become your habits</em></p>

<p><em>Your habits become your&nbsp;character</em></p>

<p><em>Your character becomes your destiny</em></p>

<p>Character was never more eminently displayed than at Calvary. One of the most overlooked events that occurred at Christ’s oblation on the cross was when he offered his flesh as love’s ransom. This keenly portrays the body as a vessel that carries the spirit which houses positive emotion. Positive emotion is that which is manufactured in the heart and compassionately distributed to self and others. Prayer, meditation, contemplation and random acts of kindness will all open the heart and resolve the mental emotional disparity. We should not be a slave to habitual mindset, but a friend of flowing compassion.</p>

<p>The biblical Moses serves as an ageless example of compassionate action. With his story, we can observe a 40-year struggle between his mind and his heart. Although God himself spoke to him and asked him to lead his people, his cerebral nature gnawed at him continually surfacing doubt, skepticism and fear. As we know, the heart superseded the mind and the end result was a nirvanic experience. Patience, being the representation of compassion, should be Moses’ middle name.</p>

<img src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/09/iStock_000035367318_Large-300x200.jpg" alt="" class="mb-15 mb-lg-20">
<p>Compassion goes well beyond moral decision-making. It is an irresistible force that breaks down the thickest fortress which separates us from ourselves and others. Psychologist Pumla Gobodo-Madzikela, a member of the South African Truth and Reconciliation Commission, took it upon herself to interview the jailed former secretary chief of the apartheid regime, Eugene de Kock, chief planner and sometimes trigger man in the government’s brutal shadow war. De Kock masterminded the infamous Vlakplaas “death farm” where the most brutal murders and tortures took place. With his own hands he had killed and maimed many. For the horror he had visited on so many, he had become known to the public as a representative of “Prime Evil.” Madzikela’s prison interviews began as a detached study of a specimen of inhuman detritus through a psychological microscope. After being convicted as a common criminal, de Kock surprised everyone when he asked to meet the widows of three black policemen whom he killed by planting a bomb. One of the wives told Madzikela shortly after her meeting with de Kock, “I could not control my tears. I could hear him, but I was overwhelmed by emotion and I was just nodding as a way of saying, ‘Yes, I forgive you.’ I hope that when he saw our tears he knew that they are not only tears for our husbands, but tears for him.” The widow’s response went beyond empathy; she had offered de Kock a priceless gift, a re-entry into the human community. “I would like to hold him by the hand, and show him that there is a future and that he can change,” she said.</p>

<p>In the effort to heal, your foremost friend is a compassionate heart. It acts as an endless reserve contributing to the continual cycle we call life. It is for us to create the very existence in which we flourish, at all times contributing our most sincere heartfulness. There is seldom a time when we can so succinctly spotlight the central ingredient that displaces the fabricated burdens of the mind, replacing them with the godliness and persistence of the heart.</p>



<p><strong>Foundational information for this article is from:</strong></p>

<p>Field Notes on the Compassionate Life: A Search for the Soul of Kindness, Marc Ian Barasch, Rodale Press, 2005.</p>

<p>Compassion: A Reflection on the Christian Life, Henri J.M. Nouwen, Donald P. McNeill&nbsp; and Douglas A. Morrison, Image Books- Doubleday, New York.1966.</p>

		<title><![CDATA[Lacinato Kale Ribbons]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/lacinato-kale-ribbons/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <h2>Lacinato Kale Ribbons</h2>
<p>Yield: 6 Cups</p>
<h3>Ingredients:</h3>
<p>5 C. Chiffonade Lacinato Kale</p>

<p>1 C. Greek Sun-Dried Olives, Pitted &amp; Chopped</p>

<p>1/2&nbsp;Pepper (Either Red, Yellow, or Orange)</p>

<p>1/4&nbsp;Onion</p>

<p>1 C. Whole Leaf Dulse, Snipped Into Pieces</p>

<p>1/2&nbsp;C. Hippocrates House Dressing</p>
<p></p><ol><p></p>
<p>	</p><li>In a Mixing Bowl, add a little dressing at a time and massage into the kale to soften texture. Next, combine all ingredients. Mix well and season to taste.</li><p></p>
<p></p></ol><p></p>

<h3>Hippocrates House Dressing:</h3>
<p>Blend at high speed:</p>

<p>¼ cup plus 1 T Lemon Juice</p>

<p>1/8 cup Braggs</p>

<p>1 T. Water</p>

<p>3 Cloves Garlic</p>

<p>2 tsp Ground Yellow Mustard Seeds</p>

<p>1/8 tsp Cayenne</p>

<p>While Blending Slowly Add:</p>

<p>¾ cup of oil blend: olive, flax, hemp</p>


<h3>This dressing is thick and creamy and will last in the fridge for 2 weeks.</h3>

		<title><![CDATA[Tight Clothing’s Link To Health Problems]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/tight-clothing-s-link-to-health-problems/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <h2><strong>Tight Clothing’s Link To Health Problems</strong></h2>
<p>What if everything you thought you knew about bras and breast cancer turned out to be wrong? Can you question your long-held assumptions and personal habits, but more importantly, make necessary lifestyle corrections that will protect and improve your health? Is putting your ‘chest eggs in a tight nest,’ as breasts in bras are sometimes equated, really necessary or even healthy?</p>

<p>These are the kinds of questions that Dr. Elizabeth R. Vaughan began asking herself and her patients over a decade ago. Her background and upbringing isn’t that of someone who might ordinarily be expected to become a maverick health care provider, much less one who challenges conventional health wisdom with passionate conviction. She’s the daughter of two physicians, a descendant of four generations of physicians, whose great-grandfather was president of the American Medical Association. But her provocative outside-the-mainstream ideas about bras, toxins, and breast cancer prompted <em>USA Today</em> to call her “the Erin Brockovich of medicine.” You might recall Erin Brockovich as the legal crusader who defied conventional wisdom and exposed the toxic contamination of an entire town, and whose story was later told in a movie starring Julia Roberts.</p>

<img src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/09/iStock_000034580562Large.jpg" alt="" class="mb-15 mb-lg-20">
<p>What Dr. Vaughan, CEO of Vaughan Medical Center in Greensboro, N.C., began to notice was a relationship between the development of breast lumps/cysts and the wearing of&nbsp; bras. She personally treated more than 100 women who, in her words, “chose to go bra free after yet another biopsy of a lump in their breasts or aspiration of a cyst. Over 3-6 months, their breast cysts/lumps got smaller and less tender and they developed no new lumps that we could detect.” Dr. Vaughan’s observation has since been demonstrated in practice by other health care providers.</p>

<p>Breast cysts may be one of the flashing red warning signs for the onset of breast cancer. A 1999 study in the prestigious British medical journal, <em>The Lancet</em>, examined 1,374 women with breast cysts and tracked them based on their incidence of breast cancer. It was found that premenopausal women with breast cysts had a nearly 6-fold increased risk of breast cancer compared to women who didn’t have breast cysts. Here is how the authors of this study succinctly summarized their findings: “Women with breast cysts are at an increased risk of breast cancer.”</p>

<p>That shouldn’t come as a surprise given that most women wear bras which are much too tight for them and have worn them this way since they received their first ‘training bra’ as a young girl. According to The Johns Hopkins University Breast Center, “as many as 80 percent of women are actually wearing a bra that is the wrong size for them,” a chronic condition that can produce health problems, particularly in the backs of women with large breasts.</p>

<p>With a connection possibly established between breast cysts and breast cancer, along with Dr. Vaughan’s findings that bras cause or exacerbate the development of breast cysts, you don’t need to be the Sherlock Holmes of common sense to grasp that bras, lymphatic drainage impairment, breast cysts, and breast cancer may be linked, much like a chain reaction automobile wreck.</p>

<p>A key circumstantial piece of evidence showing a link between bras and breast cancer emerged in 1991 from a study of breast size and breast cancer risk by researchers in the Department of Epidemiology at the Harvard School of Public Health. Published in the <em>European Journal of Cancer</em>, this survey of thousands of women found that, “Premenopausal women who do not wear bras had half the risk of breast cancer compared to bra users.”</p>

<p>The study authors speculated this could be because these premenopausal women are “thinner and likely to have smaller breasts.” But that observation received little or no support from subsequent medical studies. As the director of The Johns Hopkins University Breast Center declared in 2007: “Simply having breasts and being female places all women at risk. Women with size 32AA bras get breast cancer just like someone with 46DDs.”</p>

<p>This Harvard study finding about bra usage and a higher risk for breast cancer should have set off alarm bells within the health field and the clothing industry. At the very least, it should have spawned a spate of new studies exploring this connection between bra use and breast cancer. But it caused barely a ripple in public health awareness. Once again, as in the Emperor’s New Clothes, reflexive rejection and obstinate denial had triumphed over reality and common sense.</p>
<h1><img src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/09/Bra-Front-2-273x300.jpg" alt="" class="mb-15 mb-lg-20">
<p><strong>New Options for Breast Health</strong></p></h1><p></p>
<p>At Hippocrates Wellness our line of organic bras are made with luxuriously soft organic cotton that is free of of chemicals, heavy metals, bleach, and harmful dyes to ensure they are as PURE FOR YOUR SKIN as possible. Our elastic free design is great for women with latex sensitivities and elastic irritations. The bras are underwire free for all-day comfort and better breast health. Specially designed to promote lymph flow throughout the body and ergonomically designed to support the body’s anatomy for overall health. The breathable organic fibers help to regulate your body temperature and allow the skin to eliminate toxins naturally which is important in preventing inflammation and stagnancy in the body.</p>

<p>We offer several styles to choose from, including designs for every day wear, sportswear, as well as maternity and mastectomy wear. In addition to these current styles, we will continue to expand our line with new and attractive designs for every women’s physique.</p>

<p>To order or to learn more about our organic bras, go<strong> <a href="http://hippocratesinst.org/product-category/organic-clothing">here</a></strong>&nbsp;or call our Hippocrates store at: 877-582-5850 (in the USA) or 561-623-1019</p>

<p>To stay up-to-date with our latest offerings, follow our “Ohganix” organic apparel brand online @Ohganix.</p>

            <h2>Sichuan (Szechaun) Mustard Greens</h2>
<h3><strong>Almond Ginger Dressing</strong></h3>
<p>Yield: 4 Cups</p>
<p>2 C. Chopped Bell Pepper</p>
<p>1 C. Raw Almond Butter</p>
<p>1/2 C. Chopped Scallion</p>
<p>1/4 C. Chopped Red Beet</p>
<p>2 T. Chopped Ginger</p>
<p>1 Clove Garlic</p>
<p>1 1/2 T. Kelp Powder</p>
<p>1 C. Water</p>
<p>1 T. Braggs Aminos or Nama Shoya (optional)</p>
<p>1/2 T. Fresh Lemon Juice</p>
<p>Cayenne to taste</p>
<h3>Technique</h3>
<p>1. Dress fresh organic mustard greens with the Almond Ginger Dressing.</p>

<p>2. Garnish with chopped dehydrated almonds.</p>

<p>Enjoy!</p>

		<title><![CDATA[Stay Young Longer!]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/stay-young-longer/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <h2>Stay Young Longer!</h2>
<h2>Raw Food For Smart, Busy People</h2>
<h3>by Cherie Soria</h3>
<p>Most people hesitate to make healthful dietary changes if it takes too much time, they think it is too restrictive, or they are afraid the foods will be tasteless and unappealing. People tend to enjoy foods that provide the level of flavor, texture and visual appeal they are accustomed to. Who can blame them? Unless they are in a life-threatening situation, it’s hard for anyone to give up the foods they love. In fact, people may refuse to make dietary changes even when facing death.</p>

<p>Today, smart, busy people all over the world are discovering that raw food doesn’t need to be flavorless or take a lot of time to prepare. What may have been considered a fad diet 10 years ago is now recognized as a revolutionary new cuisine that is nurturing to both body and spirit.</p>

<p>People everywhere are sick and tired of being ‘sick and tired’ and they are eager to learn how to take control of their health and make better food choices. However, since they aren’t willing to give up the flavor, texture and appearance of the foods they love, they’re delighted to find raw foods that can be both delicious and nutritious, and they begin to make positive changes that they can immediately feel in terms of increased energy and well being. The answer is as simple as knowing where to start, what to eat and what (and when) not to eat.</p>
<h3>Where to Start…</h3>
<p>Start right here, right now. The raw food lifestyle doesn’t need to be 100% raw, 100% of the time. Include both raw and cooked plant-based foods. How much raw food is needed to maintain good health and stay young and vibrant depends on each person’s starting point and what their health goals are. For most of us, it isn’t just how much raw food we eat; it’s also which raw foods we choose, which cooked foods we consume, and  (equally important) which foods we choose not to eat. The truth is that some cooked foods are better choices than certain raw foods. For example, lightly steamed broccoli is a healthier choice than raw cashew cheesecake, which is primarily sugar and fat. It doesn’t matter that the fat is raw and the sugar is natural; it’s important to remember that foods like raw cheesecake are for celebration rather than everyday consumption. Knowing what foods to eat and what foods not to eat isn’t difficult if you know a few simple rules.</p>
<h3>What to Eat…</h3>
<p>Our bodies are high-performance vehicles that need the best fuel possible to ensure maximum performance and long life. Of all the steps anyone can take to look younger, feel more vibrant and joyful, and have clear beautiful skin and healthy hair and nails, one thing stands out among  the rest — raw plant foods.</p>
<p style="text-align: center;"><img src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/09/iStock_000029852510_Large.jpg" alt="" class="mb-15 mb-lg-20">
</p>
<p>Fresh, ripe, raw, organic, colorful plant foods contribute nutrients important for clear skin, vivid eyesight, a sharp mind and radiant health as we age. Many of these nutrients act as antioxidants, helping protect our cells from free radicals (highly reactive molecules that contain unpaired electrons, which can damage cells and cause premature aging). Let’s take a look at a few high performing fruits and vegetables.</p>

<p>Deeply colored foods high in phytonutrients and antioxidants combat free-radical damage and promote good health and healing:</p>

<p>Dark blue or purple foods: beets, blueberries, blackberries and black mission figs</p>

<p>Dark green leafy vegetables:</p>

<p>collard greens, kale, bok choy,  broccoli and Napa cabbage</p>

<p>Yellow-orange foods: squash, peaches, sweet potatoes and carrots</p>

<p>Red foods: tomatoes, bell peppers, watermelon and strawberries</p>

<p>Foods high in vitamin C: lemons, oranges, strawberries, papaya, kiwi, broccoli, Brussels sprouts, tomatoes, red bell peppers, romaine lettuce, kale and mustard greens</p>

<p>Foods containing omega 3 fatty acids: chia seeds, flax, hemp seeds and dark green leafy  vegetables like kale, romaine and dandelion greens</p>

<p>Foods containing zinc: pumpkin seeds, sesame seeds, sunflower seeds, pine nuts and lentils</p>

<p>Hydrating foods: juicy fruits, non-starchy vegetables, non-chlorinated drinking water and fresh green juice</p>

<p>Probiotic-rich foods: sauerkraut, grain-free miso and fermented vegetables</p>
<h3>What not to eat …</h3>
<p>Animal proteins: meat, eggs, and dairy products  (raw or cooked)</p>

<p>Foods high in concentrated sugars (raw or cooked)</p>

<p>Foods devoid of nutrients: refined wheat and other high-gluten products (pasta, pizza and pastries)</p>

<p>Fried foods and high-fat foods: nuts that are cooked at temperatures above 240 degrees Fahrenheit</p>

<p>GMO foods and conventionally grown (non-organic) foods</p>

<p>Don’t make alcohol consumption part of your daily routine</p>

<p>Eat foods that are easy to digest and won’t interfere with sleep, and do not eat anything late at night</p>

<p>What cooked foods can I include?</p>

<p>Lightly steamed vegetables: broccoli, yams, and squash</p>

<p>Non-glutinous ancient grains: quinoa and millet</p>

<p>Legumes: lentils, adzuki beans and mung beans</p>

<p>What makes raw food tasty?</p>

<p>We want contrast and excitement in the foods we eat, whether they are raw or cooked, so include these:</p>

<p>Pair crunchy and creamy foods together, like crispy cucumbers with guacamole or flax crackers with raw nut cheese</p>

<p>Contrasting flavors like a sweet and sour salad dressing on bitter greens</p>

<p>Dramatic, pungent flavors like garlic, onion or chili</p>

<p>Raw foods offer the best quality fuel for good health, healing from disease and anti-aging — and the best part is, they can also be delicious! Why wait until you are old or sick to try to get healthy, when you can enjoy great taste and excellent health NOW?</p>
