		<title><![CDATA[The Hippocrates Herbal Tea Guide]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/the-hippocrates-herbal-tea-guide/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p>If you are like most people, reaching for that hot cup to sip in the morning is a top priority to getting the day started. While most drinks like coffee and black teas are popular for the morning jumpstart, switching out the caffeinated beverages with an herbal tea can be soothing and comforting, while also providing your body with antioxidants and other medicinal properties that promote health. The simple aroma from a freshly brewed cup of herbal tea invokes in us a calm and warmth, and helps provide a feeling of peace and relaxation. Aside from the pleasure herbal teas provide, they also offer healing properties, and because they are naturally caffeine-free, they are suitable for drinking any time of the day.</p>

<p>One of the easiest and most nutritious ways to drink herbal teas is by infusing the herbs in hot water for at least 10 minutes, and up to 8 hours maximum. Studies have shown that it takes at least four hours for a significant amount of minerals to extract into the water, releasing the medicinal constituents. These long herbal infusions draw out the most significant amounts of vitamins, enzymes and essential oils. Depending on how much time and preparation needed, at least 10 minutes of steeping is necessary to extract any medicinal properties, and allowing the herb to steep at least 8 hours will extract the most nutrients.</p>

<p>There are many beneficial herbs that provide medicinal properties for different ailments and different herbs are better suited for steeping for longer periods of time.</p>

<p>If you are looking for a quick and easy herbal tea, the following herbs are simple and effective with at least 10 minutes of steeping time:</p>
<p></p><ul><p></p>
<p> 	</p><li><strong>Peppermint:</strong> improves digestion, prevents nausea and vomiting, boosts immunity</li><p></p>
<p> 	</p><li><strong>Ginger:</strong> supports digestions, eases pain, increases weight loss, enhances immunity</li><p></p>
<p> 	</p><li><strong>Echinacea:</strong> boosts the immune system, reduces redness and swelling, promotes cell health</li><p></p>
<p> 	</p><li><strong>Rooibos:</strong> lowers blood pressure, improves bone &amp; heart health, balances blood sugar</li><p></p>
<p> 	</p><li><strong>Chamomile:</strong> induces sleep, antispasmodic &amp; anti-inflammatory, relieves stress &amp; anxiety</li><p></p>
<p></p></ul><p></p>
<p>When you start steeping the herbs for four hours or longer, the medicinal constituents (phytochemicals) become primarily nutritive rather than stimulating/sedating. This also gives these nourishing long infusions their characteristic tastes: bland, sweet or earthy. These types of herbal infusions can be used on a regular basis. The following herbs are popular to use for long herbal infusions:</p>
<p></p><ul><p></p>
<p> 	</p><li><strong>Oatstraw:</strong> relieves insomnia, anxiety and ADHD; helps combat obesity, varicose veins and irritations to the digestive tract</li><p></p>
<p> 	</p><li><strong>Nettle:</strong> treats arthritis and joint pain, antihistamine and anti-inflammatory qualities, used to treat bladder infections</li><p></p>
<p> 	</p><li><strong>Comfrey:</strong> strengthens and heals bones, reduces pain, anti-inflammatory, boosts immune system</li><p></p>
<p> 	</p><li><strong>Red Clover:</strong> eases anxiety, relieves muscle and joint pain, prevents osteoporosis and strokes</li><p></p>
<p></p></ul><p></p>
<p>These are just a few of the more popular herbs that are used to make herbal teas and infusions and by experimenting and trying new ones, you are sure to find a few favorites that you enjoy. Tea drinking has been around for thousands of years and is not only used for its medicinal properties, but is valued for everyday pleasure and refreshment. Incorporating a time in your day to savor a cup of herbal tea is a great way to improve your overall health and wellbeing. This daily ritual will help you feel rooted in mindfulness, respect and living in the moment while also reducing stress.</p>



<p>Article by Andrea Nison</p>

		<title><![CDATA[Raw Vegan Sauerkraut]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/raw-vegan-sauerkraut/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p class="image-center" style="line-height: 14.25pt;">Are you looking to stay away from heavy or sugary&nbsp;salad dressings? Sauerkraut can be a perfect alternative. Enjoy it as a&nbsp;fat free dressing rich in probiotics that is great for digestion. Add it to your salad&nbsp;whole (shredded) or even blended.</p>
<p class="image-center" style="line-height: 14.25pt;">This delicious recipe yields 4-5 cups!</p>
<p class="image-center" style="line-height: 14.25pt;">Ingredients:</p>
<p>1 Head Red Cabbage, Shredded</p>
<p>1/2 Apple, Seeded</p>
<p>Kombu Seaweed, Soaked, As Needed</p>
<p>Outer Cabbage Leaves, As Needed</p>

<p>1.&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Place half of the shredded&nbsp;cabbage in a ceramic or glass&nbsp;container.</p>
<p>2.&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Press down firmly.</p>
<p>3.&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Place the apple in the center of the cabbage.</p>
<p>4.&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Place the remaining ½ of the shredded cabbage on top, always pressing it down firmly.</p>
<p>5.&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Cover the top of the cabbage with a layer of hydrated kombu seaweed.</p>
<p>6.&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;On top of the kombu, place a layer of cabbage leaves.</p>
<p>7.&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Place a heavy weight on top of the cabbage leaves, making sure that the entire container is covered so that no foreign matter can enter the kraut. The cabbage will begin to foam and bubble as a result of the fermentation process.</p>
<p>8.&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Leave out at room temperature.</p>
<p>9.&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;After 3-5days (if ready), discard the cabbage leaves, kombu, and apple in the middle.</p>
<p>10.&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Place the sauerkraut in a&nbsp;container for storage and&nbsp;refrigerate.</p>

					<item>
		<title><![CDATA[Fermented Foods and Your Health]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/fermented-foods-and-your-health/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p>The process of fermenting foods has been a common practice throughout nearly every civilization. Different cultures have adopted methods and use different foods to ferment. In Japan, natto is a common dish made with soybeans and commonly eaten as a breakfast food. Russians love kvass, which is made using stale, sourdough or rye bread or beets and has been around since the Middle Ages. In West African countries, garri is made from a root vegetable, and if not prepared properly, it can be poisonous.</p>

<p>Fermentation is a method of pre-digestion that takes place when there are beneficial bacteria naturally present, or even a yeast strain, which breaks down the starch and sugars in the food. As these bacteria divide, the process forms lactic acid, which is described as lacto-fermentation. This lactic acid halts the growth of bad bacteria and also gives the fermented foods that “tangy” or “acidic” taste.</p>
<blockquote>This fermenting process increases the digestibility of the foods by neutralizing plant toxins and is incredibly rich in beneficial bacteria and probiotics. Adding these fermented foods to your diet can boost immunity, while also assisting the body in detoxification.</blockquote>
<p>Fermenting your own foods is a great practice to incorporate to your health routine. It’s very simple and you only need a few ingredients to get started. Most store-bought fermented foods have been preserved in vinegar and they are not as beneficial as the traditional recipes with naturally occurring bacteria. Storing these fermented foods is simple and as long as they are covered in the liquid brine and stored in a cool dark place, they can last for months and even up to years!</p>

<p>Here at Hippocrates Wellness, we love the selection of sauerkraut, kimchi and other fermented foods that are available on our raw, living foods buffet. &nbsp;Here is a long-standing sauerkraut recipe from our Hippocrates kitchen:</p>

<p>Hippocrates Raw Vegan Sauerkraut</p>

<p>Ingredients:</p>

<p>1 Head Red Cabbage, Shredded</p>
<p>1/2 Apple, Seeded</p>
<p>Kombu Seaweed, Soaked, As Needed</p>
<p>Outer Cabbage Leaves, As Needed</p>
<p></p><ol><p></p>
<p> 	</p><li>&nbsp;Place half of the shredded&nbsp;cabbage in a ceramic or glass&nbsp;container.<p></p>
<p>2.&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Press down firmly.</p>
<p>3.&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Place the apple in the center of the cabbage.</p>
<p>4.&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Place the remaining ½ of the shredded cabbage on top, always pressing it down firmly.</p>
<p>5.&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Cover the top of the cabbage with a layer of hydrated kombu seaweed.</p>
<p>6.&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;On top of the kombu, place a layer of cabbage leaves.</p>
<p>7.&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Place a heavy weight on top of the cabbage leaves, making sure that the entire container is covered so that no foreign matter can enter the kraut. The cabbage will begin to foam and bubble as a result of the fermentation process.</p>
<p>8.&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;Leave out at room temperature.</p>
<p>9.&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;After 3-5 days (if ready), discard the cabbage leaves, kombu, and apple in the middle.</p>
<p>10.&nbsp;&nbsp;Place the sauerkraut in a&nbsp;container for storage and&nbsp;refrigerate.</p></li><p></p>
<p></p></ol><p></p>






<p>Article by Andrea Nison</p>

					<item>
		<title><![CDATA[Your Mood and Food]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/your-mood-and-food/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <h3>When overeating is driven by emotional hunger.</h3>
<p>We all enjoy eating and, on occasion, will eat when not hungry or overeat just because the food&nbsp;is incredibly tasty or because it enhances our personal or social experiences. An afternoon out with a good friend is certainly more enjoyable with a vegan treat. What would a good movie be&nbsp;without some airpoped popcorn? There’s nothing wrong with occasionally using food to enhance enjoyment and celebrate life. The problem arises when we use food in this way so often that we are overweight or our health is at risk. If you regularly eat when you’re not hungry, overeat at meals, or choose to&nbsp;eat unhealthy comfort foods more often than you’d prefer, there’s a chance you’re eating has an emotional component to it. A craving—or an exaggerated desire to eat in the absence of true physiological hunger cues—represents an emotional appetite. Emotional hunger often feels the same as physical hunger.</p>

<p>As an emotional eater, you may treat food as a coping tool in a number of ways:</p>

<p>• To dull or tranquilize emotions that are difficult to cope with, such as anxiety, anger, sadness, frustration, hopelessness, loneliness, shame, guilt and even happiness and joy</p>

<p>• To calm yourself when experiencing unpleasant sensations such as nervousness, agitation or muscle tension</p>

<p>• To soothe and comfort yourself</p>

<p>• For pleasure, escape and excitement</p>

<p>• To handle stress</p>

<p>• To silence negative, critical, self-defeating thoughts and quiet your mind</p>

<p>• To manage feeling overwhelmed</p>

<p>• To distract yourself from low-motivation states like boredom, lethargy and apathy</p>

<p>• To procrastinate</p>

<p>• Because your life lacks purpose, meaning, passion or inspiration</p>

<p>• Because you feel so much regret regarding your life</p>

<p>• Because you feel deprived in life and want to have no limits</p>

<p>• To try to fill up an inner emptiness</p>

<p>• To reward or punish yourself</p>

<p>• To rebel against someone or something</p>

<p>• To ward off sexual attention</p>

<p>• To feel safe.</p>

<p>Many emotional eaters believe&nbsp;eating challenges are the result of factors outside their control. Some people simply love food. Some say they have no time to eat healthy and exercise while working full-time and raising a family. Others say there’s constantly unhealthy, high-fat food around them and it’s just too tempt-ing. Others still say that eating healthy in restaurants without off ending others is nearly impossible.</p>

<p>While these factors are reasonable and may play a part in your overeating, they do not represent the true cause of your inability to regulate your intake. Emotional eating highlights a difficulty in connecting to yourself; in paying attention to your mind, body, and spirit signals; and in responding appropriately to meet your needs. It’s a sign that you’re lacking self-care skills that are generally learned in childhood.</p>

<p>No doubt, your emotional eating has helped you cope daily with emotional states like anxiety and depression, general stress and self-defeating thoughts. But it isn’t a very effective long-term strategy for meeting your needs and desires. Not only does it lead to poor health and weight gain, but it also can never be a substitute for learned skills. Unfortunately, you won’t learn more effective self-care skills by going on another diet, either! Focusing on external solutions, such as the latest diet or exercise regimen, is like trying to solve the problem of a stalled train by giving it a new coat of paint and polishing its wheels. No matter how much paint or polish we apply, the train will remain stuck.</p>

<p>We need to access the&nbsp;engine that drives the train and accurately diagnose the problem. It’s our inner world of emotions, sensations, needs and thoughts that drive our behavior. In order to understand and resolve the behavior of emotional eating, we have to tune in to and explore our inner world.</p>
<h3>3 STEPS TO ADDRESS YOUR EMOTIONAL EATING</h3>
<p><strong>1. ASK YOURSELF: “What am I feeling in this moment?” </strong></p>

<p>Perhaps you just had an argument with your spouse and now all you can think about is ice cream. Pull away from the kitchen and grab pen and paper. Sit upright and ground yourself. Feel your rear in the seat and your feet planted firmly on the floor. Jot down what you’re feeling—both emotions and bodily sensations. Research shows the act of writing down your feelings helps regulate your nervous system and interrupt wayward behaviors. You write that you’re feeling angry, frustrated, hurt, drained, lonely and sad. You notice your head hurts, your shoulders are tense and your stomach is in a knot. Ask the noisy, thought-generating part of your brain to be quiet for a moment. Notice your breathing. Inhale relaxation; exhale tension. Try placing one hand on your heart and one hand on an area of tension. You’re beginning to calm down.</p>

<p><strong>2. ASK YOURSELF “What do I need in this situation?” </strong></p>

<p>See if you can identify a need you can meet yourself, rather than one that involves someone else. For example, rather than writing that you need your spouse to be less reactive, you might write that you need peace and harmony in your relationship. Maybe you need hope that things can improve. It may take some flexibility and creativity. It’s often easier to meet physical needs than emotional needs. The more you let go of rigid expectations, the more you’ll open yourself up to a satisfying solution.</p>

<p><strong>3. TELL YOURSELF “My feelings are valid and my needs can be met.” </strong></p>

<p>Access an inner supportive voice—the mature, wise, kind and loving part of you. Using this voice, jot down a few validating, hopeful statements: “It makes sense to feel hurt and angry when my spouse yells at me. The truth is, we both prefer peace and harmony. Let’s revisit this discussion on the week-end when we’re both more relaxed.” When the urge for food is strong, there is an opportunity to practice</p>
<p>and build new self-care skills. Every time you practice these skills, you’re wiring-in new neural patterns, making it easier to calm and set limits with yourself. If you’ve been looking outside yourself for the loving kindness and nurturance you crave, you will discover that your true source lies within.</p>





<p>BY JULIE M. SIMON</p>

		<title><![CDATA[Healthy By Design]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/healthy-by-design/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <h3>All it takes to be healthier than yesterday is a step in the right direction.</h3>
<p>No&nbsp;matter where we are with our health, we can always get better. We can lose weight, feel terrific, eat&nbsp;more, sleep better, and be energized with</p>
<p>no notion of a lotion or a potion. And this can be done easily. Unless you’ve stayed in the hospital, I bet you never knew there were so many kinds of physicians—cardiologists, endocrinologists and pathologists, to name a few. One function of a pathologist in particular is to study the history and evolution of disease. When we abuse ourselves for long periods of time, we get little “stings” in the form of headaches, colds, bad breath, low energy, bad nerves and insomnia. When we continue this abuse, we look for something to make us better, instead of wondering what</p>
<p>in the world we are doing that’s making us sick. Then we get a bigger sting. Eventually, we really get stung and can wind up with cancer, heart disease, diabetes or strokes, thinking we inherited them.</p>

<p>I myself was chairman of the board of that mindset for years. I was a sick, fat, miserable, unhealthy kid, and thought being healthy was something for the select few (or you were just born into it).</p>

<p><strong>STAGES OF DISEASE</strong></p>

<p>Well, now is the time for us to understand how disease forms over time. These are the six stages of pathology in a nutshell:</p>

<p>1. ENERVATION. In this stage, you’ll just feel tired and irritable. You need more sleep, you get more colds and you may wonder why you’re suffering from bad breath, gas and constipation. You probably also find yourself with a short temper because your nerves are shot.</p>

<p>2. IRRITATION. Your physical body is beginning to reflect your health. You may suffer from sore joints, rapid heart rate and migraines or severe headaches.</p>

<p>3. INFLAMMATION. This is often your body’s first line of defense against allergens and disease. You’ll have red sores around cuts, pimples, shortness of breath, fever and inflamed areas around the kidneys, lungs and liver.</p>

<p>4. ULCERATION. Ulcers will appear in the stomach, lungs, liver and other organs. You’ll also be dealing with a lot of pus and boils.</p>

<p>5. INDURATION. By this point, hormonal glands are barely active. You’ll be suffering from the formation of fibroid tissues, as well as poor arterial blood flow, senility and tumors.</p>

<p>6. FUNGATION. This is where life is hanging by a thread. The intelligence of the cell, the DNA, has lost control and can no longer guide cellular function.</p>

<p>THE GOOD NEWS Diagnosis defines conditions of a disease. Prognosis defines the chances of survival. Prognosis of stage four is usually terminal. The good news is that at every stage, disease is still reversible.</p>

<p>Since we are all healthy by design and sick by default, it stands to reason that we want to be well and it would be good to stop making ourselves sick. But we need&nbsp;to want health in a special way, because we only pursue what we want when the want is greater than the effort.</p>

<p>All success starts with a beginning. Everyone who got where they are had to begin where they were. Opportunities are all around you.</p>

<p>Develop tendencies toward action. Break your big plan into small steps and take the first step right away. You can make&nbsp;something happen right now. A journey of a thousand miles begins with one step. Take one.</p>

<p>We all know that what you do from Christmas to New Year’s doesn’t matter that much, but what we do from New Year’s to Christmas really matters. Let go of perfection and settle for excellence, knowing that excellence is no accident.</p>



<p>B Y WAYNE PICKERING, ND, ScM</p>

		<title><![CDATA[Optimal Nutrition with Raw Vegan]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/optimal-nutrition-with-raw-vegan/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <h2>Why is everyone talking about going vegan? What are the benefits&nbsp;when eating a raw vegan diet?</h2>
<h3>Raw vegan foods help to provide:&nbsp;More Energy</h3>
<p>When we eat raw vegan&nbsp;foods that are easier for our bodies to digest, assimilate, and eliminate, we have more energy left over. This enables our body to cleanse, heal, and repair itself so we feel healthy, vital, and energized.</p>
<h3>Fiber</h3>
<p>• Fiber is the indigestible portion of plant foods. Fruits, vegetables, sprouts, nuts, and seeds contain an abundance of dietary fiber.</p>
<p>• Fiber acts as a pre-biotic agent. This helps to populate beneficial bacteria in the gut for supporting immune and gastro-intestinal function.</p>
<p>• Fiber helps to regulate blood sugar by allowing the carbohydrates in food to be released into the bloodstream more gradually.</p>
<p>• Fiber helps to lower cholesterol.</p>
<p>• Fiber also keeps everything moving through the intestines, which prevents constipation.</p>
<h4>Two main categories of fiber</h4>
<p><strong>• Soluble</strong></p>
<p>-This type of fiber actually binds to cholesterol in the intestines and flushes it out of the body</p>
<p><strong>• Insoluble</strong></p>
<p>-&nbsp;Is good for regularity</p>
<p>-&nbsp;Insoluble fiber helps “bulk up” the stool and prevent constipation</p>
<h3>Vitamins and Minerals</h3>
<p>Raw and living foods are very high in various vitamins and minerals. Sprouted foods have a very high nutrient-per-calorie ratio, which help us feel satisfied on fewer calories. This is in addition to having a high water and fiber content.</p>

<p>We all know many of the other benefits of vitamins and minerals.</p>
<p>• Vitamins and minerals found in raw fruits, vegetables, nuts, and seeds are in a whole food complex with cofactors.</p>
<p>– They are abundant and absorbable</p>
<p>– They are synergistic in their effects</p>
<h3>Alkaline Minerals</h3>
<p>• Fruits and vegetables contain beneficial alkaline minerals such as:</p>
<p>– Magnesium</p>
<p>– Calcium</p>
<p>• Most of the byproducts of metabolism in our bodies are acidic.</p>
<p>• Consuming alkaline foods helps counteract this acidity.</p>
<p>• Without minerals, vitamins have no function.</p>
<p>• Research indicates that calcium from our bones is often used to counteract this acidity, so eating foods that have an alkalizing effect may contribute to the maintenance of bone health.</p>
<h3>Phytonutrients</h3>
<p>• Raw vegan foods are very high in phytonutrients. Phytonutrients contain protective, disease-preventing compounds that interact with other plant nutrients to produce a synergy that can help fight many diseases. Some phytonutrients are lycopene, beta-carotene, and chlorophyll.</p>
<p>Chlorophyll is the green coloring in plants</p>
<p>– Helps to build blood</p>
<p>– Has antioxidant properties</p>
<p>– Has antibacterial, anti-fungal and anti-inflammatory benefits.</p>
<h3>Carotenoids</h3>
<p>– A group of phytonutrients that have yellow, orange, and red pigments</p>
<p>– Act as antioxidants in the body</p>
<p>– Yellow pigments – lutein and zeaxanthin</p>
<p>*&nbsp;They help to support optimal vision.</p>
<p>*&nbsp;The body utilizes these pigments to protect the back of the eyeball from the damaging rays of the sun (the macula).</p>
<p>*&nbsp;These two pigments work together synergistically to confer this protection.</p>
<p>*&nbsp;Are best obtained from yellow and green vegetables like summer squash and leafy greens.</p>
<h3>Antioxidants</h3>
<p>Raw and living foods contain antioxidants which reduce free radical damage and help us age gracefully. Many phytonutrients also act as antioxidants. Antioxidants counteract the damaging effects of “free radicals.”</p>
<h3>Alkalinity</h3>
<p>Raw and living foods help to maintain the proper alkaline pH in the bloodstream, which is very beneficial to the body in a number of ways, such as supporting energy.</p>
<h3 style="text-align: left;">Calorie Density</h3>
<p>• Calorie density is defined as the amount of calories in a given weight or volume of food.</p>
<p>• Filling our stomach helps activate stretch receptors which is one of the primary mechanisms that helps us feel satisfied.</p>
<p>• Three primary factors that determine calorie density</p>
<p>– Water content</p>
<p>– Fat content</p>
<p>– Fiber content</p>
<p>• Water is by far the most significant determinant of calorie density, and raw and living foods have excellent water content.</p>
<p>• It is interesting to note that despite the high fat content, rich and creamy avocados still have less than half of the calorie density of brown rice cakes, indicating how water content plays a bigger role in calorie density than fat content does.</p>
<p>• The fiber content of a food contributes to the calorie density as well, but not as much as fat and not nearly as much as water.</p>
<p>– Including lots of water and fiber rich raw vegan and living foods in one’s diet makes it easy to feel full and satisfied without eating excess calories.</p>
<h3>Plant Fats</h3>
<p>• Higher fat raw plant foods, such as avocados and nuts and seeds, contain relatively healthy, unsaturated fats.</p>
<p>• These high fat plant foods contain plenty of their own fiber, which binds to excess cholesterol.</p>
<p>• Essential fatty acids:</p>
<p>– Two types of fats that the body cannot make, so they need to be obtained from diet. These are called essential fatty acids (EFAs).</p>
<p>*&nbsp;<strong>Alpha linolenic acid</strong> – <a href="https://hippocratesinst.org/shop/naturesage-omega-3-oil">Omega 3</a>.&nbsp;Omega 3 fats reduce inflammation.</p>
<p>* <strong>Linoleic acid</strong> – Omega 6.&nbsp;&nbsp;Omega 6 fats generally promote inflammation.</p>
<p>– Ideal ratio of omega 6 to omega 3 fats is between 1 to 1 and 4 to 1.</p>
<p>– When we consume in excess of four times the amount of omega 6 fats compared to omega 3 fats, we tend to create excess inflammation.</p>
<p>– Omega 6 fats</p>
<p>*&nbsp;The average American consumes 20 times more omega 6 fats than omega 3 fats.</p>
<p>*&nbsp;Omega 6 fats are largely found in animal products and processed foods.</p>
<p>– Omega 3 fats</p>
<p>* Omega 3 fats are abundant in leafy green vegetables, flax seeds, chia seeds, hemp seeds, and certain types of algae.</p>
<p>* Smaller amounts of omega 3 fats can be found in fruits and non-green vegetables.</p>
<p>• The standard American diet (SAD) diet contains an over-abundance of omega 6 fats from:</p>
<p>– Processed foods.</p>
<p>– Commercially produced animal products.</p>
<p>– Not enough fruits, vegetables.</p>
<p>* They contain the omega 3 fats that reduce inflammation.</p>

<p>A diet based on raw fruits, vegetables, nuts, and seeds, and especially a diet that has an abundance of greens and includes some flax or chia seeds, supplies adequate amounts of omega 3 fats. This is without the excess of omega 6 fats, which is seen in typical modern human diets.</p>
<h4>Healthy fats and blood sugar regulation:</h4>
<p>– Glucose – blood sugar</p>
<p>– Insulin escorts glucose out of blood and into cells</p>
<p>– Insulin resistance – insulin is unable to do its job properly and blood sugar remains too high</p>
<p>– Insulin resistance – is the hallmark of type II diabetes, also known as adult onset diabetes.</p>

<p>An excess of saturated fats, trans fats, and omega 6 fats, along with decreased amounts of omega 3 fats, make major contributions to insulin resistance.</p>
<p>Numerous studies have shown that diets that include more whole natural plant foods, instead of processed foods, can have a significant impact on insulin resistance and blood sugar levels.</p>

<p>Cholesterol comes from two places: animal foods and your body.</p>
<p>– Low fat and high fiber whole natural plant foods, such as raw vegan and living foods, cause the liver to produce less cholesterol to make bile that emulsifies fat in the foods.</p>
<p>• Fresh raw and living foods also contain an abundance of fiber to bind to any excess cholesterol, thus keeping cholesterol at an appropriate level.</p>
<h3>Enzymes</h3>
<p>Raw vegan and living foods are high in food-based enzymes.</p>
<p>• Enzymes are protein molecules that initiate biochemical reactions in all living things, plants and animals alike.</p>
<p>• Research indicates that plant enzymes are found within plant cells and are released when plant cell walls are broken down either by chewing, juicing, or blending.</p>
<p>• If plants are heated above 115°F the enzymes may denature or break down.</p>
<p>• Chewing raw plant foods well is important for releasing enzymes from plant cells.</p>
<p>• This gives the body a “head start” in digestion, creating less work and taking less energy, so you may feel lighter and more energetic than you would if you ate heated foods without active enzymes.</p>
<h3>Increasing raw and living foods in your diet helps to provide:</h3>
<p>• More energy</p>
<p>• Feeling lighter</p>
<p>• Greater overall well-being</p>
<p>• An abundance of nutrients</p>
<p>• Weight normalization over time</p>
<p>• Avoidance of hunger and deprivation</p>
<p>– It’s not just another diet, but a healthful, delicious, and - most importantly - sustainable way of changing your eating habits that you can happily maintain for a lifetime!</p>


<h5>By Tom Fisher RN, BA</h5>
<h3></h3>

					<item>
		<title><![CDATA[Stress Free?]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/stress-free/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <div>So the wife tells her husband: &nbsp;“I’m going with you tomorrow when you get your physical. &nbsp;In fact, I would like to speak to the doctor myself.”

<p>Her husband for the past six months had become a mental and physical wreck. &nbsp;He experienced chronic insomnia, fatigue, anxiety and panic attacks. &nbsp;No longer exercising, he mostly complained. &nbsp;Their sex life had become a distant memory. &nbsp;His food choices were standard American diet of carbohydrates, fast food, pizza and ice cream.</p>

<p>Like a lemming falling off the cliff, the prognostication was dismal.</p>

<p>After his examination, the wife met with his doctor she had known for 10 years and admired for his alternative and Integrative approaches for health prevention and focus on lifestyle choices.</p>

<p>“So,” the wife said as she sat on the couch across from the physician, “what is wrong with my husband?”</p>

<p>The doctor, reputed for his knowledge of holistic living, replied: &nbsp;“His condition is chronic stress. &nbsp;The bad news is he won’t last much longer doing the same things the same way expecting different results.</p>

<p>“The good news is everything is reversible with lifestyle change.”</p>

<p>The wife paused, considering what he had told her, then asked: &nbsp;“So what can I do to help?”</p>

<p>The doctor smiled knowingly. &nbsp;Now 72-years-young, he practiced what he preached. &nbsp;Youthful and vital, he practiced martial arts, walked rigorously daily, and body surfed.</p>

<p>“Here’s what you can do,” he said. &nbsp;“If you follow this very specific and demanding regimen, your husband should be good as new in six months to a year.”</p>

<p>“First, since he has difficultly sleeping, give him a massage at bedtime. &nbsp;This will produce ‘feely good’ endorphins that is essentially the body’s morphine. &nbsp;Soon he’ll be sleeping like a baby.</p>

<p>“Next,” the doctor coached, “since he is in chronic stress syndrome, relieve him of all household duties like book keeping and anything relating to finances.”</p>

<p>The wife blanched. &nbsp;“Anything else, like an anti-depressant medication?” she asked.</p>

<p>No, the doctor responded. &nbsp;“That would be counter-productive. &nbsp;We need to get him on his proper MEDS; that being the acronym for ‘meditation, exercise, diet and sleep.”</p>

<p>Aware the wife had practiced formal meditation and mindfulness for many years, he then urged that on awakening, she should first “cuddle and snuggle” to transition from sleep to alertness in a loving manner. Then include her husband in the daily meditation and tai chi/qigong practice.</p>

<p>Tai chi and qigong, he reiterated, is a 5,000 year old healthcare system to remove blocks, congestion, obstruction and pain from both the mental and physical body.</p>

<p>The wife knew he was preaching to the choir. &nbsp;She credited her daily practices with her longevity and excellent health. &nbsp;But she knew he was special and his advice priceless.</p>

<p>“Is there anything else,?” starting to feel overwhelmed with this largesse of responsibility, especially dealing with a stubborn and reluctant to change husband.</p>

<p>Still smiling, the doctor then stressed the importance of a vegan diet with enzyme supplementation. &nbsp;And a diet primarily sugar and dairy free. &nbsp;Then he leaned back in his recliner waiting for the wife’s response.</p>

<p>In summary, the wife said, “I need to be a co-enabler in optimal health. &nbsp;This means relieving him of all stressful responsibilities, catering constantly to restore his self-confidence, massage, exercise and entertain him for the next six months to a year and then he will be fully recovered.”</p>

<p>The doctor stood. &nbsp;“I have a patient waiting,” he said politely. &nbsp;“Good luck and be well!”</p>

<p>On the way driving home the husband finally asked the question lingering on his mind since his wife had gone into the doctor’s conference room for an hour.</p>

<p>“And,” he said, “what did the doctor say?”</p>

<p>“Honey,” the wife responded sadly shaking her head, “you don’t have much longer.”</p>

<p>________________________________________________________________________________________</p>

<p>This story is all too very familiar and recounted many times over day after day throughout the world. &nbsp;And that is why my one-week emphasis on stress reduction along with the Hippocrates protocols for vital and restorative living is being offered twice annually.</p>

<p>Everything the doctor in the above story discussed is part and parcel of this 20-hour intensive training in stress reduction and mindfulness.</p>

<p><a href="https://hippocratesinst.org/detoxdestress">See you in October at Hippocrates!</a></p>
<p>- Edwin Riley</p></div><p></p>

		<title><![CDATA[Mind Over Perpetual Patterns]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/mind-over-perpetual-patterns/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p><em>"In our multidimensional academic understanding of the mind, many of us have lost our way. Professionals and the public alike misunderstand the importance of this powerful gift. All too often we think about developing knowledge and increasing our capacity to use our brain in a linear way."</em></p>

<p>Unfortunately, the mind has very little to do with the brain itself. It has more to do with the omnipresent, invisible library of perpetual wisdom and consistent truth that surrounds all of us at all times.</p>

<p>Our job is not to tame the mind, but to liberate it and allow our heart to take the lead in choosing enriched thoughts. It is from this epi-center of enlightenment that we clearly find and define what knowledge is important.</p>

<p>We have come to believe the perpetual patterns of harvesting knowledge and categorically placing it on the shelves of our memory is appropriate. But in order to free ourselves to harvest true wisdom we must knock down those shelves and abolish crude data.</p>

<p>Calming the brain by focusing on instinct is the most effective route to accomplishing this essential feat. Some choose to do this via prayer, contemplation, meditation, exercise or even deep rest. Whichever route you favor, employ it so the calming influence is abundant and effective.</p>

<p>Once you free yourself from the grips of perpetual thinking and permit the higher level of instinct to become your platform for growth, it becomes&nbsp;easier to access the heart and find unchallengeable truth. Truth in its purest form makes every cell in your body tingle, and your overall sense becomes confident in its grace.</p>

<p>Your ultimate mission as a member of the species Homo sapiens is to reach back to the untainted time when you were an embryo—all capable, all wise and all-knowing—and become comfortable with that magnitude of responsibility.</p>

<p>Our concept of age creating sophistication has been shattered and needs to be re-thought. At the young vulnerable time, our unadulterated self was limitless with endless potential to be, do, or create anything we dreamed of. As years passed, we gathered increasing perpetual patterns of thoughts and clutter. It became more difficult for us to access the godliness within our souls.</p>

<p>The mind is much more than we have thought it to be in the past. When passionate in pursuing self-realization, you are actually rediscovering who you are from the beginning. When you’re prepared for it, it’s a magnificent encounter that empowers you with the strength to stand for honesty, purity and power.</p>

<p>Your self-doubt will dissolve into a universal strength that is the greatest gift God bestowed upon us. Doubt comes from the misuse of the brain and its pretense to be the mind. You are not who you think you are. You are much greater!</p>

<p>Our frailty and insignificant faith in self often comes from a life of tenuous commitment. The truth you gather and employ from the heart maintains a protective armor and impenetrable fortress so you can live passionately and contribute fully.</p>

<p>At Hippocrates Wellness, one of the most important areas where we help people grow is true mind development. Until you walk this route and change the signpost placed there by a disharmonious culture and society, it is impossible to flourish and heal permanently.</p>

<p>My message to you today is that everything you struggle with can easily be resolved. All the problems you perceive to be insurmountable can be conquered. Your true power is God’s gift of free-flowing and fluid thought.</p>
<blockquote>Once you free yourself from the grips of perpetual thinking and permit the higher level of instinct to become your platform for growth, it becomes easier to access the heart and find unchallengeable truth.</blockquote>
<p>Article by Brian Clement PhD LN</p>

					<item>
		<title><![CDATA[Take a walk. Live Longer]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/take-a-walk-live-longer/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <h2>Study after study proves the importance of international movement.</h2>
<p>Massive amounts of evidence now show that walking, a natural state, prolongs life by&nbsp;to seven years (European Society of Cardiology) and helps prevent arthritis, depression, diabetes, heart disease, strokes and cancer.</p>

<p>Thirty minutes of walking per day, five days per week, helps prevent heart attacks, strokes and diabetic conditions as reported by the American Heart Association. Furthermore Japanese studies reveal interval&nbsp;walking—three minutes fast, three minutes slow to moderate—further enhances benefits and helps alleviate the potential for many forms of cancer.</p>

<p>A high percentage of the half-million yearly cancer deaths in the United States alone are due to little exercise and poor diet (university of Pennsylvania). Exercise alone may help prevent cancer by regulating sex hormones, insulin, prostaglandins and immunity.</p>

<p>Ten hours of activity a week reduces the likelihood of breast cancer by 22 percent (breastcancer.org), endometrial cancer by 30 to 40 percent (NIAMSD), colorectal cancer by 40 percent (DESGUETZ) and lung cancer by 20 to 40 percent depending on geographical location (EMAUS).</p>

<p>The arthritis Foundation points out that movement feeds your joins and allows the cells within them to take up nutrients and hydrate, preventing erosion and join disorder.</p>

<p>Dr. John Ratey of Harvard Medical School explains how IQ and cognitive function dramatically improve depending on the amount of aerobic exercise performed.&nbsp;Scientific America reports that children require a minimum of 60 minutes of daily exercise to be at their best inherent cognitive abilities. Stamford University found that walking improves creativity and problem-solving ability.</p>

<p>Ironically, schools in the United States are reducing physical education and increasing stress by testing and evaluating more often. A U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics survey shows that in 1969, 48 percent of North America youths&nbsp;traveled to school either on foot or by bike. Currently, that figure is less than 16 percent. This downward trend will encourage lifelong lethargy and skyrocketing disease rates.</p>

<p>Walking is now revered equally to running; it may take longer to gain benefits, but the impact and injury that accompanies running make it questionable as a long-term health strategy.</p>

<p>I always encourage those who suffer melancholy or light-to-moderate depression to exercise aerobically.&nbsp;This is one act that diminishes and, in some cases, relieves their concerns. As nomad agrarians, we consistently moved. Sadly, modern Homo sapiens consistently sit and endure stress. We have a choice to either prolong life, diminish disease and be happy or sit around and complain about how tired we are. Please choose the affirmative!</p>

<p>My advice to people of any age is to purchase flat walking or running shoes with a slight heel elevation and thick, flexible soles.&nbsp;These sneakers cushion the foot and absorb shock. Wear 100 percent organic and brightly colored clothing so you are visible when walking outdoors.</p>

<p>Nature's abundant landscape welcomes us like a loving mother to utilize her strength in our quest to maintain and gain health. Walking, climbing, skating, skiing, boating and swimming make the act of movement a joy. Walk forward into life proudly, healthfully and happily!</p>



<p>Article by Anna Maria Clement, PhD, LN</p>

		<title><![CDATA[Sprouts The Living Super Food]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/sprouts-the-living-super-food/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p>The reason sprouts are a main focus of the Hippocrates program is because they contain a high level of nutrients and enzymes, which make them easy to assimilate by the body. This allows the body to direct newly discovered energy toward cleansing, regulating and building the immune system as well as creating healthy cells.</p>

<p>Through chromatography and Kirlian photography, modern science can demonstrate the immeasurable properties of life force energy (chi) existing within these sprouts. The increased enzymatic activity gives someone eating these living foods a greater sense of vitality and energy which far surpass even what is gained from eating solely raw foods.</p>

<p>On a personal note, my wife Pam and I have found that when we go to raw restaurants, which rarely serve sprouts, we do not feel as good as when we adorn our plates with the array of sprouts offered on the buffet at Hippocrates. This is why we say we enjoy a living foods diet as opposed to a raw foods diet. At Hippocrates, we take this process one step further by serving green juice made from sprouts and vegetables every day. We regard this as an important component of the Hippocrates lifestyle as well.</p>

<p>As far back as 5,000 years ago, ancient Chinese physicians were prescribing sprouts for curing disorders. They, like Hippocrates, realized the importance of nutrition in bringing vitality to the body.</p>

<p>Let’s explore the sprout and discover some of its many attributes. It all begins with the seed, which contains within it both nutrients and enzymes. The enzymes are considered the life-force of food and assist in both the digestion and absorption of nutrients. They are the catalyst for all activities which take place within the body. When the seed gets air, water, and temperature to its liking, it germinates. It begins to sprout and a flow of energy or life-force is released.</p>
<div><strong>As a sprout:</strong></div>
<p></p><ul><p></p>
<p> 	</p><li>The greatest enzyme activity is from germination up to 7 days and is 100 times greater than the enzyme content of fruits or vegetables which helps to replenish our own body’s reserve of enzymes.</li><p></p>
<p> 	</p><li>Its carbohydrates become easier to assimilate as the starches are changed to simple sugars.</li><p></p>
<p> 	</p><li>Its fats are changed to fatty acids which are an easily digested soluble compound.</li><p></p>
<p> 	</p><li>Its complex protein is converted into simple amino acids, which essentially means that it is "predigested".</li><p></p>
<p> 	</p><li>Vitamin production is increased three to twelve times more.</li><p></p>
<p> 	</p><li>Minerals are chelated, a natural state where they are chemically bonded to amino acids and easily assimilated by the body.</li><p></p>
<p> 	</p><li>It has delicate cell walls so it can release nourishment easily.</li><p></p>
<p> 	</p><li>It contains photochemical, which are plant compounds that protect against disease.</li><p></p>
<p> 	</p><li>It contains highly active antioxidants that prevent DNA destruction and the effects of aging.</li><p></p>
<p> 	</p><li>It contains both increased fiber (up to 300%) and water.</li><p></p>
<p></p></ul><p></p>
<p>So when you hear the statement "It’s not the food in your life, it’s the life in your food", you can think of the sprout. It is essentially a baby plant which is bursting forth with new life. The concentration of proteins, vitamins, minerals, enzymes, RNA &amp; DNA is greater than at any other point in that plant’s development.</p>

<p>There are a variety of sprouts to choose from, each offering different benefits and tastes. Here's a great line up with which to become familiar.</p>

<p><strong>Sunflower</strong> — 3,000 years old and named after its golden rayed flower, which are reminiscent of the sun, it is a rich source of protein (up to 30%), lecithin, and Vitamin D (rarely found in vegetables). It is high in trace minerals which make it beneficial for bones, muscle and tissue tone and healthy red blood corpuscles.</p>

<p><strong>Sweet Pea</strong> — It is rich in protease inhibitors that prevent certain viruses and chemicals that promote cancer, and it is useful in reducing LDL (bad cholesterol) in the blood.</p>

<p><strong>Buckwheat</strong> — It promotes proper circulation, digestion and elimination with its anti plaque properties and it helps neutralizes the effects of radiation. (Secondary sources of nutrition)</p>

<p><strong>Cover</strong> — It is known as a blood purifier, it is high in calcium content which relaxes the central nervous system. It contains plant estrogens which balance hormones and it also contains isoflavones, which are anti cancerous.</p>

<p><strong>Broccoli</strong> — It contains sulfophane which protects cells from becoming malignant. It occurs 10-100 times greater in sprouts than in broccoli as a vegetable. It also causes the body to release glutathiones, a natural body enzyme, which neutralize or detoxify carcinogens, before they damage the DNA.</p>

<p><strong>Radish </strong>—It is an expectorant which clears mucous from the respiratory tract, expels worms and benefits the intestinal flora.</p>

<p><strong>Mung, Lentil. &amp; Adzuki</strong> — They contain soluble fiber and help lower cholesterol by clearing out dangerous LDL cholesterol in the blood. They also help regulate insulin and thus blood sugar.</p>

<p><strong>Fenugreek</strong> — It is soothing to mucous membranes which also is cleansing and nourishing to the digestive system, reduces inflammation and contains chorine (a fat controller) which helps with weight loss.</p>

<p>Some other great secondary sources of nutrition include alfalfa, mustard, garlic, cabbage and onion. The germinating and sprouting process is also used with nuts, seeds and grains increasing their nutritional &nbsp;value up to eight times removing toxins and enzyme inhibitors allowing for easier digestion.</p>

<p>Combining all of the components listed above make this the most nutritious way of eating on the planet. It provides our body with all essential amino acids, essential fatty acids, vitamins and minerals.</p>

<p>Not only are sprouts a powerhouse of life force energy, they are economically and environmentally friendly as&nbsp;&nbsp; well. Sprouts can be grown anywhere in the world all year round. At a time when people are concerned about cost of living and food shortages, it is less than half of a dollar to grow a pound of fresh green organic sprouts. It requires only minutes of your time per day This also relieves a burden on the earth, which some modern agricultural practices as well as animal and fish farming have created.</p>

<p>The resources that provided a great deal of information for this article are "Sprouts The Miracle Food" by Steve Meyerowitz (<a href="http://www.sproutman/">www.sproutman</a>), the International Sprout Growers Association (<a href="http://www.isga-sprouts.org/">www.isga-sprouts.org</a>), and Sprout People (<a href="http://www.sproutpeaople.com/">www.sproutpeaople.com</a>).</p>

<p>Ken Blue is a graduate of the Hippocrates Health Educator Program and&nbsp;is the Executive Chef at Hippocrates. Previously Ken owned and operated his own vegetarian restaurant in Baltimore, Maryland which earned "The Best Restaurant for Vegetarians” award. In addition to his food preparation and kitchen management responsibilities, Ken finds time to teach tai chi and qigong classes at the institute.</p>

		<title><![CDATA[Interview with Conscious Muscle]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/interview-with-conscious-muscle/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <h3>What’s on the mind of Instagram’s most famous vegan bodybuilder?</h3>
<p>| INTERVIEW BY THERESA CAMPBELL |</p>

<p>Jordan Drane is the man behind Conscious Muscle. He has been a personal trainer in West Palm Beach for over 10 years, yet he says the day his life and health really turned around was four years ago, when he adopted the vegan lifestyle. “My regret is not going vegan a lot sooner,” he says.</p>

<p>He’s pleased to have helped transform the lives of hundreds of people so far. “The thrill for me is when a&nbsp;non-vegan wants to give it a try.” He says. “Not only do they transition to a vegan diet, but they start getting in amazing shape. It shows that it’s possible.”</p>

<p>Jordan’s social media and online program are incredibly popular. In fact, @Conscious_Muscle is listed as the No. 1 vegan body builder on Instagram. “I’ve built quite an audience through showing people that their gains don’t have to be an animal’s loss,” he says.</p>

<p><em><strong>When did you ﬁrst decide to adopt the vegan lifestyle?</strong> </em></p>

<p>An amazing lady by the name of Susan convinced me. She and her husband Jon were personal training clients of mine, and after she went to vegan she tried her best to convince us to do the same. I did my research and found out the cruelty that eating meat entails and the detrimental effects on us and our planet. It really hit me after watching “Forks over Knives” and “Earthlings.” Going vegan made sense from a health standpoint.</p>

<p><em><strong>Did you notice any changes after cutting out meat?</strong></em></p>

<p>I had more energy and recovered from workouts more quickly. I had mental clarity, and my bloodwork phenomenally improved. My doctor was amazed and surprised. I applied all my knowledge to promoting a plant-based lifestyle and never looked back.</p>

<p><em><strong>What’s your message to meat eaters? </strong></em></p>

<p>I wish they knew the cruelty and suffering that factory farming and modern agriculture entails. A plant-based diet is the best thing for your health and your family—you have no idea what you’re putting into your children’s bodies. You can get protein, vitamins, minerals and everything else you need from a plant-based diet, without all of the carcinogens, cholesterol and cruelty associated with meat.</p>

<p><em><strong>What about vegetarians? What is your message? </strong></em></p>

<p>There are alternatives to dairy. There are nut milks and plant-based cheese alternatives that are delicious and healthy with-out the acidic and carcinogenic nature of dairy. The dairy industry is cruel. Animals are kept alive and in extreme suffering, being deprived of the right to even move, shackled and standing in their own filth. Plus, with dairy, females are forcefully impregnated so they continue to produce milk. People have a misconception that cows are constantly in a state of milk production, but that couldn’t be further from the truth. Shortly after birth, their calves are sent to veal farms to be slaughtered for meat. I would just ask that you take this into consideration.</p>

<p><em><strong>What does it take for your program to work for others?</strong></em></p>

<p>It just takes a willingness to change. You have to be ready for progress and you have to be ready to do your part. I give you a foundation to follow with both your nutrition and training for the most optimal results. Simply put, it only works if you work it.</p>

<p><em><strong>What do you love most about your job?</strong></em></p>

<p>Taking somebody from an animal-based diet to not only becoming vegan, but showing them amazing results. It’s a no-brainer, and it makes the transition really easy.</p>

<p><em><strong>What’s one thing that surprises your clients? </strong></em></p>

<p>The amount they can eat while still losing body fat. I’m a proponent of “sustainable eating,” which is ensuring you are fueled for lean muscle mass while still shedding body fat.</p>

<p><em><strong><img src="https://hippocratesinst.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/Leroy_n-e1536866569233.jpg" alt="" class="mb-15 mb-lg-20"></strong></em></p><em><strong>
</strong></em><p><em><strong>What is your personal philosophy for success? </strong></em></p>

<p>The best definition of success I have ever heard is from Earl Nightingale: “success is the progressive realization of a worthwhile goal or ideal.” Simply meaning if you are living in line with what matters most to you and taking steps towards that daily you are indeed a successful person.</p>

<p>I feel that I’m as successful as I am because of my passion for what I’m doing. It’s literally my life’s work, promoting a plant-based lifestyle, having an animal sanctuary, and contributing to the animal rights movement. I couldn’t ask for more. So if there’s anything I attribute to my success, it’s finding veganism.</p>

<p><em><strong>What do you do for fun? </strong></em></p>

<p>I spend time with my daughters, or outdoors at the sanctuary with all the critters. I lift weights and I take any opportunity to laugh and get into shenanigans with friends.</p>

<p><em><strong>Which celebrity would you most love to train? </strong></em></p>

<p>Leonardo DiCaprio. He speaks out on the sustainability of our planet and investing in plant-based meat substitutes. If he were to go vegan, it would be amazing. I would do my best to convince him.</p>

<p><em><strong>Where do you see yourself in ﬁve years?</strong> </em></p>

<p>I see myself traveling the world talking about veganism while doing big things in the animal-rights arena.</p>

<p><em><strong>If you could have dinner with anyone, who would it be?</strong></em></p>

<p>It would be my stepfather Terrell. He came into my life when I was young, and I credit him for sending me on a positive path in life. I would love to catch up with him and let him know where my life has gone and what I’m about. I think he’d be proud.</p>



<p>To support Jordan's animal rescue Lily and Friends <a href="https://consciousmuscle.net/shop/donation/1-00-conscious-muscle-animal-sanctuary/">click here to learn more and donate.</a></p>

		<title><![CDATA[Heart Failure, ITP Thombocytopenia]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/heart-failure-itp-thombocytopenia/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p>My journey to enlightenment started several years ago, at a time when my health was not so marvelous. I was sick for many years, and was facing the threat of death. I went to the emergency room— almost too late.</p>

<p>I had lost all but three units of blood and had an extremely weak pulse. I was diagnosed with congestive heart failure, anemia and an autoimmune complication called ITP thrombocytopenia. My platelet count would suddenly drop to dangerously low levels.</p>

<p>In my early 20s, I was diagnosed with ITP. Later came congestive heart failure, which caused more swelling and edema. Because of my illness, I lost my job and all the benefits of having an income and my own life. I felt as if my soul had been taken from me. I was bedridden because I lacked the strength to walk or stand. I crawled from the bed to the toilet, stubbornly waited until my condition was critical before going to the emergency room. It was the most frightening time of my life. Despite everything, I still had a strong will to live.</p>

<p>Medical doctors tried everything to help me, but I knew in my heart that medicine was a temporary bandage. I often&nbsp;wondered, “Why this was happening to me?” Despite the high doses of medications and steroids, which had terrible side effects, we still had no root cause. Without further surgeries and continuing medications, I was likely to die in three years. I had to find answers. I realized I had to take steps to understand my illness. My&nbsp;own research led me to Hippocrates Wellness, and my time there transformed my state of being and led me to my true life’s calling.</p>

<p>The transformation started with the plant-based lifestyle, which opened new doors of truth about my ability to heal my own mind, body and spirit. I became fascinated with the theory of energetic modalities and how they provide a sense of awareness about the truth behind the eye. I explored detoxification theories to learn the anatomy of the self-healing body.</p>
<blockquote>After all my turmoil and adversity, my life had new direction.</blockquote>
<img src="https://hippocratesinst.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/Screen-Shot-2018-09-13-at-2.23.31-PM.png" alt="" class="mb-15 mb-lg-20">
<p>Waking up at Hippocrates is like waking up in paradise. It reminds me I’m here to heal and listen to my intuitive body. On my journey to health and wellness, I learned how to be attentive to my own intuition. Now I am vibrant and healthy, and I want to share this amazing experience with everyone.</p>

<p>I am now a raw food coach, licensed massage therapist, licensed spiritual healer coach, and restorative health instructor. Many people believe my illness was a tragedy. I believe it was a blessing in disguise.</p>

<p>My ailment enlightened my world and gave me the motivation to follow&nbsp;my own heart. It provided me with a new sense of direction and allowed me to inspire others to become vibrantly healthy like I did. On your own journey to wellness, the one gift I wish you will receive is empowerment. My story is one of many, but your story will create a true reality for you and the world around you.</p>



<p>Amanda Johnson | Healed and Transformed since 2014</p>

		<title><![CDATA[The “Chocolate Fruit”  Black Sapote]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/the-chocolate-fruit-black-sapote/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p>Here at&nbsp;Hippocrates we are blessed to have well over one hundred fruiting trees of more than thirty different varieties spread out all over our fifty acre campus. These trees combined with our many thousands of ornamental trees, bushes, plants, vegetable gardens, and herb gardens make for a beautiful tropical oasis intended to create a beautiful, peaceful, serene, and healing environment. I harvest our food bearing trees in season throughout the year and take the fruit to the kitchen for the benefit of our guests.</p>

<p>One of our trees is the black sapote otherwise known as the “Chocolate Fruit” because it tastes like chocolate! The black sapote tree (Diospyros nigra) a species of persimmon, is a rare tropical exotic native to the Caribbean and tropical areas of Central America. The black sapote fruit contains a fair amount of vitamin A, Vitamin C, a relatively high amount of potassium as well as other vitamins and minerals. The tree requires warmer climates and will not tolerate heavy frost.</p>

<p>The tree can be propagated from the seed which may take up to 30 days to germinate. It likes lots of water so you may want to plan on regular irrigation during the dry season. While the black sapote tree grows slowly, about one foot a year, it may begin to bear fruit in just four years. It will eventually reach a height of up to 25 feet tall. Its fruit starts out hard with a bright green color it will grow to the size of a softball. The unripen fruit and the skin are inedible. As it ripens it turns to a deep yellow green olive color and softens like an avocado while the inside turns dark brown and sweetens with the consistency of papaya.</p>

<p>I have had several requests from guests who joined us for our spectacular raw New Year’s Eve gala party for our delicious Black Sapote Chocolate Pudding recipe. So, here it is. Enjoy!</p>
<h3><strong>Chocolate Pudding Recipe</strong></h3>
<p>4 cups avocado</p>

<p>1 cup black Sapolte</p>

<p>6 pitted dates</p>

<p>2 tablespoons carob powder</p>

<p>¼ teaspoon cinnamon powder</p>

<p>1 Tablespoon vanilla flavor (alcohol free)</p>

<p>8 drops liquid Stevia</p>

<p><em><strong>Place all ingredients into a food processor fitted with the “S” blade and blend thoroughly.</strong></em></p>



<img src="/wp-content/uploads/2016/01/sapolte-300x224.jpg" alt="" class="mb-15 mb-lg-20">









<p style="text-align: left;">by Brian Hetrich</p>

		<title><![CDATA[Cancer Conquest]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/cancer-conquest/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <h4><em>For many cancer victims, the treatment is just as dangerous as the disease. Is there a better way?</em></h4>
<p>For more than 60 years, we have been teaching worldwide about the connection between&nbsp;excess protein and sugar and the proliferation of cancer. Of course, it’s also our chemical- and heavy metal-saturated world that caused this disease to supersede heart maladies as the No. 1 killer.</p>

<p>Recent findings from MIT verify our concerns, and the international science landscape has revealed the war has been lost. As we know, RNA is the building block for DNA. Musashi proteins bond the RNA, preventing proper foundation for the DNA. The work done in Boston on tumor biology highlights that excess protein, certainly from animal-based&nbsp;foods, in coordination with all forms of sugar, including fructose, establishes the epicenter for mutation to occur.</p>

<p>Lead author of the study, Yardin Katz, stated, “RNA is processed at several places within the cell and this gives opportunities for RNA-binding proteins to regulate RNA at each point. We’re very interested in trying to understand this class of proteins and how they regulate cell-state transitions” (tumors).</p>

<p>Across six decades of clinical observations, we’ve noticed that the removal of complex proteins and the absence of all forms of sugar work as a spring-board, allowing the body’s immunity to fully engage in its attack on cancer cells.</p>

<p>Unfortunately, current&nbsp;mainstream protocols weaken and destroy the immune system cells, leaving the patient in a weakened state, literally&nbsp;fighting both the disease and the treatment. Recent studies reported in Natural Health 365 highlight that only 2.1 percent of people survive after having chemotherapy administered as their main treatment after five years.</p>

<p>Britain’s Public Health England and Cancer Research UK reported that chemotherapy drugs kill half of the patients that take them within the first 30 days. There seems to be mounting evidence of the sources’ impetus and treatments of cancer failing us. There needs to be a fresh set of eyes objectively placed on the&nbsp;treatments, so the scientific community can rethink the current state of affairs. Guy Faguet, MD reported in an Australian journal that in his home country, the survival rate after chemo is only 2.3 percent after five years. When one analyzes patients who either opted out or were advised by their physicians not to undergo this form of nuclear medicine, there were better outcomes and less mortality.</p>

<p>A study on the chemeurope website described the genesis of all cancers in connection with epigenetics. Lifestyle is central in the prevention and reversal of this disease. Professor Graeme Morgan, radiation oncologist; Robyn Ward, medical oncologist; and Dr. Michael&nbsp;Barton, radiation oncologist, collaborated at the Royal North Shore hospital in Sydney, resulting in a meta-study analysis that provoked their statement that chemotherapy was, in fact, statistically shown to be ineffective in the overwhelming majority of cases.</p>

<p>Today, it is widely accepted that a positive attitude, a clean, plant-based diet and consistent productive movement and exercise work together to prevent and even reverse mutagenic disease. Although one cannot state that there is never a time or place to intervene with nuclear medicine, global research is slowly disassembling the ironclad control of these procedures. Educated patients are challenging the status quo&nbsp;and demanding honest and transparent evaluations of any and all suggested treatments.</p>

<p>In the four decades I have worked in the field of natural health care, I’ve observed a healthy lifestyle as central to the prevention and recovery of a wide variety of maladies. Epigenetically, we can turn on and off the cancer switch.</p>

<p>I challenge all healthcare professionals to embrace a wide and comprehensive approach in the pursuit of helping people in their time of need. There is no doubt that the future of medicine includes lifestyle as the fundamental premise of a healthy protocol. Continue to be educated and learn as much as you can before you make any and all decisions.</p>



<p><strong>Article by Brian Clement, PhD, LN</strong></p>

            <h4><em>The old adage "beauty comes from within" is the key to Elle Macpherson's continued success.</em></h4>
<p><strong>Interview by Anna Maria Clement, PhD, LN</strong></p>

<p>One of Australia’s most iconic exports, supermodel Elle Macpherson, has enjoyed a highly successful career spanning three decades in front of the camera. She has graced the silver screen, international runways, and magazine covers, including Sports Illustrated a record ﬁ ve times. But today, Elle’s roles as a proud mother of two, entrepre-neur, and businesswoman overseeing two successful international companies make her most proud. Elle sat down with me recently and discussed health, beauty, business and motherhood.</p>
<blockquote>What is the most important part of well-being?</blockquote>
<p>Good life balance, for me, is key to my well-being. I know if I take good care of myself, everything else in life will fall into place. That means eating a plant-based, wholefood diet, taking super greens every morning, meditation, exercise and good quality sleep. Throw in a good dose of love and laughter, and I feel my very best. I am a mother fi rst and businesswoman second. Life can get chaotic trying to balance both, but I know if I take a balanced approach and do all of these things, I have the energy to fulfi ll both roles to the very best of my ability. It is my aim every day.</p>
<blockquote>What is the key ingredient for a happy, beautiful life?</blockquote>
<p>I think if you are healthy, you instantly feel happier. Good health comes from nourishing your body from the inside out, which is the ethos behind WelleCo. From the very beginning, my business partner Andrea and I believed the future of beauty lay in ingestible beauty. Our premium whole food nutrient powders are designed to be absorbed easily at a cellular level, so they nourish all&nbsp;systems of the body. We believe when our gut health is good, and our body is healthy and al-kaline, it shows on the outside. Our loyal customers tell us the same. They are our very best advocates. Taking time for wellness—physical, emotional and spiritual—is very important to me. That’s why I love coming to Hippocrates. It’s a complete wellness institute. We follow similar philosophies, and I love the fresh, raw vegan food. I find I’m inspired and learn a lot from the fabulous team at HHI.</p>
<blockquote>How do you want to be seen on the global stage?</blockquote>
<p>I am aiming to be a woman who is doing her best as a mother, a friend, a sister and a business-woman, and who promotes and supports wellness which, to me, is the greatest of luxuries. I believe no matter who you are, how old you are or what job you do, a healthy body, active mind, good spirit, and a connection to nature or God or the universe is vital in life.</p>
<blockquote>What’s your deepest secret for health?</blockquote>
<p>For me, it is nourishing and taking care of myself from the inside out. When I was turning&nbsp;50, I started to feel fatigued and unwell. My nutritionist, Dr. Sim-one Laubscher, taught me about alkaline versus acidic foods and how our bodies were designed to absorb nutrition via natural foods, not synthetic pills.</p>

<p>She formulated an alkaline green powder that turned my life around. I noticed my skin wasn’t dry anymore, looked plumper, and had what nutritionists call “the alkaline glow.” My sugar cravings subsided as my blood sugar levels became more balanced. My digestion improved, and I felt more up-beat and emotionally balanced. I found myself choosing healthier options as my body became more in tune. Most importantly, I learned how to listen to what my body needs every day to function at its best.</p>

<p>The benefits were so life-changing, I wanted to share this formulation with every-body. So it went on to become WelleCo’s core product, the Super Elixir, super greens. For me, taking two teaspoons in filtered water every day, along with a raw, organic, whole-food, plant-based diet and our Nourishing Protein, helps keep me in optimum health, which shows on the outside. Health and beauty go hand-in-hand. It works for me!</p>



<p>Learn more about Elle and her wellness at welleco.com</p>

		<title><![CDATA[A State of Mind | Psychotherapy Q&A]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/a-state-of-mind-psychotherapy-q-a/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <h3>Q&amp;A with&nbsp;the beloved Psychotherapists Antony Chatham and Andy Roman of Hippocrates Wellness.</h3>
<blockquote><em><strong>Question:</strong> I miss the good old days when I ate what I wanted. I have fond memories of holiday foods and candies from my youth. Sometimes I try to recapture that feeling and “fall off&nbsp; the wagon” to indulge. What can I do about that?</em></blockquote>
<p><strong>Answer:</strong>&nbsp;You’re talking about a very emotional relationship with food,&nbsp;and you don’t have a patent on that. I think it’s a matter of which part of you is in charge: the adult or the kid. Kids don’t see the big picture and get swept away in the magic of the moment.&nbsp;Trick-or-treating was so much fun—sorting and eating brightly-wrapped candy and swapping goodies with my friends! No worries, just pleasure. But later came tooth decay, stomach aches, diabetes and weakened immune function.</p>

<p>Now, look at the adult who sees the lurking danger, the power of the seduction, the lie beneath the fantasy. Enter the adult who recognizes that today’s pleasure can lead to tomorrow's pain.&nbsp;That adult who always says “No!” That downer, no-fun parent who denies us pleasure for our own good. That “adult” who stimulates inner rebellion with rigid rules. Not much better, is it? My conclusion is this: when either a lost child or a rigid adult is in charge, damage or self-sabotage inevitably follows.</p>

<p>I recommend pathway #3: the benevolent adult who creatively replaces antiquated, unhealthy habits with new, fun ways to do the old holiday rituals. Enter the artistic adult who makes new healthy foods to associate with the holidays. Keep the magic going—just be smart about it. You can have your nostalgic indulgences, as long as you let the right adult be in charge.&nbsp;Make it work for both sides of you, not for one at the other’s expense.</p>


<blockquote><em><strong>Question:&nbsp;</strong>I’ve been coming to the Institute for years, but I still feel skeptical about certain parts of the program at times. Is this the Doubting Thomas in me? Does it mean there’s a chance I’ll never commit 100 percent?</em></blockquote>
<p><strong>Answer:&nbsp;</strong>&nbsp;It means you haven't yet answered all your questions.&nbsp;Because the Hippocrates program is so textured and complex, you probably won’t reach the end of your learning curve any time soon. Obviously you’ve got the gist of it, though. You likely return for several reasons, and these are my guesses as to why: One, you’re getting the results you want. Two, you love the atmosphere.&nbsp;Three, you appreciate the people, both guests and staff . Four, you feel inspired by the individual progress and spirit that you see. Jesus’s response to Doubting Thomas was, “come and touch my hands.” That means to me that it isn’t about punishing the doubters, but reassuring them. Explore more. Ask questions. Get to the root of things.</p>

<p>Real faith and commitment come from experience, from reaching a point of critical mass in your knowing. Keep educating yourself. The good news is that you can measure your progress on the path to health both subjectively and objectively. Critical mass is at hand!</p>


<blockquote><em><strong>Question:</strong> You suggest spending therapy time not talking about differences, but rather discussing expectations of an improved relationship. Is it not important that we share why there are problems between us?</em></blockquote>
<p><strong>Answer:</strong> Yes, it is important to know what the major problems in your relationship are. In a solution- focused therapeutic approach, we can know the major issues affecting the relationship when you propose your ideal solutions to the problems. Each of your perspectives will be clear when you suggest your ideal solutions.</p>

<p>There is a general principle that what your mind focuses on will begin to capture your energy. If you spend time on your disagreements and differences, they become the focus. In addition, many couples tend to prove why their point of view is right and the other person’s view is wrong. This process takes a major part of the therapy time. On the other hand, if we commonly think about solutions, our focus will be on resolving the differences, at least to a great extent.</p>

<p>As a rule, in the solution-focused approach, I ask the couple to give six different suggestions each for an improved relationship and then begin to agree on common priorities. Couples also give six different compliments to each other in such a session.</p>

<p>Using these suggestions and compliments, couples are helped to visualize their ideal relationship and life in a Guided Imagery/Creative Visualization Session and record them (along with each one’s compliments to each other) on a cellphone or other devices and reinforce their commitment to the improved relationships by playing back the recording in their bedroom.</p>

<p>This may not be practical in every case; however, according to the feedback received, many of our couples have benefited from this approach.</p>
