		<title><![CDATA[Clean the Air with Indoor Plants]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/blog/clean-the-air-with-indoor-plants/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <h2>How Plants Clear the Air</h2>
<p>Are plants the best way to purify the air in your home? Indoor air can be up to can be up to 1,000 times dirtier than outdoor air. The EPA estimates that most Americans are exposed every day to indoor air contaminants than can lead to serious health problems including cancer, respiratory ailments, fatigue and headaches. The air you are breathing in your home is likely contaminated with pollutants and toxic chemicals such as:</p>
<blockquote>• Dust and dirt</blockquote>
<blockquote>
<p>• Dander (from pets and humans)</p>
<p>• Paint fumes</p>
<p>• Outgassing from synthetic carpet, curtains, fire retardants, glues, cleaning solutions, pressure treated wood, perfume, personal care products, and even your synthetic clothes</p>
<p>• Cooking and tobacco smoke</p>
<p>• Carbon monoxide</p>
<p>• Mold</p>
<p>• Bacteria</p>
<p>• Viruses</p>
<p>• Pollen</p>
<p>• A whole host of harmful Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC’s) such as formaldehyde, benzene, ammonia, xylene, and potentially thousands more.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>While a standard fiber weave furnace filter will remove most suspended pollutants larger than 50 microns a High Efficiency Particulate Air (HEPA) filter will remove most suspended pollutants down to 0.3 microns. However, neither type of filter is effective at removing dissolved pollutants such as Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC’s.) Even a carbon filter is only effective in removing VOC’s if the fan runs continuously and you change the filters regularly. This uses up electricity and the used air filters contribute to toxic waste accumulation in landfills. Changing the filters exposes you to a substantial concentration of toxins during the replacement process.</p>
<p>House plants are not only an attractive addition to any home but they also moonlight as efficient air purifiers. All you need to add is water! Plants convert carbon dioxide into oxygen through the process of photosynthesis. Root-associated microbes convert toxins in the air into nutrients the plants eat and thrive on. House plants become more effective over time while HEPA air cleaners become less effective over time. House plants are also less expensive and naturally more attractive than any HEPA filter unit.</p>
<p>While all plants are beneficial for improving the quality of the air, some are clearly better than others. Some plants are capable of removing up to 90% of VOC chemicals dissolved in the air in just twenty-four hours! Here are my favorite six house plants for clearing the air:</p>
<p><strong>Wheatgrass</strong></p>
<p>• The best air purifying plant</p>
<p>• Enhances the oxygen in the air</p>
<p>• Generates healthful negative ions</p>
<p>• Wheatgrass juice is nature’s finest medicine and is more than twenty times denser in nutrients than other choice vegetables.</p>
<p><strong>Boston Fern</strong></p>
<p>• The second best air purifying plant</p>
<p>• Removes formaldehyde</p>
<p>• Prefers plenty of light</p>
<p>• Keep the soil moist and mist the leaves often</p>
<p><strong>Aloe Vera</strong></p>
<p>• Removes formaldehyde</p>
<p>• Good for cuts and burns on the skin</p>
<p>• Needs well drained soil</p>
<p>• Prefers plenty of light</p>
<p>• Water only once a week</p>
<p><strong>Dwarf/Pygmy Date Palm</strong></p>
<p>• Removes xylene</p>
<p>• Removes ammonia</p>
<p>• Prefers plenty of light</p>
<p>• Keep well watered</p>
<p><strong>English Ivy</strong></p>
<p>• Removes benzene</p>
<p>• Cleans air of cigarette smoke</p>
<p>• Removes formaldehyde</p>
<p>• Great for those suffering from asthma and allergies</p>
<p><strong>Golden Pothos</strong></p>
<p>• Removes carbon monoxide</p>
<p>• Removes formaldehyde</p>
<p>• Prefers plenty of light</p>
<p>• Water less in colder temperatures</p>
<p>In general, you will need one plant (10-12 inch pot) for a small room and two or three plants for a large room to effectively clear the air. Fertilize once every two weeks with a side dressing of compost or compost tea. Dust the leaves once a month with a damp cloth. Use pots with holes in the bottom with a drain saucer. Place a bunch of pebbles in the bottom of the pot and add well-draining potting soil on top. Be sure not to overwater, as too much soil moisture can lead to mold growth. Empty the drain saucer if it accumulates water.</p>
<p>Play classical music to your plants and speak to them with loving intentions. Enjoy the simple beauty of house plants while your lungs benefit from their natural air cleansing action.</p>
<h3>By Brian Hetrich</h3>

					<item>
		<title><![CDATA[Your Healthiest Shopping List]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/diet/your-healthiest-shopping-list/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p>Ever feel as though you're in a rut at the grocery store or farmers market? Are you wanting to integrate healthier foods into your life to contribute to a&nbsp;more optimal level of wellness? Well, we are here to get you started.</p>
<h2>HERBS AND WEEDS</h2>
<p><em>The earthy, wild flavors of herbs</em><em>&nbsp;and strong, green weeds</em><em>&nbsp;tell us two things: that they are good to eat and – for the modern person – that they are full of healthful substances. We have evolved over thousands of years to prefer foods that provide a healthful effect, and these wild foods were some of the first consumed by humans. .&nbsp;&nbsp; </em></p>
<h3>Dandelion</h3>
<p>Dandelion is a wild food&nbsp;that can occasionally be found at green markets but seldom at the grocery store. But why buy dandelion greens&nbsp;if they are available wild? As you may know, the average neighborhood is filled with edible wild plants; I’ve chosen to highlight dandelions for their availability and popularity. If you are a fan of mildly bitter greens, this plant cannot be beat.</p>
<p>If you have ever seen a dandelion pushing through a crack in the sidewalk, you know what a hardy weed it is. It passes its strength on to those who eat it. Of the numerous phytochemicals&nbsp;that it contains, the most conspicuous are taraxacin and taraxol, both substances that provide dandelion leaves with their bitter flavor. They are also potent agents for cleansing the liver&nbsp;and gallbladder<strong>. - [</strong>Gallová<strong>]</strong></p>
<p>Lethargy can result when a body is filled with toxins, so one of the best ways to maintain a high energy&nbsp;level is by consuming foods that aid the body’s natural cleansing organs.</p>
<p>There are many ways to enjoy the healthful benefits of dandelion, and the average health food&nbsp;store will stock several varieties of dandelion extract, either in the form of tea, concentrate or pill. Many of these may be fine, but I would highly recommend the fresh greens themselves. They are ideal for salad and juicing, though most would find the undiluted juice rather bitter, so try mixing it with other vegetables.</p>
<h3>Dill</h3>
<p>Dill is one of the greatest herbs&nbsp;for those on a raw-food&nbsp;diet. It can be used in small quantities or as a main vegetable, and its flavor is strong but never overpowering.</p>
<p>Aside from the expected health benefits of a green herb, dill&nbsp;has some interesting qualities. Its main flavor component, dillapiol, is currently being researched for its possible effect in treating malaria. It seems to exhibit synergistic activity with gedunin and 7-methoxygedunin, both of which are used to treat the disease. Dillapiol increased their effectiveness by around 15%. - [Omar].</p>
<p>It is an amazing booster of the immune system&nbsp;with phenomenal health effects. Its cousin, fennel<strong>,</strong> is also a delicious green with similar healing properties.</p>
<h3>Epazote</h3>
<p>Although little known outside of Mexico, this pungent&nbsp;weed is quickly becoming more widely available. The herb&nbsp;is valued for its flavor, but like many strong spices, humans may have originally acquired a taste for it based on its anti-parasitic&nbsp;effect. It contains ascaridole, an organic&nbsp;peroxide&nbsp;effective in the treatment of amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, malaria, cholera, hysteria, catarrh, and asthma.</p>
<p>In the small quantities used to flavor food, the herb&nbsp;acts as a cleanser and can help prevent infection by funguses, parasites&nbsp;and other harmful pathogens. These foreign organisms drain our energy&nbsp;and sow the seeds of disease, so it is best to remain free of them.</p>
<p>As an added bonus, epazote&nbsp;is well known in Latin-American countries for its anti-flatulent&nbsp;properties. When consumed with pulses&nbsp;it achieves this effect.</p>
<h3>Oregano</h3>
<p>Oregano is known best in its dried, shakable form, but it is widely available fresh and easy to grow. An important addition to the cuisine of many cultures, oregano&nbsp;can be found growing from Italy to Mexico.</p>
<p>In recent years, a great deal of research has been done on the phytochemical&nbsp;content of oregano, owing to its reported benefits in the treatment of pathogenic diseases. One stood out, and it has since been isolated and is widely available. This is carvacrol, a thick lipid&nbsp;that has proven anti-microbial&nbsp;properties even outside of the body. Research has shown, in fact, that its amazing oxidizing&nbsp;abilities can disinfect&nbsp;a stainless steel surface. - [Knowles]</p>
<p>Yet, it is entirely safe for human consumption! Funguses, parasites&nbsp;and yeast&nbsp;can decrease one’s vitality&nbsp;and contribute to larger health problems, and it is well known that many cancers originate with foreign pathogens. Oregano is great for cleaning the body of these invaders, and it should be used liberally, especially in warmer climates where one is more likely to encounter parasitic invaders.</p>
<h3>Parsley</h3>
<p>Parsley may be the strongest weed available at the average grocery store. Unlike most common vegetables, which have been hybrid&nbsp;to soften their flavor, parsley&nbsp;is unapologetic about its strength. Perhaps for this reason, it too often finds its way back to the kitchen when the meal is done.</p>
<p>Parsley is a Western garnish, not a main course, and it is most often eaten in small quantities as a breath freshener&nbsp;following garlicky dishes. But there is no reason why this potent herb&nbsp;shouldn’t be treated with more respect.</p>
<p>The breath-freshening attributes of Parsley are due to the plant’s incredibly high chlorophyll&nbsp;content, and chlorophyll is a powerful carrier of nutrients. Like dill, parsley&nbsp;also contains dillapiol&nbsp;and a smorgasbord of other phytonutrients&nbsp;including bitter glycosides, carotenoids&nbsp;(including lutein&nbsp;and violaxanthin, both important for the eyes), and terpenoids. Choline, a nutrient&nbsp;necessary for proper cardiovascular and brain&nbsp;function, is also present in significant quantities.</p>
<h3>Perilla</h3>
<p>Also known as <em>Shiso </em>or “beefsteak plant,” perilla&nbsp;is a powerful and delicious herb&nbsp;that is quickly becoming popular in the United States and Europe. It can often be found in Korean grocery stores as “sesame leaf,” though the plant is unrelated to sesame.</p>
<p>Though I have no experience with it myself, perilla&nbsp;is reportedly easy to grow and will even thrive indoors. It can be eaten raw,&nbsp;in salads, prepared with vegetables, or pickled. It is a popular addition to <em>kimchi</em>, or Korean “sourkraut.” If you have the opportunity to grow this herb, do so, because it is one of nature’s most marvelous plants.</p>
<p>Aside from the plant’s extremely healthful oil, which has been implicated in cancer&nbsp;prevention, the leaves contain a number of powerful agents, including apigenin, ascorbic acid, beta carotene, caffeic acid, citral, dillapiol, elemicin, limonene, luteolin, myristicin, perillaldehyde, protocatechuic-acid, quercetin, and rosmarinic acid.</p>
<p>All of these agents have potential or proven health effects, but perhaps the most promising is one that perilla has a great deal of - luteolin. Luteolin is a flavanoid&nbsp;that not only protects cells&nbsp;from free radicals; its ability to shrink cancerous tumors has also been demonstrated. - [Selvendiran].</p>
<h3>Rosemary</h3>
<p>Research conducted in Taiwan has recently demonstrated the phenomenal effect of rosemary&nbsp;in the prevention&nbsp;and treatment of cancer. - [Ai-Hsiang<strong>]</strong></p>
<p>One of its active ingredients is carnosol, a phytopolyphenol&nbsp;that scavenges free radicals&nbsp;and protects DNA. Another study, conducted in China, demonstrates the effect of two other, similar triperpene acids, ursolic acid and oleanolic acid, on colon cancer. Together, they not only prevent but also wipe out pre-existing tumors. - [Jie Li]</p>
<p>Though I am tempted to sing rosemary’s praises as a marvelous culinary gift, I will limit myself to the topic at hand. Let it be said, however, that learning to skillfully use flavorful herbs&nbsp;such as rosemary will enhance one’s life both aesthetically and physically. Rosemary, being one of the most delicious and useful herbs, should be used without reserve.</p>
<h2>PULSES</h2>
<p>Peas and beans should be a vital&nbsp;part of every person’s diet. In terms of maximum nutritional benefit, all pulses&nbsp;are best consumed sprouted, a form in which they retain their high-protein, high-density character but contain plant phytonutrients&nbsp;in unmatched quantities. A healthy person can enjoy them cooked on occasion, but the pulses that I mention arebest eaten germinated&nbsp;(all pulses should be germinated before being cooked).</p>
<h3>Azuki Beans</h3>
<p>Azuki, a popular legume&nbsp;in many parts of Eastern Asia, is one of the most digestible beans available. It contains all of the powerful nutrients&nbsp;found in its cousins but is more easily digested than any of them, with the exception of mung. It is a healer of lung, kidney, and bladder ailments due to its high antioxidant and phytochemical content.</p>
<h3>Chickpeas</h3>
<p>How can I say enough about chickpeas? Their usefulness as a staple food&nbsp;will be clear if you look at cuisines across the globe. This legume&nbsp;is prominent from Cuba to Turkey, from Mexico to India.</p>
<p>The physical profile of a chickpea looks rippled, like a well-sculpted abdomen. And its physique corresponds to the legume’s’ healthfulness. Chickpeas are rich in daidzein, a powerful isoflavone&nbsp;that is one of nature’s biggest cancer&nbsp;fighters. Most of the studies on this isoflavone have been conducted on soybeans, but other legumes, especially chickpeas, have higher levels of the substance. (It is easy to research soybeans&nbsp;because they are so widely consumed, but of all the legumes&nbsp;they are one of the least healthful and difficult to digest even when raw.)</p>
<p>Sprouted chick peas&nbsp;are one of the most delicious and least flatulence-producing legumes.</p>
<h3>Lentils</h3>
<p>Lentils, which have been cultivated since the Neolithic age, are one of the oldest human foods. They are also one of the most valuable nutritionally. For this reason, they are widely cultivated throughout the world, especially by largely vegetarian&nbsp;societies.</p>
<p>Genistein is the most prominent isoflavone&nbsp;found in lentils. Although cooked lentils are only a low antioxidant,&nbsp;sprouting&nbsp;increases their healthfulness exponentially. Genistein is usually isolated in soy, but lentils are a better source of the valuable nutrient.&nbsp; Studies have proven genistein’s ability to kill cancer&nbsp;cells, particularly those in the prostate. - [Kyle]</p>
<p>Lentils are also rich source of protease inhibitors, which promote cellular&nbsp;homeostasis, yet these will be completely lost if the lentil is cooked. Luckily, this small, thin lentil germinates quickly and is delicious.</p>
<h3>Peas</h3>
<p>An especially rich source of the isoflavone&nbsp;daidzein, peas&nbsp;provide the benefits of both legumes&nbsp;and green plants. They are best consumed fresh and raw, but dried peas can be prepared like any other legume. When grown as an indoor garden sprout on soil it’s anti-cancer effect greatly increases.<br><strong>&nbsp;</strong></p>
<h2>VEGETABLES</h2>
<p>This category is a mix of things: greens, fruits&nbsp;that work as vegetables, roots, sprouts&nbsp;and tubers. For health seekers and raw-foodists, a meal will be based on food&nbsp;from this category. These are main-course foods; here are some of the best.</p>
<h3>Artichokes</h3>
<p>Artichokes are rich in a flavanoid&nbsp;called silymarin&nbsp;and, like the quercetin&nbsp;so abundant in onions&nbsp;and apples, silymarin protects the liver&nbsp;from toxicity damage. Our organs are constantly being bombarded by oxidants&nbsp;and harmful chemicals. Over time, the damage can be significant. An underachieving liver will force toxins into the bloodstream, causing illness and disease.</p>
<h3>Garlic</h3>
<p>The amount of information on the health benefits of garlic&nbsp;is nearly overwhelming. We know conclusively that it cleanses the body, prevents cancer&nbsp;and acts as a natural antibiotic. Garlic has an extremely high concentration of organo sulflides, but it has been proven that even minimal heating destroys their effectiveness. - <strong>[</strong>Song<strong>]&nbsp; </strong></p>
<p>The best way to consume garlic&nbsp;is by crushing the bulbs through a press and placing the pulp directly on food.</p>
<h3>Onions</h3>
<p>Although vitamin E&nbsp;is often touted as the most powerful antioxidant, quercetin&nbsp;may be even more powerful, and onions&nbsp;contain a higher concentration of this flavanoid&nbsp;than any other known food. Quercetin is so powerful, in fact, that it can effectively neutralize liver&nbsp;damage caused by arsenic&nbsp;exposure. - [Bongiovanni]</p>
<p>Quercetin is being researched by conventional medical scientists who are interested in its ability to rapidly shrink prostate tumors. - [Shoskes]</p>
<p>Onions are also a rich source of allium&nbsp;compounds, organosulfides unique to the allium (or onion and garlic) family.</p>
<h3>Peppers</h3>
<p>As is usually the case, the brilliant colors of ripe peppers, whether sweet or spicy, are a sign that they are brimming with vitality. They should be consumed when they turn red, which is their ripest state, when they contain far more nutrition&nbsp;than they do unripe. Red bell peppers contain nearly four times as much folate&nbsp;as green bell peppers. - [Phillips<strong>] </strong></p>
<h3>Spinach</h3>
<p>I mention spinach&nbsp;because it is a phenomenal food, but most commercial spinach has been stored too long to retain its healthful benefits. Fresh, spinach has all the benefits of dark green foods at maximum concentration.</p>
<h3>Sunflower Sprouts</h3>
<p>Sunflower sprouts&nbsp;are an incredibly powerful food, and I recommend their consumption on a regular basis. Like the sprouts of many seeds high in fatty acids, sunflower sprouts&nbsp;are high in secoisolariciresinol, a lignan&nbsp;(or phytoestrogen), which is a proven anti-carcinogen. - [KITTS]</p>
<p>This research has primarily been done on flax, but flax does not produce a palatable green. Sunflower spouts are a staple food&nbsp;in the raw&nbsp;living diet.</p>
<h3>Sweet Potatoes</h3>
<p>Sweet potatoes are one of the most nutritionally rich foods on the planet. If asked what foods I would take on a permanent trip to a desert island, sweet potatoes&nbsp;would show up near the top, directly after a long list of green foods.</p>
<p>They are amazingly rich in phytonutrients, many of which stand up to blending (sweet potato is edible raw, but it is one of the best vegetables to include in the cooked portion of a healthy person’s diet.)</p>
<p>Although I am primarily referring to the familiar sweet potato tuber, the leaves of the plant are also one of the most nutritious greens available. - [Kurata<strong>] </strong></p>
<p>Sweet potatoes are a virtual cocktail of anti-oxidizing&nbsp;nutrients. If you are lucky enough to have enough space to plant a garden, sweet potatoes&nbsp;are an excellent choice. The sweet potato blossom is also edible and sometimes available at Asian supermarkets in dried form.</p>
<h2>Cruciferous Vegetables</h2>
<p><em>I have places these vegetables, all of which belong to the mustard</em><em>&nbsp;family, in their own category. All share similar nutrients</em><em>, most notably the glucosinolate sulforaphane</em><em>. Glucosinolates are sulfur-based organic</em><em>&nbsp;compounds (forms of</em><em> Isothiocyanates</em><em>) that plants use to deter pests, and sulforaphane is one of the most common. It is present in all crucifers and responsible for their pungent</em><em>&nbsp;flavor. Naturally, more pungent foods like mustard and arugula</em><em>&nbsp;tend to be higher in this natural chemical. It is also responsible for the spicy flavor of horseradish. </em><em>Sulforaphane is one of</em><em> the most powerful antioxidants</em><em>&nbsp;known. <br><br></em></p>
<p>The amount of research that has been done on the healthfulness of these vegetables over the last decade is impressive. Not only are they proven cancer&nbsp;fighters, but sulphoraphane’s pest-deterring qualities seem to have an effect on bacteria&nbsp;that are harmful to humans.</p>
<p>A landmark study published in 2002 demonstrated the link between consumption of sulphoraphane-rich foods and a reduction of the stomach pathogen Helicobacter pylori.- [Fahey].</p>
<p>This bacteria&nbsp;is responsible for ulcers and most stomach cancer, especially in tropical regions.</p>
<p>I will list a few of the most notable and accessible species, but there are literally hundreds. All are superb.</p>
<h3>Arugula</h3>
<p>Arugula&nbsp;is loved by those who gravitate toward vital&nbsp;foods. Its pungent&nbsp;flavor is stimulating for both the senses and the digestive system, and eating the greens provides a sense of well-being.</p>
<h3>Bok Choy</h3>
<p>A popular Chinese vegetable, bok choy&nbsp;is light and not as strongly flavored as most of its cousins.</p>
<h3>Broccoli</h3>
<p>Broccoli, of course, is king of the cruciferous vegetables. One should eat nothing but organic&nbsp;food, but this is especially important in the case of broccoli. Broccoli (and its cousin, cauliflower) is a sponge for pesticides. Organic broccoli is also far more nutritious.</p>
<h3>Cabbage</h3>
<p>Cabbage is an incredible food. Although it seems denser than a potato, cabbage&nbsp;is nutrient-packed from its leaves to its core.</p>
<h3>Cauliflower</h3>
<p>Not as nutritious as broccoli, but excellent nonetheless. Don’t discard the green leaves on the sides of a cauliflower&nbsp;head - they are as delicious as cabbage!</p>
<h3>Collard Greens</h3>
<p>Collards are not as strongly flavored as kale, but their flavor is similar. As well as sulforaphane, they are also a rich source of zeaxanthin, a yellow carotenoid&nbsp;linked to the prevention&nbsp;of age-related macular degeneration.</p>
<h3>Kale</h3>
<p>Kale&nbsp;is deep green (some species&nbsp;are nearly blue) and closer to its wild ancestors than most of its cousins. Kale should be eaten regularly.</p>
<h3>Mustard Greens</h3>
<p>Mustard greens&nbsp;taste like… well, mustard. Their seeds are used to flavor the ubiquitous mustard condiment, and the greens have a similar flavor.</p>
<h3>Watercress</h3>
<p>With a flavor not completely unlike that of mustard and arugula, watercress&nbsp;tends to be milder than both. It is one of the oldest cultivated greens.</p>
<h2>FRUIT</h2>
<p><em>For a healthy person, there is nothing wrong with including a moderate amount of fruit in the diet</em><em>. Eat fruit in moderation, however; the high sugar</em><em>&nbsp;content of fruit (even that of acid citrus) makes over consumption dangerous. A large quantity of sugar overworks our vital</em><em>&nbsp;organs and drains us of vitality</em><em>. </em></p>
<h3>Açaí</h3>
<p>Açaí is nearly impossible to find fresh if you don’t live in Brazil, but this unique fruit from a tropical palm is widely available in frozen form. It has become a “wonder food” for its unique nutritional profile. Besides being packed with scores of phytonutrients, açaí&nbsp;also contains an exceptional level of essential fatty and amino acids.</p>
<p>Açaí’s phytonutrient&nbsp;qualities are mainly due to Anthocyanin, water-soluble pigments that show as blue or red in leaves or the flesh of fruit. Notably, they are responsible for the color red in apples and roses. Other compounds found in the skin&nbsp;are Cyandin 3-glucoside and cyanidin 3-rutinoside, orientin, taxifolin deoxyhexose, isovitexin and scoparin. - [Schauss]</p>
<p>It is safe to say that, given its remarkable nutritional profile, this “berry” is one of the more complete foods on the planet.</p>
<p>That said, it is a sweet fruit, and a great deal of the attention it gets may be due to the fact that it tastes like chocolate and happens to be rather good for you. Don’t overdue it, in other words. It is always best to rely on green vegetables and foods with lower sugar&nbsp;content. A great deal of the vital&nbsp;energy provided by the fruit may be compromised when the body is forced to deal with a high sugar load.</p>
<h3>Apples</h3>
<p>We use apples&nbsp;at Hippocrates&nbsp;in conjunction with our liver&nbsp;cleanse. Like onions, they are high in quercitin, one of the most powerful antioxidants&nbsp;known to man. They also contain catechins&nbsp;and tartaric acid.</p>
<h3>Blueberries</h3>
<p>There is a great deal of talk about the blueberry, and most of it is warranted: the blueberry is a powerful food. As always, consumption of sweet fruit should be limited, but blueberries are one of the most powerful and antioxidant-rich foods available. One of the nice things about blueberries is that they are widely available.</p>
<p>Perhaps one of the reasons that blueberries are so nutritious is that, unlike many cultivated fruits, they are close to a wild food. Wild blueberries, (the type one should eat if at all possible), are dense with the substances that many people seek in wine - without the unhealthy side effects of alcohol consumption. Almost as a rule, dark blue and purple fruits are especially high in antioxidants.</p>
<p>Because blueberries are popular, easy to access, and delicious, a great deal of antioxidant&nbsp;research has been done on them, and a number of studies have demonstrated their ability to reverse cellular&nbsp;destruction and protect against it. - [Yi<strong>] </strong></p>
<h3>Citrus Fruit</h3>
<p>Aside from the vitamin C&nbsp;for which citrus fruits&nbsp;are known, there are many reasons to indulge in citrus fruit, particularly those with less sugar&nbsp;such as lime and grapefruit. (These not only have the least sugar but they are the most nutritious). All citrus fruits contain high levels of alpha and beta carotene, and rinds&nbsp;of all citrus fruit are high in monoterpene&nbsp;and D-Limonene, powerful anti-cancer&nbsp;agents.</p>
<h3>Goji Berry</h3>
<p>Like the açaí, the goji berry&nbsp;(also known as the wolfberry) is a much hyped fruit fashionable in health-conscious circles. And like açaí, it is virtually impossible to find fresh. While açaí is often sold frozen, however, goji berrys are popular as a dried snack. The fact that the berries are dried increases the risk of overeating sugar.</p>
<p>That said, research done on this high-protein, high-polysaccharides member of the nightshade family&nbsp;has proven that they are undoubtedly a superfood. With one of the highest antioxidant&nbsp;levels of any known food, goji berries are incredible at protecting cells&nbsp;from free radicals&nbsp;and thereby preventing cancer. - [HU]</p>
<p>As we age, the only way to retain maximum vitality&nbsp;is by preserving our senses, including sight, which is often the first to go. Goji berries are rich in the carotenoids&nbsp;zeaxanthin&nbsp;and lutein, both of which are vital&nbsp;to proper vision and the prevention&nbsp;of macular degeneration.&nbsp; Carotenoids, particularly these two, are so important to vision that they may single-handedly prevent the formation of cataracts. - [Trevithick-Sutton]</p>
<p>This would be a good time for a reminder that in seeking full-spectrum nutrition, just because there are volumes of research on how wonderful goji berries are, and just because they are highly nutritious it doesn’t mean that one should make them a staple food.</p>
<h3>Mangosteen</h3>
<p>Mangosteen (which is unrelated to mango) has all the characteristics of an over-hyped fruit: as well as purportedly being excellent for us, it is also rather difficult to find, and is prohibitively expensive. Most people who do not live in a tropical environment&nbsp;will be lucky to see it in a form other than pasteurized juice. In this form it is almost always adulterated with other fruit juices.</p>
<p>Mangosteen is truly unique, and its health benefits make it well worth the effort it takes to procure it.&nbsp; Because mangosteen contains a variety and quantity of nutrition&nbsp;unavailable in most fruit, I mention it here with great praise.</p>
<p>The miraculous attributes of this strange looking, tangerine-sized fruit are due to xanthones, compounds used by the plant to deter pests. Over 200 xanthones have been discovered, and most of them can be found in the pericarp (the flesh surrounding the skin) of the mangosteen&nbsp;fruit. Virtually all are powerful deterrents of fungus, cancer, and viruses. - [Moongkarndi]</p>
<p>Pharmaceutical companies are busy trying to discover why xanthones&nbsp;are so effective against leukemia; pharmaceutical drugs do not work nearly as well. The most active and unique of the compounds seems to be mangostin which, as its name suggests, is unique to this fruit.</p>
<h3>Noni</h3>
<p>Noni is a strange fruit. Like some others on this list, one is unlikely to find it fresh in the produce section of the grocery story. But this isn’t because the fruit is simply difficult to ship. Ripe noni’s scent has been likened to dirty feet or rotten cheese. It is not a delicious fruit, and on its native island of Fiji it is only eaten as a famine food.</p>
<p>Nevertheless, noni&nbsp;is available at most health-food&nbsp;stores, usually in pasteurized juice form. Though studies are largely inconclusive, the fruit seems to exhibit some anti-cancer&nbsp;properties. Noni is safe to use, and I take it myself. My only recommendation would be to make sure that the noni extract you choose is as pure and uncooked as possible. Certain companies ride on the reputation of a touted “superfood” but adulterate their extract with large quantities of apple juice, grape juice or sugar. Pure noni enhances cell anatomy communication.</p>
<h3>Papaya</h3>
<p>Papaya&nbsp;is notable for being high in carotenoids, as one would expect from such an orange fruit. It is also high in digestive enzymes.</p>
<h3>Pomegranate</h3>
<p>As one would expect, this high-pigment fruit is extremely vital. I recommend eating the seeds of the pomegranate&nbsp;over drinking the juice). This fruit is <em>entirely </em>as nutritious as the red grape’s thin skin&nbsp;(see below).</p>
<h3>Red Grapes</h3>
<p>Research demonstrating the healthful effects of wine is rather silly, since the very same nutrients&nbsp;supposedly abundant in wine are obviously found in grapes as well. Dark-colored grapes contain the highest level of resveratrol, a powerful phytoalexin. Other plants have it as well, notably raspberries and mulberries, but deeply-colored grape skins are an incredible source.</p>
<h3>Watermelon</h3>
<p>Watermelon&nbsp;contains an abundance of lycopene, the same nutrient&nbsp;found in tomatoes and other red fruits&nbsp;and vegetables. It also contains zeaxanthin, sulphoraphane, and indole-3-carbinol.</p>
<p><strong>Nuts and Seeds </strong></p>
<p><em>Nuts and seeds should be eaten sparingly. Often, those new to the raw</em><em>&nbsp;food</em><em>&nbsp;diet</em><em>&nbsp;eat far too many, which is understandable: the transition from a high fat, high density diet can be challenging and requires a transition. That said, sprouted organic nuts</em><em>&nbsp;and seeds are a must. They provide us with protein</em><em>, phytonutrients</em><em>, and essential fatty acids</em><em>. Without these fatty acids</em><em>, other nutrients</em><em>&nbsp;are not absorbed by the body. They are also important for proper brain</em><em>&nbsp;function. I mention them here not as much for their antioxidants</em><em>&nbsp;&nbsp;(which they have, but those should come primarily from foods with a high water</em><em>&nbsp;content) but for the part they play in processing other nutrients.<br><br></em></p>
<p><em>Nuts should always be eaten raw</em><em>, preferably germinated</em><em>, and should be purchased from an organic seller – old nuts</em><em>&nbsp;will contain rancid oils that defeat the purpose of eating them. Store nuts in a refrigerator or, for long-term storage, a freezer.&nbsp; </em></p>
<h3>Almonds</h3>
<p>Almonds&nbsp;are the most digestible of the nuts, and the easiest to consume in germinated&nbsp;form. They contain a high level of bio-available fatty acids.</p>
<h3>Pine Nuts</h3>
<p>Pine nuts contain about 31% protein, making them higher in protein than any other nut. Like all nuts, they should be eaten sparingly but often. One of the reasons that you should be sparing with pine nuts is because they are rather unpalatable in germinated&nbsp;form.</p>
<h3>Pistachios</h3>
<p>The pistachio&nbsp;is a familiar nut whose color should clue you in to its possible health benefits: bright green, deep red, rusty orange – what a beautiful nut! As previously mentioned, the color of food&nbsp;is a great indicator of whether it will increase our vitality.</p>
<h3>Sesame Seeds</h3>
<p>Filled with lignans&nbsp;(sesamin, sesaminol, sesamolinol, sesamolin), vitamin&nbsp;E, lecithin, pinoresinol, myristic acid, and linoleate, sesame seeds&nbsp;are one of the most nutritious, oil-rich foods. Raw tahini&nbsp;(sesame butter) is an important element in vegan&nbsp;cuisine. - <strong>[</strong>Morris<strong>]</strong></p>
<h3>Walnuts</h3>
<p>The walnut&nbsp;is one of the healthiest nuts. If anyone tries to argue the necessity of including fish in the diet&nbsp;for it’s omega-3 fatty acids, simply offer them a handful of walnuts. Fish does not offer any benefit that walnuts do not offer as well, and walnuts contain no pollutants.</p>
<p>The health benefits of nutritional phytochemicals&nbsp;are innumerable. By consuming a variety of these powerhouses in your diet&nbsp;you will invariably create more vitality&nbsp;in your life.</p>

		<title><![CDATA[26 Scientific Studies on Avocado]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/diet/26-scientific-studies-on-avocado/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p><strong><u>Avocados</u></strong></p>
<p>Native to South America and the Caribbean, the avocado tree produces a fruit that is actually a large egg-shaped berry with a sizable seed at its center. Its use among pre-Incan and other ancient Mesoamerican cultures has been dated to about ten thousand years ago by archaeologists. The Aztecs considered avocado to be a fertility booster.</p>
<p>Though dozens of avocado cultivars are harvested, the Hass cultivar accounts for three-fourths of all avocados consumed. Mexico remains by far the biggest producer. Avocados contain much more potassium than bananas, are high in monounsaturated fats and B vitamins, and have a high fiber content. They have proven health benefits in many areas, particularly in lowering levels of harmful LDL and triglycerides and raising levels of beneficial HDL.</p>
<p><strong><u>Anti-Inflammatory</u></strong></p>
<p><em>AV119, a Natural Sugar from Avocado gratissims, Modulates the LPS-Induced Proinflammatory Response in Human Keratinocytes. </em>Donnarumma G, Paoletti I, Buommino E, Et al. Inflammation. 2010 Oct 9 (Epub ahead of print). <strong>Key Finding</strong>: “Our data show that AV119, a patented blend of avocado sugars, is able to modulate significantly the proinflammatory response in human keratinocytes, blocking the NF-kB activation in human keratinocytes.”</p>
<p><strong><u>Atherosclerosis</u></strong></p>
<p><em>Hypoglycemia and hypocholesterolemic potential of Persea Americana leaf extracts. </em>Brai BI, Odetola AA, Agomo PU. J Med Food. 2007 Jun;10(2):356-60. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“These results suggest that aqueous and methanolic leaf extracts of P. Americana (avocado) lower plasma glucose and influence lipid metabolism in hypercholesterolemic rats with consequent lowering of T-CHOL and LDL-CHOL, and a restoration of HDL-CHOL levels. This could represent a protective mechanism against the development of <strong>atherosclerosis.</strong>”</p>
<p><strong><u>Cancer (oral; prostate)</u></strong></p>
<p><em>Selective induction of apoptosis of human <strong>oral cancer</strong> cell lines by avocado extracts via a ROS-mediated mechanism. </em>Ding H, Han C, Guo D, Chin YW, Ding Y, Kinghorn AD, D’Ambrosio SM. Nutr Cancer. 2009;61(3):348-56. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“Avocados have a high content of phytochemicals with potential chemo preventive activity. Previously we reported that phytochemicals extracted from avocado meat selectively induced apoptosis in cancer but not normal, human oral epithelial cell lines. In the present study, we observed that treatment of human oral cancer cell lines containing high levels of reactive oxygen (ROS) with D003 increased ROS levels twofold to threefold and induced apoptosis. These data suggest that perturbing the ROS levels in human oral cancer cell lines may be a key factor in selective apoptosis and molecular targeting for chemoprevention by photochemical.”</p>
<p><em>Chemoproventive characteristics of avocado fruit. </em>Ding H, Chin YW, Kinghorn AD, D’Ambrosio SM. Semin Cancer Biol. 2007 Oct;17(5):386-94. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“Our recent studies indicate that phytochemicals extracted with chloroform from avocado fruits target multiple signaling pathways and increase intracellular reactive oxygen leading to apoptosis. This review summarizes the reported phytochemicals in avocado fruit and discusses their molecular mechanisms and targets. These studies suggest that individual and combinations of phytochemicals from the avocado fruit may offer an advantageous dietary strategy in <strong>cancer </strong>prevention.”</p>
<p><em>Inhibition of <strong>prostate cancer</strong> cell growth by an avocado extract: role of lipid-soluble bioactive substances. </em>Lu QY, Arteaga JR, Zhang Q, Huerta S, Go VL, Heber D. J Nutr Biochem. 2005 Jan;16(1):23-30. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“Avocado contains numerous bioactive carotenoids. Because the avocado also contains a significant amount of monounsaturated fat, these bioactive carotenoids are likely to be absorbed into the bloodstream, where in combination with other diet-derived phytochemicals they may contribute to the significant cancer risk reduction associated with a diet of fruits and vegetables.”</p>
<p><em>An avocado constituent, persenone A, suppresses expression of inducible forms of nitric oxide synthase and cyclooxygenase in macrophages, and hydrogen peroxide generation in mouse skin. </em>Kim OK, Murakami A, Takahashi D, Nakamura Y, Torikai K, Kim HW, Ohigashi H. Biosci Biotechnol Biochem. 2000 Nov;64(11):2504-7. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“This study suggests that persenone A, an avocado constituent, is a possible agent to prevent inflammation-associated diseases including <strong>cancer</strong>.”</p>
<p><strong><u>Cholesterol (and Hypercholesterolemia)</u></strong></p>
<p><em>High-density lipoproteins (HDL) size and composition are modified in the rat by a diet supplemented with “Hass” avocado (Persea Americana Miller). </em>Perez-Mendez O, Garcia Hernandez L. Arch Cardiol Mex. (Spanish). 2007 Jan-Mar;77(1):17-24. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“The inclusion of avocado in the diet decreased plasma triglycerides increased HDL-<strong>cholesterol</strong> plasma levels and modified HDL structure. The latter effect may enhance the antiatherogenic properties of HDL.”</p>
<p><em>Effects of a vegetarian diet vs. a vegetarian diet enriched with avocado in <strong>hypercholesterolemic</strong> patients. </em>Carrznza-Madrigal J, Herrera-Abarca JE, Alvizouri-Munoz M, Alvarado-Jimenez MR, Chavez-Carbajal F. Arch Med Res. 1997 Winter;28(4):537-41. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“All three diets reduced HDL levels. To obtain beneficial effects on lipid profile with avocado, lower amounts of carbohydrates and polyunsaturated fatty acids are probably needed.”</p>
<p><em>Monounsaturated fatty acid (avocado) rich diet for mild <strong>hypercholesterolemia.</strong> </em>Lopez LR, Frati Munari AC, Hernandez Dominguez BC, Cervantes MS, Hernandez Luna MH, Juarez C, Moran LS. Arch Med Res. 1996 Winter;27(4):519-23. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“High lipid, high MFA-avocado enriched diet can improve lipid profile in healthy and especially in mild hypercholesterolemic patients, even if hypertriglyceridemia (combined hyperlipidemia) is present.”</p>
<p><em>Effects of avocado on the level of <strong>blood lipids</strong> in patients with phenotype II and IV dyslipidemias. </em>Carranza J, Alvizouri M, Alvarado MR, Chavez F, Gomez M, Herrera JE. Arch Inst Cardio Mex. (Spanish). 1995 Jul-Aug;65(4):342-8. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“Avocado is an excellent source of monounsaturated fatty acids in diets designed to treat hypercholesterolemia with some advantages over low-fat diets with a greater amount of carbohydrates.”</p>
<p><em>Carotenoid absorption from salad and salsa by humans is enhanced by the addition of avocado or avocado oil. </em>Unlu NZ, Bohn T, Clinton SK, Schwartz SJ. J Nutr. 2005 Mar;135(3):431-6. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“Adding avocado fruit can significantly enhance carotenoid absorption from salad and salsa, which is attributed primarily to the lipids present in avocado.”</p>
<p><strong><u>Hypertension</u></strong></p>
<p><em>Cardiovascular effects of Persea Americana Mill (Lauraceae) (avocado) aqueous leaf extract in experimental animals. </em>Ojewole JA, Kamadyaapa DR, Gondwe MM, Moodley K, Musabayane CT. Cardiovasc J Afr. 2007 Mar-Apr;18(2):69-76. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“The findings of this study tend to suggest that P. Americana leaf could be used as a natural supplementary remedy in essential <strong>hypertension</strong> and certain cases of cardiac dysfunctions.”</p>
<p><em>Effect of an avocado oil-rich diet over an angiotensin II-induced <strong>blood pressure</strong> response. </em>Salazar MJ, El Hafidi M, Pastelin G, Ramirez-Ortega MC, Sanchez-Mendoza MA. J Ethnopharmacol. 2005 Apr 26;98(3):335-8. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“Avocado oil-rich diet modifies the fatty acid content in cardiac and renal membranes in a tissue-specific manner. Diet content can be a key factor in vascular responses.”</p>
<p><strong><u>Osteoarthritis</u></strong></p>
<p><em>A potential role for avocado and soybean based nutritional supplements in the management of osteoarthritis: a review. </em>Dinubile NA. Phys Sportsmed. 2010 Jun;38(2):71-81. <strong>Key Finding</strong>: “Basic scientific research studies and a systematic review and meta-analysis of the available high-quality randomized clinical trials indicate that 300 mg of avocado and soybean unsaponifiables per day (with or without glucosamine and chondroitin sulfate) appears to be beneficial for patients with <strong>hip or knee osteoarthritis</strong>.”</p>
<p><em>Symptomatic efficacy of avocado-soybean unsaponifiables (ASU) in <strong>osteoarthritis </strong>(OA) patients: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. </em>Christensen R, Bartels EM, Astrup A, Bliddal H. Osteoarthritis Cartilage. 2008 Apr;16(4):399-408. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“Based on the available evidence, patients may be recommended to give avocado/soybean unsaponifiables a chance for e.g., 3 months. Meta-analysis data support better chances of success in patients with knee OA than in those with hip OA.”</p>
<p><em>Avocado/soybean unsaponifiables in the treatment of knee and hip <strong>osteoarthritis.</strong> </em>Angermann P. Ugeskr Laeger (Danish). 2005 Aug 15;167(33):3023-5. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“These studies indicate that ASU has an effect on the symptoms of knee and hip osteoarthritis but not on the structural changes caused by osteoarthritis.”</p>
<p><em>Avocado-soybean unsaponifiables (ASU) for <strong>osteoarthritis</strong>—a systematic review. </em>Ernst E. Clin Rheumatol. 2003 Oct;22(4-5):285-8. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“The majority of rigorous trial data available to date suggest that avocado/soybean unsaponifiables is effective for the symptomatic treatment of osteoarthritis.”</p>
<p><em>Structural effect of avocado/soybean unsaponifiables on joint space loss in <strong>osteoarthritis </strong>of the hip. </em>Lequesne M, Maheu E, Cadet C, Dreiser RL. Arthritis Rheum. 2002 Feb;47(1):50-8. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“Avocado/soybean unsaponifiables significantly reduced the progression of joint space loss as compared with placebo in the subgroup of patients with advanced joint space narrowing.”</p>
<p><em>Symptoms modifying effect of avocado/soybean unsaponifiables (ASU) in <strong>knee osteoarthritis</strong>. A double-blind, prospective, placebo-controlled study. </em>Appelboom T, Schuermans J, Verbruggen G, Henrotin Y, Reginster JY. Scand J Rheumatol. 2001;30(4):242-7. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“The efficacy of ASU at a dosage of 300mg/day and 600mg/day was consistently superior to that of placebo at all endpoints, with no differences observed between the two doses.”</p>
<p><em>Modification of articular cartilage and subchondral bone pathology in an ovine meniscetomy model of <strong>osteoarthritis</strong> by avocado and soya unsaponifiables (ASU). </em>Cake MA, Read RA, Guillou B, Ghosh P. Osteoarthritis Cartilage. 2000 Nov;8(6):404-11. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“These findings support other studies which have proposed that avocado and soya unsaponifiables may exhibit disease-modifying anti-osteoarthritis activity.”</p>
<p><em>The possible ‘chondroprotective’ effect of the unsaponifiable constituents of avocado and soya in vivo. </em>Khayyal MT, el-Ghazaly MA. Drugs Exp Clin Res. 1998;24(1):41-50. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“An experimental in vivo model for studying <strong>cartilage destruction</strong> has been used to study the possible chondroprotective effect of the unsaponifiable constituents of avocado, soya and their combination. The unsaponifiables of both avocado and soya significantly reduced the degenerative changes induced by the granuloma tissue on the implanted cartilage in control animals. The effect was even more marked when animals were treated with the combination of the two unsaponifiables at a 1:2 ratio.”</p>
<p><em>Efficacy and safety of avocado/soybean unsaponifiables in the treatment of symptomatic <strong>osteoarthritis </strong>of the knee and hip. A prospective, multicenter, three-month, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. </em>Blotman F, Maheu E, Wulwik A, Caspard H, Lopez A. Rev Rhum Engl Ed. 1997 Dec;64(12):825-34. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“One of the objectives of symptomatic slow-acting drugs for osteoarthritis is to reduce the need for drugs with a less favorable safety profile, mainly analgesics and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. Avocado/soybean unsaponifiables reduced the need for these drugs in patients with primary femorotibial or hip osteoarthritis. The functional index showed a significantly greater improvement in the active (avocado/soybean) group.”</p>
<p><strong><u>Psoriasis</u></strong></p>
<p><em>Vitamin B(12) cream containing avocado oil in the therapy of plaque <strong>psoriasis</strong>. </em>Stucker M, Memmel U, Hoffmann M, Hartung J, Altmeyer P. Dermatology. 2001;203(2):141-7. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“The results of this clinical trial provide evidence that the recently developed vitamin B (12) cream containing avocado oil has considerable potential as a well-tolerated, long-term topical therapy of psoriasis.”</p>
<p><em>The effect of various avocado oils on skin collagen metabolism. </em>Werman MJ, Mokady S, Nimni ME, Neeman I. Connect Tissue Res. 1991;26(1-2):1-10. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“The effects of various avocado oils on collagen metabolism in skin were studied in growing rats. Rats fed the unrefined avocado oil extracted with hexane from the intact fruit, its unsaponifiables or the avocado seed oil, showed significant increases in soluble collagen content in skin.”</p>
<p><strong><u>Schleroderma</u></strong></p>
<p><em>Natural remedies for <strong>schleroderma</strong>. </em>Gaby AR. Altern Med Rev. 2006 Sep;11(3):188-95. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>Avocado/soybean extract is a promising natural treatment for scleroderma, an <strong>autoimmune disease</strong> of the connective tissue characterized by fibrosis and thickening of various tissues.</p>
<p><strong><u>Wounds</u></strong></p>
<p><strong><em>Wound healing</em></strong><em> activity of Persea Americana (avocado) fruit: a preclinical study on rats. </em>Nayak BS, Raju SS, Chalapathia Rao AV. J Wound Care. 2008 Mar;17(3):123-6. <strong>Key Finding: </strong>“Avocado oil is rich in nutrient waxes, proteins and minerals, as well as vitamins A, D and E. It is an excellent source of enrichment for dry, damaged or chapped skin. This study aimed to evaluate the wound-healing activity of fruit extract of Persea Americana in rats. Rate of wound contraction, epithelialization time, together with the hydroxyproline content and histological observations, supports the use of Persea Americana in the management of wound healing.”</p>

		<title><![CDATA[Where is Sugar Hiding?]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/diet/where-is-sugar-hiding/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <h3>Where Does Sugar Hide?</h3>
<p>By far the largest source of added sugars (which includes both table sugar and high-fructose corn syrup) in the North American diet comes from sugar-sweetened beverages—soft drinks, sports drinks, energy drinks, and tea and coffee to which sweeteners have been added. Statistics paint a large part of this disturbing health story. According to the Centers for Disease Control, from 1980 to 2011 the diagnosed cases of diabetes in the U.S. increased 167% for people below 44 years of age, though almost comparable increases were recorded for all age groups. During that same period, obesity prevalence increased nearly three-fold until by 2010, 35.5% of U.S. adults were classified as obese. It is certainly no coincidence that during the same time frame that diabetes and obesity became a documented contagion, consumption of sugar-sweetened beverages increased 135% among all age groups. Consider how closely the statistics track each other: a 167% diabetes increase during the same general time period as a 135% increase in sugar-sweetened beverage intake. Studies reported over the past decade further sealed the direct connection between sugar consumption and diabetes risk. This was true worldwide. European researchers studying hundreds of adolescents in 2013 found that markers for diabetes, such as insulin resistance, became measurably elevated in those who consumed sugar-sweetened beverages five times a week versus those who drank them two or so times a week. The frequency of consumption was directly linked to an increased risk for diabetes. Published in the British Journal of Nutrition, a team of scientists examined medical studies from dozens of countries in 2014 and compared the results, finding an unmistakable pattern of both sugar-sweetened and artificially-sweetened beverages sharply raising type 2 diabetes risks. More intensive analysis of the study literature in the journal Obesity Review turned up more specifics about the risks: just one to two servings a day of sugar-sweetened beverages raises the overall type 2 diabetes risk by 26% compared to drinking just one such beverage a week.</p>
<h3>Hidden Sugars in Alcoholic Drinks Are Often Overlooked</h3>
<p>Some of the self-professed ‘healthiest’ eaters, people who are vegetarians or vegans and believe they are effectively managing their sugar intake, make a serious mistake by drinking alcohol in any form and thinking this is not having an impact on their risk for developing diabetes and other health problems. Most people have absolutely no idea how much sugar lurks inside those alcoholic drinks. And despite what some of you may choose to believe, it’s not just beer that provides the highest sugar content and calories to inflate your waistline. A March 2014 report released by the World Health Organization advised adults to consume no more than 25 grams of sugar a day from all sources, about six teaspoons. Many people absorb more than that in the alcohol they consume on a daily basis as a so-called ‘social’ drinker.</p>
<p><img class="mb-15 mb-lg-20" src="/wp-content/uploads/2016/05/iStock_000079691837_Double.jpg" alt=""></p>
<blockquote>• Apple cider (alcoholic): 20.5 grams of sugar in a pint. (0.72 ounce)<br><br>
<p>• Port wine: 20 grams of sugar per glass. (0.70 ounce)</p>
<p>• Bailey’s Irish Cream: 19.5 grams per 100 ml. (0.68 ounce)</p>
<p>• Sherry: 9.5 grams per 100 ml. (0.33 ounce)</p>
<p>• Gordon Gin: 14 grams per 250 ml. (0.49 ounce)</p>
<p>• Ale beers: 5 grams per 500 ml. bottle. (0.17 ounce)</p>
<p>• Merlot wine: 2 grams per glass. (0.07 ounce)</p>
<p>• Champagne: 1.5 grams per glass. (0.05 ounce)</p>
</blockquote>
<p>The human body treats the presence of alcohol as if it were a nasty chemical toxin; that helps to explain why inebriation produces headaches, fatigue and other symptoms in the body after this alcohol has been absorbed. After drinking an alcoholic beverage, your blood sugar levels drop. This can be particularly dangerous if you exercise before drinking alcohol because exercise also lowers blood sugar levels. What this effect does is to produce cravings for sugary and carbohydrate-laden foods, making alcohol a trigger for repeated cycles of overeating and addictive sugar consumption.</p>
<p>Finally, I want to share with you the abstract of a report by Dr. Robert Lustig, one of the pioneers in warning about the dangers of sweeteners, who has drawn a link between fructose and alcohol in their related effects on the body. Fructose: it’s alcohol without the buzz. Lustig RH1. Advances in Nutrition. 2013 Mar 1;4(2):226-35. doi: 10.3945/an.112.002998. “What do the Atkins Diet and the traditional Japanese diet have in common? The Atkins Diet is low in carbohydrate and usually high in fat; the Japanese diet is high in carbohydrate and usually low in fat. Yet both work to promote weight loss. One commonality of both diets is that they both eliminate the monosaccharide fructose. Sucrose (table sugar) and its synthetic sister high fructose corn syrup consist of 2 molecules, glucose and fructose. Glucose is the molecule that when polymerized forms starch, which has a high glycemic index, generates an insulin response, and is not particularly sweet. Fructose is found in fruit {and yet it} does not generate an insulin response, and is very sweet. Fructose consumption has increased worldwide, paralleling the obesity and chronic metabolic disease pandemic. Sugar (i.e., fructose- containing mixtures) has been vilified by nutritionists for ages as a source of “empty calories,” no different from any other empty calorie. However, fructose is unlike glucose. In the hypercaloric glycogen-replete state, intermediary metabolites from fructose metabolism overwhelm hepatic mitochondrial capacity, which promotes de novo lipogenesis and leads to hepatic insulin resistance, which drives chronic metabolic disease. Fructose also promotes reactive oxygen species formation, which leads to cellular dysfunction and aging, and promotes changes in the brain’s reward system, which drives excessive consumption. Thus, fructose can exert detrimental health effects beyond its calories and in ways that mimic those of ethanol, its metabolic cousin. Indeed, the only distinction is that because fructose is not metabolized in the central nervous system, it does not exert the acute neuronal depression experienced by those imbibing ethanol. These metabolic and hedonic analogies argue that fructose should be thought of as “alcohol without the buzz.”</p>
<p>By Brian Clement, PhD, LN</p>

		<title><![CDATA[Oral Hygiene’s Sweet Disaster]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/health/oral-hygiene-s-sweet-disaster/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p>It was a long time coming but finally, in 2014, a prominent medical journal published the definitive scientific study telling consumers what many of us had already had&nbsp;intuitively known: eating sugar triggers not just tooth decay, but initiates the more serious condition called periodontal disease, a gum impairment which leads to even more devastating ailments.</p>
<p>Writing in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, a team of five scientists described how they studied data from 2,437 young adults, ages 18 to 25, and estimated their sugar intake using food-frequency questionnaires. Periodontal disease in&nbsp;the study participants was considered to be present based on gum bleeding on probing to a depth of about 3 mm at one or more gum sites. In both the upper and middle levels of sugar consumption among the young adults, periodontal disease was found. The sugar connection was clear.</p>
<p>It’s known that the type of bacteria producing periodontal disease thrive when the human mouth is an acidic environment, which is what dietary sugars are expert at creating. When those bacteria and resultant plaque produce inflammation of the gums around the teeth, gingivitis starts and if left untreated, evolves into pyorrhea, a chronic degenerative gum condition resulting in tooth loss.</p>
<p>Periodontal disease is accelerated even more as a result of nutritional deficiencies, such as Vitamin C and Vitamin D deficits. These deficiencies also destroy bone around the teeth and the periodontal ligaments anchoring your teeth to your jawbone.</p>
<p>It’s estimated that up to 75% of all American adults, and most likely the same in most developed countries, currently have some degree of gum disease, mostly as a result of high sweetener usage.</p>
<p>In postmenopausal women, it’s well established that the loss of bone density, the disease commonly called osteoporosis, can be traced in part to the occurrence of periodontal disease. One reason is that periodontal conditions can combine with postmenopausal estrogen deficiencies to dramatically reduce&nbsp;bone mineral density. Whole Food Vitamin and mineral supplements are important for these women to take in order to help correct the risk factors.</p>
<p>Among other findings in the sugar consumption=periodontal disease=other ailments scenario is the connection to Rheumatoid arthritis.</p>
<p>Still another connection exists between sugar consumption, periodontal disease, and the onset and severity of diabetes. After reviewing research on the common links between sugar, periodontal disease, and diabetes, Dr. Steven W. Seibert, an Illinois specialist in the field of Periodontology, noted how the sugar link swings both ways: “Research has emerged that suggests that the relationship between periodontal disease and diabetes goes both ways. Periodontal disease may make it more difficult for people who have diabetes to control their blood sugar, and people who have uncontrolled diabetes and uncontrolled blood sugar level may be more prone to having periodontal disease.”</p>
<p>We’ve come a long way in our understanding of sugar’s toxic effects on the human mouth since 1983, when a report in the British medical journal, The Lancet, observed: “Sugar is the principal cause of the most common disease in industrialized countries, dental caries (decay).”</p>
<p>Now with confirmation that sweeteners are directly linked to periodontal disease and not just tooth decay, medical science can finally begin to explore all of the many possible ways&nbsp;that migration of toxic bacteria from the mouth, caused by sugar consumption, can wreak havoc on the human body and its health.</p>
<p>“Sugar is the principal cause of the most common disease in industrialized countries, dental caries. The sugars implicated in dental caries, in decreasing order of cariogenicity, are sucrose, glucose, and fructose; brown sugars are as cariogenic as white. The level of sugar consumption at which most of the population will not get dental caries is 15 kg/person a year. The goal should therefore be to reduce consumption to this level and below.” Sugars and Dental Decay. Sheiham A. The Lancet. 1983 February;321(8319):282–284.</p>
<p><img class="mb-15 mb-lg-20" src="https://hippocratesinst.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/GettyImages-1138968130.jpg" alt=""></p>

            <h1>Bitter Melon</h1>
<p>While Bitter Melon originates from India it is now commonly grown in all tropic and sub-tropic regions world-wide including China, Japan, Korea, Southeast Asia, the Philippines, the Middle East, Africa, and the Caribbean. It is widely used in these regions for both culinary and medicinal purposes. The texture is juicy and its’ appearance resembles that of cucumber only more bitter in taste and having a more bumpy and jagged exterior. It can be eaten raw and is a popular ingredient in some Southeast Asian and Indian salads.</p>
<p>Bitter melon has been traditionally used for a wide variety of medicinal purposes in many different cultures. In Okinawa, the indigenous people popularly credit this widely used vegetable for their legendary long life expectancy. Other traditional medicinal uses include stomach complaints, fever, diabetes, respiratory ailments, skin problems, ulcers, gout, and rheumatism.</p>
<p>Here at Wheatgrass Central we grow over one hundred different varieties of vegetables, fruits, herbs, and sprouts in our Greenhouses and our Organic Gardens. Every day we deliver produce grown on-site fresh to the kitchen for the benefit and pleasure of our guests. Come to Hippocrates for our world-renowned Life Transformation Program to get the full download on the amazing benefits of the plant-based diet.</p>

		<title><![CDATA[Drinking Water 101]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/environment/drinking-water-101/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <h4 class="p1">Hey you! You're probably dehydrated!</h4>
<h4 class="p1"><span style="color: #333333;"><span class="s1">Clean Water</span><span class="s2">&nbsp;</span></span></h4>
<p class="p3"><span class="s2">Water is the most important nutrient for your body second only to air. You can go for months without food but, you can only go for a few days without water. Water not only keeps your tissues and organs hydrated but it also assists in the absorption of nutrients to your cells. The water you drink becomes your blood. It gives you energy, reduces inflammation, improves your skin, lubricates your joints, and helps keep you young and healthy! But, what is the best kind of water to drink and where can I find it?</span><span class="s2">&nbsp;</span></p>
<h4 class="p4"><span style="color: #333333;"><span class="s1">Wild Springs</span><span class="s2">&nbsp;</span></span></h4>
<p class="p3"><span class="s2">When it comes to making the safest and healthiest water for human consumption it is a good idea to try to recreate the same conditions in which nature delivers the purest water to us. The best water on earth rises from great depths from free-flowing, natural wild springs. This water is scrubbed by the rocks in a natural cleansing action as it rises by its own volition until it joyously springs forth on the earth’s surface in a celebration of life ready to be consumed. Wild spring water has been distilled by nature and preserved deep within the earth for many hundreds (in some cases thousands) of years far removed from human contamination.</span></p>
<p class="p3"><span class="s2">On its long journey to the surface the water rubs itself against many miles of rocks and crystals. This movement against dissimilar materials charges the water, restructures the water and gives the water energy and life. This process makes the water molecules more linear and structured in such a way that it is more easily absorbable and better hydrating. It also makes any minerals in the water living and organic by charging them in the same way the plants charge the minerals through the xylem in their root structure. This movement prepares and arranges the minerals in such a way that your body can utilize them. Still stagnant water creates dead inorganic minerals.</span></p>
<p><span class="s2">But, not all spring water is created equal. Some springs are better than others. The best springs are typically found in the mountains. Curiously near the peak of the mountains, not near the bottom. Here are some other signs of a good spring:<br></span></p>
<ul>
<li>The water will be consistently cold in every season indicating a very deep aquafer</li>
<li>The water flow rate will be consistent even during periods of little or no rain again indicating a very deep aquafer</li>
<li><span class="s2">The pH will be close to neutral</span></li>
<li><span class="s2"></span><span class="s2">The total dissolved solids (TDS) will be low</span></li>
<li><span class="s2"></span><span class="s2">A high number of turns per foot</span></li>
</ul>
<p><span class="s2"><br>There is a list of wild springs in your area at <a href="http://findaspring.com/"><span class="s5">findaspring.com</span></a>. This online directory is a community and user created database of natural springs around the world. Some of these springs are in public state parks and some are on private property. If you bring your own bottles almost all of them will allow you to collect the wild spring water for free or with a voluntary donation. Some of these springs will have water test results posted. I recommend that you have your wild-crafted spring water professionally tested in a lab to be sure it is safe to drink.<span class="s2">&nbsp;</span><br></span></p>
<h4 class="p4"><span class="s1" style="color: #333333;">Filtered Water</span></h4>
<p class="p3"><span class="s2">Not everyone is fortunate enough to have access to good quality wild springs or have the inclination to go and get collect their own water. Even if you do I would still recommend that you have a really high quality whole house water filtration system professionally installed. This way every time you shower, bath, brush your teeth, wash your clothes, wash your dishes, water your plants, or drink from any faucet in the house you are using clean water. Some whole house water filtration systems simply perform better than others. Typically, these systems are multi-staged since it takes different kinds of filter media to remove different kinds of contaminants.</span></p>
<p class="p3"><em><strong><span class="s2">Here is what to look for in a high quality whole house filtration system:<br><br></span></strong></em></p>
<ol>
<li class="p1">Outputs water with a low TDS (less than 50ppm)</li>
<li class="p1">Removes chlorine</li>
<li class="p1">Removes fluoride</li>
<li class="p1">Removes heavy metals</li>
<li class="p1">Removes pharmaceuticals</li>
</ol>
<p><span class="s2">You will probably notice a drop in water pressure after you install a whole house water filtration system. This is because water filters have to slow the water down in order to be effective. You may want to consider installing a booster pump to maintain your normal water pressure. Water filtration technologies are constantly improving and new and better products are becoming available every year. I teach a class called “Water Wisdom” as a part of the Life Transformation Program where I share with our guests the latest and best technologies and products available and where to get them. There are water filters that will remove most of the contaminants listed above.</span><span class="s2">&nbsp;</span></p>
<p class="p3"><span class="s2">If you do not own your home or you are otherwise disinclined to install a whole house water filtration system I would recommend that you at least install shower head filters on all your showers and use a portable water filters in the kitchen for drinking, preparing meals and in the bathroom for brushing your teeth. You can also get an RV inline hose water filter for watering your outdoor plants. Again, consider coming to Hippocrates to get the full download on the latest and best portable water filter technologies and products available and where to get them.</span></p>
<h4 class="p4"><span class="s1" style="color: #333333;">Bottled Water</span></h4>
<p class="p3"><span class="s2">While bottled water is an environmental disaster it is a reality for some people because of the lifestyle they have created for themselves. I would recommend that you use a reusable water bottle whenever possible preferably made from glass. Bottled drinking water is not regulated by the USDA nor the EPA so there are now laws governing and there is no oversight. As a result the industry is rife with abuse. In fact, 50% of all bottled drinking water tested is nothing more than just plain old tap water. On a scale of one to ten (ten being the best) here is my scoring system for bottled water:</span><span class="s2">&nbsp;</span></p>
<h3 class="p3" style="text-align: center;"><strong><span class="s2">&nbsp;</span><span class="s1">Score</span></strong></h3>
<h4 class="p3" style="text-align: center;"><span class="s2">Starkey (in glass) from Whole Foods &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; 10</span></h4>
<h4 class="p3" style="text-align: center;"><span class="s2">Mountain Valley Spring (in glass)&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; 9</span></h4>
<h4 class="p3" style="text-align: center;"><span class="s2">Voss (still water only – in glass)&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; 8</span></h4>
<h4 class="p3" style="text-align: center;"><span class="s2">Smart Water (in hard plastic)&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; 4</span></h4>
<h4 class="p3" style="text-align: center;"><span class="s2">Deer Park, Nestle, Zephyrhills, etc. (in soft plastic)&nbsp; 0</span></h4>
<h4 class="p3" style="text-align: center;"><em><span class="s2">Please always recycle your bottles.</span></em></h4>
<h4 class="p4"><span class="s1" style="color: #333333;">Enhanced Water</span></h4>
<p class="p3"><span class="s2">Once we have effectively filtered the water the next step is enhancement. It is a good idea to attempt to re-create the same conditions in which nature delivers the purest water to us - freely flowing water from natural wild springs. This movement is nature’s way of energizing and enhancing the water and preparing it for consumption. These natural conditions can be replicated at home with some of the following items:<br></span></p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<ul>
<li class="p1">Pouring</li>
<li class="p1">Stirring</li>
<li class="p1">S-curves</li>
<li class="p1">Whirlpools</li>
<li class="p1">Vortex</li>
<li class="p1">Sacred geometry</li>
<li class="p1">Magnets</li>
<li class="p1">Crystals</li>
<li class="p1">Light</li>
<li class="p1">Positive thoughts&nbsp;</li>
</ul>
<p><span class="s2">This will prepare the water for your cells making it healthier, better hydrating, and better tasting. Water has consciousness and it craves our respect. These types of water enhancements will reenergize, restructure and rememorizes water that has in some cases been abused. Municipal tap water has been unnaturally mixed with chemicals and exposed to pollution, forced through miles of pipes, valves, pumps and machines exposing it to chaotic energies alone its long arduous journey. There are devices that will accomplish the type of desirable enhancements such as the ones listed above. We utilize some of these devices here at Hippocrates for providing the best water for our guests, our associates, and for our plants.</span></p>
<p class="p3"><span class="s2">Here are Hippocrates we take a holistic approach to the natural healing arts. We believe and we teach that if you give your body the right substances, forces influences and conditions that your body will take care of itself. This includes:</span></p>
<ul>
<li class="p4"><span class="s2">Adequate Sunshine</span></li>
<li class="p4"><span class="s2">Pure Fresh Air</span></li>
<li class="p4"><span class="s2">Clean Water</span></li>
<li class="p4"><span class="s2">Plant-rich, Nutrient-dense diet</span></li>
<li class="p4"><span class="s2">Exercise</span></li>
<li class="p4"><span class="s2">Adequate Rest</span></li>
<li class="p4"><span class="s2">Spiritual Outlook</span></li>
<li class="p4"><span class="s2">Positive Thinking</span></li>
</ul>
<p class="p3"><span class="s2">Of all the things you can do for your optimal health the two acts of simply consuming only the best clean water and breathing only pure fresh air are by far the most important things you can do for your body.</span></p>
<p class="p3"><strong>Article by Brian Hetrich</strong></p>
