		<title><![CDATA[A Deeper Understanding of Optimum Health]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/testimonials/a-deeper-understanding-of-optimum-health/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p><em>By Isabelle Calon</em></p>
<p>I had done some research in France to find a course to take me deeper into&nbsp; my understanding of what constitutes a plant based diet lifestyle. I wanted&nbsp; to discover its benefits and how can it be followed practically. The&nbsp; information available in France and in Europe was not sufficient. While&nbsp; researching, I came across The Hippocrates Wellness and things&nbsp; clicked. It was clearly the direction I wanted to take.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>Everything was organized and confirmed for me to take the autumn 2018&nbsp; course at the Institute in Florida but I suddenly had to change my plan&nbsp; when my Mother got extremely sick and was hospitalized.&nbsp; With Pam Blue, we re-scheduled for me to come a year later in 2019 but&nbsp; my visa to visit the United States was declined for some unknown reason.&nbsp; I then decided to take the online course. Finally, my dream came true…&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>Who am I and why choose Hippocrates Wellness?&nbsp;&nbsp;</strong></p>
<p>I was born in a tiny village in the Champagne region in France and was&nbsp; brought up on a self-sufficient farm. At 18, I left my family to travel and&nbsp; study philosophy while developing a real interest in food. I tried to find&nbsp; the connection between food, mind and health, a path which I have&nbsp; pursued since then.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>I was very lucky to have the opportunity to work in some of the UK’s most&nbsp; innovative kitchens and with their chefs, and these amazing experiences&nbsp; shaped my skills, especially creativity, in my cooking.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>I opened a locally beloved restaurant in the south of the French&nbsp; countryside and I am currently running a successful home catering business&nbsp; on the Côte d’Azur near Nice.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>Looking back, it is fascinating to see how my approach to food gradually&nbsp; became healthier, how willing I was to give my clients healthy dishes and&nbsp; how much I wished to give them information about my choice to use&nbsp; natural and organic ingredients. My ambition has been to feed people’s&nbsp; body and soul.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>I now specialize in vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free and raw food using only&nbsp; local and organic sources.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>I have also pursued studies of medicinal and edible plants and&nbsp; detoxification techniques with juices and raw food.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>My husband and I maintain and regularly use ingredients from our own&nbsp; garden where we practice permaculture and sustainable food production.&nbsp;</p>
<p>My journey lead me to the Hippocrates Wellness in pursuit of a&nbsp; deeper understanding of optimum health, and how to practice this way of&nbsp; life, and assimilate what a plant based diet means, as well as to combine&nbsp; the accumulated information into a coherent and intelligent form. I&nbsp; strongly felt that The Hippocrates Course was the perfect environment for&nbsp; me.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>How I found the transformation I was looking for in my life?&nbsp;&nbsp;</strong></p>
<p>The greatest challenge has been to alter my life’s habits and then embrace&nbsp; the changes. As Dr. Dossey says "If we do that, we will discover that the&nbsp; universe has a way of meeting us halfway."&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>Dietary transition requires courage, consistency and perseverance as says&nbsp; Brian Clement "Demons come out of you!"</p>
<p>Having my husband’s support was half of the journey.. It has been so&nbsp; exciting to share information with him. Together, we have introduced&nbsp; daily wheatgrass juice, juicing &amp; sprouting and a significant increase in&nbsp; eating raw and living food. We experiment with the benefits of the&nbsp; Hippocrates lifestyle together. What a joy! I think that this shows the&nbsp; importance of having support in making changes in our lives.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>The most striking change I have experienced while transitioning is my&nbsp; degree of vitality, particularly during the fasting periods. It feels to me&nbsp; that the fuel is distributed and regulated into my body much more&nbsp; efficiently. My blood sugar level has been more balanced, so no more&nbsp; peaks of insulin which used to make me feel tired and hungry all the time.&nbsp; Bringing back the life-force through sprouting, making it 30-50% more&nbsp; nutritious, has an extraordinary effect on the quality of my energy, be it&nbsp; physical or intellectual.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>Raw food triggers my sense of satiety preventing overeating. Snacking has&nbsp; disappeared and I can now make a clear different between real hunger and&nbsp; eating from habit.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>Here are the basic principles I have chosen to install in my daily lifestyle to&nbsp; optimize my health:&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Eat organic food : pesticides, herbicides, fungicides are a major threat&nbsp; to our health as we absorb these poisons which become a source of&nbsp; disease and the root cause for many illnesses such as cancer, neurological&nbsp; problems, inflammation, infertility, diminished immunity, Alzheimer’s…&nbsp; Moreover, they deplete and poison the life-giving earth, destroying living&nbsp; creatures and essential nutrients and vital minerals. Not only is this a&nbsp;</p>
<p>catastrophe for the equilibrium of nature, but the shortage of the&nbsp; earth’s microbiome diversity also leads to major health issues of&nbsp; nutritional deficiency, like thyroid imbalance due to the lack of selenium&nbsp; and iodine.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Eat local &amp; seasonal food : I am encouraging the local economy by buying&nbsp; straight from the local producers where the products are fresher, in&nbsp; season and more nutritious and the carbon footprint is lower.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Eliminate processed food and animal products : In doing so, one avoids&nbsp; sugar and salt in excess, chemical additives such as flavor enhancers,&nbsp; preservatives, GMO, antibiotics, growth hormones, heavy metals… and&nbsp; reduces one of the main root causes of inflammation and toxins.&nbsp; Processed food, dead food, cannot regenerate the cells of our body, being&nbsp; deprived of life and enzymes which are the very essence of life and&nbsp; regeneration.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Boost my intake of hormones, oxygen, phytochemicals &amp; enzymes : I have&nbsp; introduced wheatgrass &amp; green juices, mixed fresh sprouts as my main&nbsp; course, fermented food and of course lots of fresh raw vegetables&nbsp; instantly sourced from my garden. I now look for nutrients in my food&nbsp; intake rather than calories. If I give my body what it needs, it will&nbsp; naturally function well and maximize my quality of life.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Food combining : I have experienced the effects of improper food&nbsp; combining like difficult digestion, over acidity, fatigue, inflammation,&nbsp; flatulence… I find it difficult to apply perfect food combining but try to&nbsp; stay aware as much as I can.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Letting go of my addictions : The new lifestyle I have put into place&nbsp; meant that I had to let go of caffeine, of all refined flour, of sugar. It&nbsp; also meant to eat fruits within reason being in good health. Cooked food&nbsp; was an addiction too! Surprisingly, I find this easier as time go by. It is&nbsp; now occasionally, often in my social life, that I reach out for these&nbsp; substances. Stevia has been of great help!&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Install intermittent fasting : I eliminated breakfast in the morning and&nbsp; eat early at night, I fast for 18 hours daily. I also do longer fasts between&nbsp; seasons. It feels like a total reset of my body. It can clean, detoxify,&nbsp; eliminate and so optimize my digestion and assimilation. Fasting has&nbsp; been an amazing revelation to me, my mind is clearer and I feel so much&nbsp; better for it!&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Exercise : I have been exercising 5/6 days a week for many years. I&nbsp; alternate one day 40’ Cardio / 30’ weight, one day 20’ HIT / 30’&nbsp; trampoline. Stretching is also part of my daily session. I also go for walks&nbsp;</p>
<p>several times a week with friends from my community. I love walking&nbsp; with bare feet in nature. I do lots of gardening depending on the season.&nbsp; Exercising improves the health of the body, mind and soul. It oxygenates&nbsp; and activates stem-cells, activates my body fluids, invigorates my lymph&nbsp; system, encouraging sweating and cleansing. Weight lifting is also&nbsp; essential for my bone mass and strength and calcium assimilation.&nbsp; Exercise is the most efficient « medicine » to handle stress and emotions,&nbsp; to increase concentration and the brain’s ability to learn and perform, as&nbsp; well as the quality of sleep. It improves immunity and cardio-vascular&nbsp; function, and also slows down the release of stress related hormones. It&nbsp; is a powerful mood elevator and aids in regeneration of telomeres and&nbsp; helps with anti-aging. Life is by definition in constant movement, so to&nbsp; stay alive, one has to keep on moving. One cannot talk about health if&nbsp; one does do physical activity!&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Dry brushing : I have introduced this new habit before showering. It&nbsp; encourages the cleansing and elimination of chemicals, skin being a main&nbsp; emunctory.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Exposure to the sun : I am very lucky to live in the south of France where&nbsp; there is lots of sunshine, our number one immune builder. Vitamin D is&nbsp; critical for good health, it boosts immunity, and helps to assimilate&nbsp; calcium, boosts energy and elevates my mood.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Drink sufficient good quality water : this helps me to get the toxins out&nbsp; and hydrates my whole body. I have recently bought a Berkley water&nbsp; filter. I also energize the water I drink.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Quality of sleep : Sleep is a vital factor for good health. It should be&nbsp; restorative and seen as a medicine. Our body repairs and regenerates&nbsp; itself while we sleep. It is also very important in order to keep our&nbsp; immune system strong. I go to bed earlier and have installed a routine&nbsp; which helps me to unwire, get into and out of bed at the regular times,&nbsp; avoid spending time on the screen at night, eat early, drink calming&nbsp; tisanes.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Relaxation : Those are precious moment of the day when I can disconnect&nbsp; from the outside world in order to connect within myself. It is a time of&nbsp; gratitude and forgiveness when my intention is to bring peace and&nbsp; harmony in myself and in my environment.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Trust myself : During the course, I have learnt to listen to my body and&nbsp; trust myself. This means letting go of beliefs based on what I have been&nbsp; taught. Standing out of « I must, I must not » has been extremely&nbsp; liberating! My choices are now more based on my free will, on my own&nbsp;</p>
<p>conclusions and deductions. Being more in touch with my feelings has&nbsp; made my life so much more fluid and beautiful.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>On a more practical level, I had to re-think my food reserves, re-organize&nbsp; my kitchen space, and slightly change my daily schedule. I very quickly&nbsp; realized that planning is the secret for a successful plant based lifestyle.&nbsp; Soaking, planting, sprouting, dehydrating, all need anticipating. I have also&nbsp; learnt to anticipate my hunger!&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>During the course, some of my beliefs related to food naturally have&nbsp; changed. Brian Clement’s daily recommendation of 5% protein, 90%&nbsp; carbohydrates and 5% fat was revolutionary, especially having been cooking&nbsp; professionally for many years. Using proper sources of protein from green&nbsp; juices, wheatgrass, algae, sprouts and seeds has made a huge difference in&nbsp; my diet. I am now very much aware that organic does not mean healthy&nbsp; and clearly understand the difference between raw &amp; living food and how&nbsp; extraordinarily a plant-based diet optimizes -and regains health!&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>I have found that mind and body need to be in tune if we want truly to be&nbsp; healthy. It’s not enough to take care of my body. I need to care of my&nbsp; emotions. I need to take care of my mind.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>Being more aligned between my beliefs and my choices - i.e. building a&nbsp; bridge between my mind &amp; the physicality of the world - has granted me&nbsp; emotional serenity, as if things were falling into place. Having a tendency&nbsp; to hyper activity, I have noticed how much I have slowed down and how&nbsp; much calmer I feel. Giving myself this space has enriched my spiritual life&nbsp; enormously. It has allowed me to contemplate more and find wiser answers&nbsp; in these quiet moments. I have reached a tranquil place where it is hard&nbsp; to imagine my diet being any different and where living on a living food&nbsp; diet makes perfect sense!&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>The epoch we are living…&nbsp;&nbsp;</strong></p>
<p>The worldwide current crisis of the Covid illustrates perfectly how&nbsp; uneducated people are about their own health. It is much easier for people&nbsp; to be victims of the virus, find the cure outside themselves, and take zero&nbsp; responsibility for their own well-being.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>Each and everyone one of us is continually fighting disease in some form.&nbsp; As I am writing this essay, my body is filled with viruses, bacterias, mold,&nbsp; fungus and cancer cells. The difference between a person who falls victim&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>to disease and a person who does not, lies in the functioning of his/her&nbsp; immune system. Immunity goes beyond just food. We must understand the&nbsp; importance of a strong immune system, and what we can do to boost it.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Stress : We all have some degree of stress. Letting stress take over our&nbsp; lives has dramatic consequences on our health. Avoiding and resolving&nbsp;</p>
<p>stress is a key to becoming and staying well. Meditation is very helpful.&nbsp; Opening to some therapy work can be very useful, but takes courage.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Exercise : We cannot talk about good health without discussing physical&nbsp; activity. It is a sine qua non condition for an optimum health.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Find our passion : If we are to be in a position where we are going to be&nbsp; happy and healthy we must follow our passion. This starts with finding&nbsp; self-respect and being in touch with and loving what makes each one of&nbsp; us unique.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Educate ourselves : it is our responsibility to find and acquire the&nbsp; knowledge we need to look after ourselves. It is essential to experience&nbsp; for ourselves and make our own choices based on our feelings.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>Self-respect and self-love means taking care of ourselves. Eating unhealthy,&nbsp; processed, and highly polluted food often creates addictions (example: salt&nbsp; &amp; sugar). The people and corporations who produce this food design it this&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>way, so we then want more of something which is lethal for us but&nbsp; profitable for them. This life-style can slowly destroy our lives, lead us to&nbsp; depression, ruin our relationships, our ability to perform at work, our&nbsp; mental capacity as we age, and our fundamental enjoyment of life.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>Humanity is getting sicker and sicker. The increasing list of diseases of&nbsp; civilization and their consequences (diabetes, obesity, cancers, addictions,&nbsp; depression…) puts a tremendous burden on the world. The system is itself&nbsp; dysfunctional. Our native power for self-healing has been taken away from&nbsp; us. We have been brainwashed to seek solutions from outside ourselves in&nbsp; the form of magic pills, “vaccines, ” even surgery in the corporate pursuit&nbsp; of profit. We no longer have health care, we have sickness care.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>We need to educate people from an early age about nutrition, lifestyle,&nbsp; health , homeostasis etc … There are no shortcuts to good health. Each one&nbsp; of us has to take full responsibility for being well and healthy. People need&nbsp; to regain their power by looking at their illness as a condition which they&nbsp; participate in creating, and change the outcome because they are the co creators. Once they take charge, they can find their sovereignty again. We&nbsp; all have a capacity for self-healing, the body regulates itself constantly.&nbsp; We tend to look outside of ourselves for answers while all the keys lie&nbsp; within us. Our lifestyle and life choices keep us unaware, ignorant and&nbsp; unwell, or not…&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>I am the change I want to see in the world!&nbsp;</strong></p>
<p>Doing the online course has consolidated my determination to become a&nbsp; leader in promoting the benefits of a living food, plant-based diet for&nbsp; mankind : to reduce healthcare costs and to promote human health as&nbsp; mentioned , but also to end cruelty to animals and positively impact&nbsp; sustainable regenerative agriculture. Animals waste a lot of water&nbsp; polluting waters with tons of manure. A great percentage of the world’s&nbsp; food production goes to feeding animals, which is simply not sustainable.&nbsp; It is my responsibility to improve the health of the planet and preserving it&nbsp; for future generations!&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>Along with my vegan diet, which research now proves to be a necessity for&nbsp; the environmental sustainability of planet earth, here are necessary,&nbsp; practical and attainable steps which I try my best to put into action:&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Boycotting supermarkets, spend my money intelligently supporting small&nbsp; local businesses which share my views on food production and&nbsp; sustainability.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Minimizing environmental impact with a zero waste consciousness and&nbsp; avoiding packaged ingredients.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Making my own compost, feed the earth in my garden by creating rich&nbsp; compost, maintaining a worm farm, and building high quality dirt, so&nbsp; growing high quality vegetables and creating a world of abundance where&nbsp; surplus can be given away to my neighbors, and teaching them to do the&nbsp; same.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Aiming at self-sufficiency as much as I can by growing my own food&nbsp; (wheatgrass, sprouts, vegetables, vegetal milks, and fruits)&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Being involved in my community to open people’s awareness and teaching&nbsp; them about sustainability, and organizing activities which bring us&nbsp; together such as helping in the creation of other people’s gardens,&nbsp; teaching permaculture, harvesting fruits &amp; olives in each other’s gardens,&nbsp; discussion groups in the small associative café, delivering workshops,&nbsp; cooperative exchange of services…&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Modeling instead of telling my family, my friends and my environment&nbsp; what to do! This is the most powerful way to put a message across.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>Another key aspect of my self development is the art of communication. It&nbsp; is something I aim at perfecting each day. It has been a long journey and&nbsp; therapeutical work has helped me to go beyond the limits I was imposing&nbsp; on myself. The more my beliefs and actions are aligned, the more I am in&nbsp; touch with my deepest feelings, the more I love and respect myself exactly&nbsp;</p>
<p>the way I am, then the more authentic and transparent I can be in my&nbsp; communication with the outside world, the easier it is to build healthy&nbsp; relationships based on integrity and the more positively I can impact my&nbsp; environment for the common good. It takes courage to contradict&nbsp; mainstream media or popular misconceptions but it is a challenge I wish to&nbsp; take on.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>Time to roll up my sleeves. What can I do?&nbsp;&nbsp;</strong></p>
<p>The covid crisis has put my catering business on hold and I am taking&nbsp; this opportunity to work and re-invent my menus for the future with&nbsp; lots of new raw recipes. The course has been a fantastic source of&nbsp; inspiration, and has allowed me to pursue my passions. My goal is&nbsp; increasingly to present healthy living plant-based food to my clients. I&nbsp; live in France so this is a very daring project of mine! I love food and&nbsp; my job is to make it look and tastes delicious.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- In collaboration with a friend, I have organized an online course on&nbsp; dietary transition : how to change your diet and how to change your life?&nbsp; During the exchanges I had with the group of 9 people, I was solicited to&nbsp; discuss topics such as stress, addictions, weight loss, inflammation,&nbsp; microbiote … It was challenging but an exciting experience which we are&nbsp; planning to replicate in the next few weeks.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- I have connected with an hydrotherapy center, of which I am a big fan,&nbsp; and sharing very similar understandings of the importance of cleansing&nbsp; and detoxifying, we have decided to build a partnership where we&nbsp; promote each other services.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- I am also working in partnership with a local governmental union,&nbsp; promoting waste reduction and recycling. As part of the zero waste&nbsp; initiative, we follow households engaged in the process of reducing their&nbsp; waste production and leading people toward a healthier lifestyle.&nbsp; Together, we look at our daily habits, proposing alternatives to&nbsp; significantly reduce the amount of waste we produce. I have done hands on workshops on sprouting, fermented food and vegetal milk,&nbsp; familiarizing people with new and easy ways of preparing their food&nbsp; more sustainable for the planet.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Hosting my family and my friends at home is a wonderful opportunity&nbsp; for them to open their taste buds to new flavors and foods. It often is a&nbsp; revelation to them how plant based food can actually be delicious and&nbsp; pleasurable. Many members of my family and friends are now juicing,&nbsp; sprouting and slowly considering a healthier approach to their diet.&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Another initiative I have taken in my village is to invite people once a&nbsp; month into my small kitchen where we prepare a vegan meal which we&nbsp; then share together. Food is such a great way of connecting with people!&nbsp; Generally speaking, I find that people are eager to learn new ways of&nbsp; preparing and eating and are waking up to the parallel between their&nbsp; diet and their health.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>- Practicing permaculture is an important part of life which I share with&nbsp; my husband. Today’s world is desperately in need of this philosophy of&nbsp; life : care for the earth, care for people and redistribute the surplus. We&nbsp; have initiated and accompanied some of our friends in their garden&nbsp; development projects, who are themselves now propagating the idea of a&nbsp; more sustainable lifestyle.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>I am never short of ideas as to how to reach people positively, engaging in&nbsp; sharing information about the Hippocrates lifestyle. It is a never ending&nbsp; journey as there is a continual learning which must take place. Being so&nbsp; passionate about it, it feels that my professional and my private life are&nbsp; becoming one!&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>Each one of us can control our health destiny&nbsp;&nbsp;</strong></p>
<p>Humans have deviated from nature’s intended order. This is a sad situation&nbsp; where there is a huge gap between the reality we created and our&nbsp; aspirations. Self-justification has opened the door to defeat. Humanity has&nbsp; somehow gotten lost and is slowly committing suicide by not taking any&nbsp; responsibility for the inverted sick world we live in. We are not supposed&nbsp; to be obese with diabetes or to have cancer… We forgot that death is a&nbsp; normal process of life. Discerning the true nature of the current situation&nbsp; is essential to envisaging a better tomorrow. We must not remain passive.&nbsp; There are thousands of ways to reverse the trend. It is up to each one of&nbsp; us. Nutritional advances have taken place in recent years now that we have&nbsp; scientific support and convincing evidence.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>The Hippocrates online course has sparked something joyous in my heart. It&nbsp; feels like I am part of a network of people from all over the world&nbsp; contributing to the best of our abilities in order to create healthier&nbsp; societies. Within the Hippocrates community, I can find the strength to&nbsp; face resistance and thus find greater fulfillment. We have to heal&nbsp; individually and collectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>The thread of the tremendous amount of information I have received and&nbsp; what has touched me personally the most in this course is that diet and&nbsp; lifestyle reflect feelings of self-love and self-respect. Equilibrium seems to&nbsp; be key to live my best life. Balance is to be found in each breath, it is a&nbsp; never ending voyage. I have learned to be less extreme and realized how&nbsp; much I was missing in life. The physical, emotional, intellectual and&nbsp;</p>
<p>spiritual worlds all need to be explored, experimented and integrated in&nbsp; an intelligent form for their true purposes. That means tapping into my&nbsp; higher self to create what seems to be the best life for myself and my&nbsp; fellow human being.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>

		<title><![CDATA[You, Family, and Friends]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/you-family-and-friends/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p>by Brian Clement, PhD, LN</p>
<p>When a mother speaks about her children and a father spills over with pride for his offspring, it is the natural state of human biology. Although we believe we are here for numerous purposes, our true calling is quite simple: procreation. Our minds, emotions and internal drive are all fueled by the desire to perpetuate our species. From the time of birth until the day we die, hormones govern the core of our thoughts and emotions. Layers of deception confuse the purpose of our actions, yet, the foundation is most often the drive to create. During the last two centuries, technology, beginning with light and then media, radio and television threw the natural balance of family, community and humanity into a tailspin. Furthering our estrangement from our natural state are computers, cellphones and the related cyber information age. Walking down any street in the world today, there is no doubt that most people spend most of their time looking at a miniature screen that they hold in their hand. This, of course, robs our precious time to interact with those we love. Youth entering college today have so little experience in communication, some of the better schools literally have freshman training to teach students how to relate to something other than a machine.</p>
<p>Our modern lifestyle has driven a giant wedge between our biological purpose and our daily existence. It is not hard to understand why 40% of married couples in the developed world struggle to have babies. How far this may go is actually up to us to determine. There is nothing more powerful than personal relationships with those you love. The nuclear family is the basis for civilization, and without its strong presence, we are eroding the potential for a civil, compassionate and prosperous humanity.</p>
<p><img class="mb-15 mb-lg-20" src="/wp-content/uploads/2015/12/iStock_000068421201_Large.jpg" alt=""></p>
<p>When evaluating sociological and psychological data, it always presents a clear picture that what we all aspire for is love and the support and caring that it offers. When the significant majority, expressed this very fact (when questioned) but somehow do not prioritize it, it creates an emotional schism in their reality. “Find oneself” seems to be a universal quest in the minds of people. Yet, is it not oneself that is derived from the guidance, strength and authenticity of a supportive family. Whenever superstars are interviewed, the story of their success has one consistent thread that is always there. The mother, the father, the teacher, the coach, the friend who relentlessly pushed, supported and insisted on furthering the passion of the star. We are not solo acts, and we are wired to be interdependent, not without need of touch and caring.</p>
<p>How then do we get back to the basics without dropping out and becoming an island unto ourselves? Values are the answer. Are your values only to make money and acquire material rewards or are they to share life with those you care for? As simple as this question is, it definitively describes the profound query that needs to be immediately answered.</p>
<p>We all seem to be able to schedule the busyness of our work life, but somehow neglect to schedule time with our partners, children, family and friends. Remedying this distortion is the first step in supporting your own happiness and that of those you love. Excuses reign; yet family cries out for attention. Some of you may be suffering from a truly dysfunctional experience you had starting with your parents and siblings which most often is carried into your married life. What we learn is what we attract. So you may be asking if my memory of family is skewed, how then I can embrace something that I have no attraction to. In fact, you do have a deep emotional and biological desire to acquire the security and strength from the family, you just are frightened to take the necessary steps in doing it right this time. Years ago, a friend who taught psychology at an Ivy League school told me to guide people in the process of accepting themselves and resolving their family history by realizing that it was all that their parents and others were capable of. As he stated, “if they didn’t know how to love you, you have to learn how to love yourself.” Once you are brave enough to break the bonds of self-imposed sabotage by raising your value with self-respect, you will inherently attract likeminded people into your life. As you know, happy people attract happy; sad attracts sad.</p>
<blockquote>Loving oneself provides the possibility of emotionally stable choices. This naturally guides us into picking our partners based upon compatibility, not just sexuality. Although intimacy is powerfully important in partnerships, it cannot be the forceful factor that many of us make it in our youth. True friendships are sexier than good sex, and by the way, they can last forever. Loving partners spawn secure balanced and loving children. Here in the United States, the latest statistics are grim. We are at the highest level ever of single people in our adult population. Ironically, when you really get down to it, every one of these people would love to have a happy, enriching and rewarding relationship.</blockquote>
<p>Erickson so wisely spoke of the phases of life; pictorially it is almost like watching a flower open. As time passes and experience mounts, your needs, desires, and fulfillment evolve. Choosing the right mate will expansively support a much larger and productive life for both. Nature did not create single parent homes or lonely people; it is our lost and valueless culture that manifests this mess. Once again, we must establish what is truly important to us. Of course, we all aspire to have economic security, a clean, safe and comfortable place to reside and adequate food, etc. This cannot be our only quest, and in fact, when you look at this closely, these are only practical requirements so we can now begin to have a life. If and when your life is all about survival, you will never have enough money or size of residence or clothes or cars, etc. Without fail, you will learn that creature comforts are only a façade and not our essential desire. When having a choice between being loved and being rich, 88% of the people correctly chose love. Now there is nothing wrong with being loved and rich, yet that should come without effort not as your core value.</p>
<p>When Anna Maria and I speak on our early morning walks, we often comment how fortunate we are to have parents that truly love us. Were either of our lives Cinderella like, flawless adventures with perfect parents and siblings? No. Yet, the overriding sense of how we received our strength and faculty to persevere came from the loving guidance from our family. We in fact learned to be the parents of four, and now grandparents of four, from our nuclear family. How often it is that we meet in our work on the front lines of disease and disorder, broken and ill people who have not resolved their dysfunctional childhood resulting from a disenfranchised family structure. Are the experiences from our youth creating our health today? With a resounding YES, we are unwavering in our understanding of this fact.</p>
<blockquote>Become the person you wish you had been when nurtured as a child. Work hard with advancement and psychotherapy and be candid and transparent with close friends and family members so they can help piece together what you currently perceive as a fragile life. Once you have established the mantle for the future, deeply enlist yourself via visualization and commitment to creating a pure and desirable future. There is never a too late and always an opportunity for change and joy.</blockquote>
<p>On a lecture tour to Western Canada, I met an alumnus who had reversed cardiovascular disease, diabetes and high blood pressure. She had been single her whole life and had just met the man of her dreams at 83. When standing next to them and observing their unadulterated love, it was reminiscent of Romeo and Juliet. For the first time, I saw her eyes sparkle, her lips pucker and her appearance and dress to be impeccable. Nearly 81 ⁄2 decades after she was born, she made her dream come true. When will you make your dream come true? Is it not time that you find a way to elevate your psychological, emotional and spiritual status to a place whereas you magnetize a like-minded friend. When this holy relationship begins in your youth, you have the ability to produce sound and contributory human beings. As we age, we can feel the solace of having a collaborator, a caretaker and a colleague at our side until the candle goes out. We must never forget that the level of happiness that we acquire is quietly and visibly expressed into the universe which enhances the lives of others and all of nature that we share this beautiful planet with.</p>

		<title><![CDATA[Energy: the Regenerative Medicine of the Future]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/health/energy-the-regenerative-medicine-of-the-future/</link>

		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p><strong>By Augusta Malacarne</strong></p>
<p>Coordinator, Energy Medicine Department at Hippocrates Wellness</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>What if there was a treatment that had no side effects? And that relieved pain, strengthened the immune system, encouraged antiaging and activated the body to fight disease? A treatment that cost only the electricity used during that treatment from your home’s wall socket?</p>
<p>Sound incredible?</p>
<p>Big Pharma’s remedies treat symptoms chemically, stimulating biological activity, which in turn activate electrical magnetic activity, stimulating the body’s cells to heal, or at least to relieve the symptoms. Energy Medicine showers the body with electromagnetic vibrations which directly stimulate the cells of the body to activate healing. It is not surprising, then, that users experience results faster and stronger than those from more expensive biochemical treatments. And without side effects. Energy Medicine is a new science but it has its roots in over a hundred years of international research activity. Since, really, the discovery of electricity itself. And, as with many scientific breakthroughs it has endured the ritual of skepticism, ridicule and resistance until it has finally achieved its present prestige as the promising future of medicine. Even when electricity was discovered: when Ben Franklin linked it to lightning, Faraday captured it in a jar in 1831 and a Vermont blacksmith, Thomas Davenport produced a road-worthy electric car in 1835, few could imagine whole cities illuminated with alternating current. It was not until Nikola Tesla unveiled that possibility at the Chicago Exposition of 1893.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>And still, today, physicians have difficulty approaching a patient as an electromagnetic center. Even though, routinely they utilize CAT scans, EKGs, MRIs and X-rays for diagnosis. But not for treatment. Even though, the communications between the cells of the body are fundamentally electric. The western mind has difficulty believing something without understanding the science or the mechanism that drives it. Faith is for religion, not medicine. But now, technology has verified that it is electric impulses which make the body work. Skepticism is eliminated for those who enquire.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>The Mayo clinic does use Energy Medicine (EM) for some diagnoses. Dr. Oz in November 2011 on his television show, The Revolutionary Cure for Pain, featured a Pulsed Electromagnetic Field (PEMF) instrument. Now, the NBA, the Olympics, the Vatican Hospital and the Russian health care system employ PEMF devices as curatives. NASA used PEMF devices on MIR astronauts to ward off muscle loss during long confinements.</p>
<p>Celebrities had already begun to experiment with other technologies and word of mouth alerted sufferers to this breakthrough science. Princess Diana, Sarah Ferguson, the former Duchess of York, Hollywood’s Nick Nolte, model Elle McPherson and Lady Gaga have all experienced a form of Energy Medicine. Now ,even someone like the former US Assistant Secretary of Housing and Urban Development, who authors the Solari Report, documenting the concerns about 5G, Catherine Austin Fitts, is a regular user of QRS (Quantum Resonance Systems) in her home. It’s almost mainstream!</p>
<p>The QRS device increases the energy of all cells of the body and reduces electro smog, mitigating the negative effects of EMF exposure and 5G emissions. Treatments reduce inflammation, stress and calcification. QRS has demonstrated positive results for over 200 maladies. The user simply reclines on a soft mat connected to a frequency generator. The QRS emissions then bathe the body with gentle electromagnetic pulses, calibrated to the cells’ natural voltage. Sessions vary from 8 to 20 minutes in duration and can be repeated up to three times a day. Selected accessories like the QRS Glasses and Headphones are designed to support vision and hearing as well as neurological needs.</p>
<p>Another innovative technology available at the Hippocrates Wellness is coMra therapy (Coherent Multi Radiances). This therapy combines pulsation of ultrasound, LED lights, magnets and low laser to reduce inflammation at the cellular level to regenerate tissues. By supporting the mitochondria supply of energy to the cells, the synergistic workings of the multiple radiances increase ATP (Adenosine triphosate), the energy in the body. By employing multiple radiances the coMra therapy device can reach organs and tissues very deeply and reduce inflammation in hard to reach areas.</p>
<p>A compact, affordable version of this device is available for home use as is the portable version of QRS.</p>
<p>In addition to the remarkable results of PEMF therapy, (more than 40,000 studies exist on the subject), new reports continually emerge which demonstrate even more positive benefits of radionics. A recent comparison of PEMF therapy and circuit weight training on bone mineral density in elderly women produced a surprising result. The effortless</p>
<p>application of PEMF therapy resulted in 30% more bone mineral density and content than pumping iron. Good news for combating osteoporosis!</p>
<p>Professor Eftrati, at the Tel Aviv University said the following about their Energy Medicine research, “For many years our team has engaged in Hyperbaric research and therapy based on exposure to high pressure oxygen concentration (HBOT). Our achievements included improvement of brain functions damaged by age, stroke or brain injury. ” And, “Today telomere shortening is considered the Holy Grail of biology of aging, researchers are trying to develop a pharmacological and environment intervention that enable telomere elongation. Our HBOT protocol was able to achieve that, proving that the aging process can be reversed at the basic cellular level”.</p>
<p>The telomeres are the gate keepers to our DNA. They act as the end caps of a chromosome that protect genetic contents from deteriorating. The decline in telomere length causes cells to eventually stop dividing which explains why older people become weaker and more susceptible to illness.</p>
<p>These breakthroughs suggest that Energy Medicine is the medicine of the future. And it’s available now. The salutary relief from stress, fatigue and pain are an affordable alternative to allopathic treatment. In addition, reports of curative results, over a wide range of maladies are encouraging. As a companion to a healthy life style, plant based nutrition and regular exercise, Energy Medicine is a welcome addition. What was once termed “a mysterious fluid force”, electromagnetic frequency and other radiances will soon become household words. What once was mystical is now proven practical. As Ralph Waldo Emerson said, “In all animal and vegetable forms, the physiologist concedes that no chemistry, no mechanics can account for the facts, but a mysterious principle of life must be assumed which not only inhabits an organ, but makes the organ.”</p>
<p>With regard to health and healing it’s good to keep an open mind!</p>

		<title><![CDATA[What Type of Water Should I Consume?]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/wellbeing/what-type-of-water-should-i-consume/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p>Your body is 70% water. Your brain is 80% water, even your bones are 20% water.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Every cell in your body contains water and floats in water. Water transports nutrients to each cell and delivers these nutrients through cell membranes, while simultaneously removing the toxins that every cell creates. These toxins are then delivered to your kidneys and expelled from the body. Water delivers oxygen to each cell via red blood cells (which are mostly water) and removes carbon dioxide, which is then transported to the lungs to be expelled.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Water is required for every bodily function: breathing, digestion, growth, movement, elimination of waste, heat dissipation, metabolism, secretion and all glandular functions. Water is the basis for all chemical reactions and all electrical signals. It cools. It lubricates.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Water is the basis for life itself.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>It’s vital that you not only consume enough water, but you should only consume the best water. This brings up the question, “What is the best type of water to consume?”</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>There is a lot of misinformation about what is the best type of water to consume, so we want to set the record straight.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>FIRST, WHAT IS WATER?</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Water is a molecule with two atoms of hydrogen and one atom of oxygen, often referred to as H2O. To be specific though, liquid water is not actually H2O, but rather it forms long strings of H2O molecules grouped together. Water only becomes H2O when it evaporates and becomes a vapor (you will soon see that this is a very important point).</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Water has remarkable properties that make it essential for all life on this planet, such as the fact that it is lighter when it freezes solid. This means that ice floats, so bodies of water rarely freeze solid, which is why fish are able to survive in subzero temperatures.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>But another aspect of water is even more fascinating, and that is called the hydrologic cycle. As you know, most water on Earth is in the oceans, which contain very salty water. So where does fresh (non-salty) water come from? Interestingly enough, it starts in the oceans. Here’s how it works…</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>The Sun provides heat to the oceans, which causes the water to evaporate. When water evaporates it becomes pure H2O, and it leaves all of the contaminants behind in the ocean. The pure water vapor rises, and then condenses into clouds. When conditions are right, the water in the clouds precipitate into drops of water and then fall to the Earth. Rainwater, as long as there is no air pollution, is high purity water.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>This is the source of all fresh water on the planet, from lakes, streams, rivers and even underground aquifers. This is why you and I are alive today.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>This process is actually water’s built-in water purification process: evaporation, condensation and precipitation.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>SO, WHAT TYPE OF WATER SHOULD WE CONSUME?</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>To answer this question, we have to look at the type of water humans evolved to drink. Humans, like most animals, drank rainwater directly or they drank recently fallen rainwater from streams (the fresher the better). This was high purity water.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Humans did not drink water that contained any modern-day chemicals, pharmaceuticals or refined metals. The chemicals we are surrounded by today have only been in our environment for the past 150 years or so.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Nor did humans often drink ground water, which is typically high in minerals. Europeans only started drinking mineralized ground water after they formed communities, which had poor sanitation. Ground water proved to be safer than the bacteria ridden streams and rivers, but this is not what humans were meant to drink.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>So, the answer to the question, “What type of water should I consume?” is very simple: you should consume the purest water possible. It is very important that you should drink the purest water available, because any impurity puts stress on your body.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>The fact is, we live in a very toxic world, and these toxins have been linked to countless illnesses. The majority of toxins have unknown effects on our bodies, but the effects are clearly significant and worse than modern medical science acknowledges.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Let’s look at some different examples…</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Tap Water: As was demonstrated in Flint, Michigan, tap water can contain high levels of dangerous contaminants without your knowledge. A month after lead was found in Flint, an independent investigation showed that over 2,000 other water systems across all 50 States also had high levels of lead in the water. And this is just one toxin out of the 100,000 possible toxins.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Mineral Water: Humans were not meant to drink mineral water. The minerals in water are not in a usable form for humans. These minerals can build up in your body and are just one more contaminant that your body has to get rid of.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Alkaline Water: To alkalize water, you have to start with contaminated water. Pure water naturally has a neutral pH and cannot be alkalized. Alkalized water should not be consumed.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Filtered Water: Filters (including reverse osmosis) are typically better than just drinking tap water, but they produce variable results so you can’t count on them and the purity of water they produce declines over time, thus requiring “filter changes”</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Distilled Water: The purest form of water available is distilled water, which is why freshly distilled water is the best type of water to drink. The distillation process mimics nature’s hydrologic cycle of evaporation, condensation and precipitation. In other words, distillation uses water’s built-in purification process to purify water.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Brian Clement has used a water distiller for 50 years to produce the highest purity drinking water for his family. He credits his distiller with playing a key role in protecting his family’s health over the years and he says that his Pure Water distiller was one of the best investments he has ever made.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>The brand of distiller that Brian purchased decades ago was called a “Pure Water” distiller. This is a USA-based company that is still producing US-made, high quality water distillers. Pure Water and Hippocrates partnered up to offer a special price for the Hippocrates audience.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>Learn more at <a href="http://www.HippocratesWater.org">www.HippocratesWater.org</a></p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>If you want to take a significant step towards health and vitality, we recommend investing in a Pure Water Distiller.</p>

		<title><![CDATA[Wheatgrass a Breath of Fresh Greens]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/archive/wheatgrass-a-breath-of-fresh-greens/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p>Go green, be green, eat green, live green, drink green.</p>
<p>Clearly, we are in the midst of an unprecedented planetary trend. For many this is a ground-breaking idea, but at its core “green” means living simply and naturally. “Green” encompasses all of planet Earth’s true superfoods: on the ground in the form of vegetation, in the oceans in the form of sea vegetables and in fresh water in the form of algae. These foods help us reconnect to Earth, listen to nature’s wisdom, and allow our bodies to heal. Feel free to watch the movie “Avatar” again for this simple and powerful message. It’s time to become healthy again by tapping into the basic yet profound awareness of our instincts.</p>
<p>The foundation of Hippocrates Wellness, and, in the larger perspective of planet Earth, is the greens: wheatgrass, sunflower, pea greens, sprouts, leafy greens, algae, seaweed and all the wonderful green life surrounding our 55 acre campus.</p>
<p>Everyone knows humans are mammals. The majority of the mammals on this planet consume a diet of grass and/or leafy greens. In fact, humans are one of the few mammals that still eat meat, and the only mammal that actually cooks its food. To say that protein only comes from eating meat is an uninformed statement. In truth, sprouted beans, nuts, seeds, algae, grains, grass and greens are the best source of digestible proteins for our bodies. Have you ever stopped to think, “Where does the ‘meat’ get its protein?” Think about it on a bigger scale. How is it possible that approximately 85% of mammals can thrive solely on leafy greens? Elk, moose, deer, giraffes, gorillas, elephants, horses…and don’t forget the mammal from which we Westerners get most of our food…the cow!</p>
<p>In the past, when you lived on red meat and dairy products, indirectly, you lived on GRASS! There is the “green” word we need back in our lives. The cow was eating the grass; we were eating the cow. We were absorbing Earth’s nutrients in our diets second hand through the animal. Today cows are shot full of antibiotics, steroids, and hormones, only perpetuating the health detracting effects of eating twice removed nutrients.</p>
<p>We are no longer getting the grass (green/earth) in our diets!</p>
<p>This nutritional tragedy is compounded by the fact that most greens are complete foods, and they produce the body’s most vital fuel, oxygen…The first thing your body needs to live, before food and water, is oxygen! Let’s face it, the only people that really focus on breath these days, unless you’re into yoga, tai chi, or meditation, are smokers! What exactly are you doing when you smoke? You’re breathing deeply. I am not encouraging smoking, however, I am encouraging breathing. Try it without the “stick.” Walk away from people, your job, etc…go somewhere, by yourself, and spend five minutes breathing deeply. You’ll be amazed at how much calmer you feel after doing this.</p>
<p>Let’s review how wheatgrass and greens came to light. Ann Wigmore founded the first Hippocrates in Boston approximately 65 years ago. She actually healed her health issues by chewing, and chewing, and chewing on lawn grass. Lawn grass…not wheatgrass. She was chewing on it and spitting out the fibers. Ann was still sick for many weeks, but stayed with it until she eventually started feeling better. This journey began by observing animals chew on grass. She was also influenced to experiment with grasses because of the following statement that was made to her as a child: “Instinct guided creatures, left to themselves, do not make mistakes.” Most of us chewed on grass or weeds as children, when it was around. Why then, and not now? Did we, as children, understand more about our vital connection to the Earth? Yes! Unfortunately, most of us have since lost sight of our instincts.</p>
<p>Ann learned that grasses are not only one of the most complete foods on the planet, but that they also possess healing properties. Of all the grass seeds, wheat emerged triumphantly because of its sweeter, more palatable taste. Her cat chose it.</p>
<p>Ann also learned that chlorophyll (the Mother of every green food) can increase hemoglobin (blood) quality, which means more efficient istribution of oxygen to every cell in our bodies.</p>
<p>Oxygen content on the planet in the 21st century has decreased. 100 years ago, there was a much higher concentration of oxygen in the air. The most oxygen out there these days, if you live in a lush, green area, is around 20%. However, in downtown major cities it is much lower. Does anyone remember “smog alerts?” I do, but not since 1990, when they stopped telling people what is really going on out there. Fact: Oxygen in the cells means less chance for cancer or even a virus, to survive. From greens we get chlorophyll, which increases hemoglobin and thus creates more oxygen in our cells.</p>
<p>Consuming greens, fresh wheatgrass juice, green sprouts, and green juices, allows your body to take care of itself. In addition, we can support internal cleansing through alkalizing, detoxifying, carrying life to the cells with oxygen, nutrients and life. Fresh wheatgrass juice alone can help replace many of your morning time supplements. The foundation of your diet and your life should be greens. Consuming fresh living greens keeps us in touch with the vibrational life force that begins with the sun’s energy radiating to Earth giving life to greens. Be conscious of your choices and understand that food is a crucial choice.</p>
<p>Get the Earth back in your life. Your cells crave clean oxygen. Get back in touch with the planet by growing your own greens: be it a garden, sprouts in your kitchen, or wheatgrass trays in your city apartment. It starts with you. “What’s simple is true.” No more waiting until tomorrow. Do it now! Live vibrantly. Love deeply. Listen to your heart as it has a lot to say. Your heart contains more answers than your head! Take a deep breath. It’s all about the greens!</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>

		<title><![CDATA[Top Wellness Trends for 2021]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/wellbeing/top-wellness-trends-for-2021/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <h2>CIRCADIAN HEALTH</h2>
<p><br>We’ve never been so sleep-obsessed. We pony up for sleep-tracking, Oura rings, the latest, smartest mattresses, and meditative sleep headbands; crawl into nap pods; and travel far to bed down at sleep retreats. We gobble sleep tonics, CBD and even “sleep ice cream.” We’ve been hit by a storm of generic sleep products, driving a $432 billion “sleep economy,”* and we’re still not sleeping. Why? Because most sleep solutions, and our modern lives, defy the basic facts of circadian biology. Circadian medicine is moving fast. In a few years, it’s likely that a single blood, saliva or breath sample will be able to pinpoint our precise circadian clock-state, and apps could then inform us when to take in light and dark, sleep and rise, and eat and exercise. We expect some circadian market mayhem ahead (very bright and dim ideas). But the right timing of light and biology will move closer to the heart of wellness. Finally.</p>
<h2>AGING REBRANDED: POSITIVELY COOL</h2>
<p>Baby boomers redefined aging, and now the market is finally catching up to them. Unlike previous generations, today’s 55+ are anything but boring; they’re active, vivacious, and far more engaged in exciting endeavors. Today’s retirees start businesses, run marathons, and travel widely. They own motorcycles and increasingly scoop up hip downtown condos. The World Health Organization predicts the 60+ population will nearly double by 2050 from 12 percent to 22 percent. Companies are wising up. Across the spectrum, from beauty to food, brands now cater to <br>this long-ignored group. They’re finally answering boomers’ call: Why shouldn’t they receive the same cool content and products as millennials? We’re just at the tip of the iceberg. Industry analysts predict that more conglomerates will invest resources in the senior market, adding new products and experiences that attest to the boomers’ vibrancy. They’re living longer and healthier, and the market can no longer afford to ignore them.</p>
<h2>J-WELLNESS</h2>
<p>Japan is the longevity nation: It has more centenarians per capita than any country on Earth. It’s a result of Japan’s unique culture of wellness, which unites ancient healing traditions with ingenious people-focused tech/design and innovative social policy. In the last few years, various Japanese wellness approaches became global trends: “Ikigai,” the lifelong pursuit of finding your true purpose; the spiritual value of minimalism and auditing our possessions, forest bathing (Shinrin-Yoku), meditative movement through the forest; and Wabi-sabi, the philosophy of embracing imperfection and transience. But these trends have been consumed piecemeal, and Japan is distinctly humble about its rich wellness assets. We think that will change: “J-Wellness” will increasingly be embraced as a holistic culture of wellbeing—from its innovations for our ageing world to the breakthroughs in J-Beauty to a reverence for nature and meditative ritual as preventative healthcare.</p>
<h2>MENTAL WELLNESS AND TECHNOLOGY: RETHINKING THE RELATIONSHIP</h2>
<p>Awareness of the need to address mental health has grown significantly in the last few years. A broad category, this includes mental illness and neurological disorders but also new categories spanning anxiety, stress and despair. Issues such as climate change-induced anxiety and work-induced stress are commonplace. Last year, the World Health Organization declared “burnout” an official medical diagnosis. As such, both the public and private sectors increasingly look to advance solutions at scale. Silicon Valley, for example, released an impressive array of digital solutions to ensure more individuals receive discreet and flexible care. Nearly 10,000 mental health apps currently crowd the market, ranging from behavioral health coaching to meditation content. Mental Health Tech will be going mainstream- Affordable virtual therapy apps such as TalkSpace give patients the ability to call, text and video teleconference with professional counselors on their schedule, whereas chatbots serve as a listening friend on-demand.</p>
<h2>ENERGY MEDICINE GETS SERIOUS</h2>
<p>In medicine, electrifying new insights will keep coming around bioelectricity, the “organized lightning” that our cells use to grow and communicate. Michael Levin at Harvard’s Wyss Institute is just one top scientist uncovering the bioelectric “language” that cells use to coordinate everything from their own regeneration to cancer suppression. Biophotons are the light particles radiating from our cells that help regulate our biological systems—and the emerging field of Biophotonics will use coherent light (lasers, lighted crystals) to positively impact tissues and organs. New “optogenetic” tools are exciting neurons using light, allowing them to map the brain’s connections and activate brain circuits.</p>
<h2>ORGANIZED RELIGION JUMPS INTO WELLNESS</h2>
<p>If going to church once meant dolling up in a dress to sit in a pew, today it might look more like wearing leggings for a HIIT-infused sermon. More and more, faith is incorporating the latest wellness trends, signifying a shift away from viewing bodywork as vanity.&nbsp; With interest in health and fitness at an all-time high, organized religion is reimagining age-old rituals and formats. For some churches, synagogues and mosques, this adoption simply reflects a desire to feel better and to take preventative health measures. Congregations no longer want to separate their physical and spiritual needs but instead, hope to fuse them together in novel new ways. This ranges from aerobic fitness classes to meditative retreats, all reworked with religious liturgy and biblical references. There are now boutique fitness studios solely devoted to worship or which cater to religious constraints. We see Ramadan bootcamps, Jewish Sabbath service hikes, Christian wellness retreats, Catholic Pilates classes and Muslim fitness YouTube channels.</p>
<h2>THE WELLNESS SABBATICAL</h2>
<p>The current vacation model: work like mad and take a week of vacation where you’re supposed to totally switch off. A great model, but one that doesn’t work for many people anymore. As work has become “always-on,” more people aren’t taking their vacation days, and vastly more people are remote/independent workers with no formal vacation time. The reality: More people desperately need a profound wellness break, but they need to keep working. Shaming them for not taking vacations—or not totally unplugging when they do—feels naive. Enter a new travel concept: the wellness sabbatical, where days of work and wellness are intentionally blended, at destinations that actively, creatively make this possible. On a wellness sabbatical, you’re set up to work a few productive hours a day (great workspaces, technology), but you also schedule a lot of daily wellness experiences (healthy food, movement, time in nature, sleep, human connection, etc.). And repeat, hopefully for a minimum of three weeks, that sweet spot to jumpstart lasting lifestyle changes and for a true mental reset. Work + Wellness is the future.</p>
<h2>THE FERTILITY BOOM</h2>
<p>Fertility is no longer a taboo topic hushed about in doctor’s offices. The last few years saw incredible progress in this space on multiple fronts. These advancements couldn’t come sooner: Fertility has reached a crisis point across the globe. Highly industrialized countries such as England, Japan and the US continue to see record-low fertility rates, which will ultimately impact the future of the workforce. The landscape is filled with apps, period trackers, platforms, and wearables that not only increase one’s chances of conceiving but even attempt to make it, well, enjoyable. So far, women’s health start-ups are believed to have secured over $1 billion in investment, and of that, 60 percent is focused on fertility or pregnancy. It’s just the start of what many see as a femtech revolution.</p>
<h2>WELLNESS MUSIC</h2>
<p>We all self-medicate through music, but most people don’t grasp just how powerful the medical evidence for music therapy is: Humans are hardwired for music; no other stimulus positively activates so many brain regions; and stringent studies show its dramatic impact on mood, anxiety and pain. If formal “music therapy” has always seemed a tad dowdy, now, suddenly, something big is happening. Music as an intentional therapy is being radically reinvented by new technologies. Music is emerging as one of the hottest trends in wellness, and wellness concepts are shaking up the massive music industry.&nbsp;Meditation apps are morphing into wellness music apps. New player Wave foregos the old whispery, guided meditations for an all-wellness-music platform that, combined with its pulse-vibrating bolster, delivers multi-frequency meditation.</p>
<h2>IN WELLNESS WE TRUST: THE SCIENCE BEHIND THE INDUSTRY</h2>
<p>Wellness is by nature a consumer industry: It evolved to supplement what traditional medicine hasn’t tackled well, whether prevention, lifestyle change or mental wellness. But because it’s a hyper-consumer, largely unregulated, $4.5 trillion market, there’s been a storm of baseless claims about pseudo-scientific products and Instagram and celeb “wellness influencers” for hire. It’s one thing when a wellness approach has little benefit but does no harm—but when a “flat tummy tea” loaded with laxatives does real harm, the situation is serious. We’ll see more online call-out platforms, such as Instagram collective Estée Laundry, which goes after the false claims of influencers and brands in the beauty industry. (Online platforms that take on the wider wellness space are likely ahead.) We’ll see more vetting and certification sites such as UK-based WellSpoken, whose content tries to counter wellness pseudoscience and certifies brands. WellSet is trying to take on questionable wellness practices with a marketplace where people can find reputable local specialists.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>BY GLOBAL WELLNESS INSTITUTE</p>

		<title><![CDATA[7 Steps to Slow Aging]]></title>
		<link>https://hippocrateswellness.clickysoft.us/learning-centre/blog/wellbeing/7-steps-to-slow-aging/</link>
		<pubDate></pubDate>
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[]]></dc:creator>
		<guid isPermaLink="false"></guid>
		<description></description>
		<content:encoded><![CDATA[
            <p>WHAT IS AGING?</p>
<p><br>Aging, defined simply, is the process of getting older with time. Biologically, it is the inevitable deterioration of physiological functions that are otherwise necessary for survival and fertility. Our cells, the basic building blocks of the body, undergo natural wear and tear but employ intrinsic means, such as autophagy, to repair themselves. However, when we age, the cells begin to break down faster than they can be repaired or replaced.</p>
<p><br>An aged or weaker cell cannot divide and multiply properly and eventually functions abnormally and dies.</p>
<p>ALL CELLS IN OUR BODY AGE WITH TIME!</p>
<p>Aging brings significant and visible changes in the body in terms of function and appearance. Some changes though, such as graying of the hair, are not that bad or harmful; but others can result in potential declines in senses and performance as well as an increased susceptibility to disability and many chronic diseases. Some of which include:</p>
<p>• Heart disease</p>
<p>• Cancer</p>
<p>• Neurodegenerative diseases including Parkinson’s, Alzheimer’s and other types of dementia</p>
<p>THE SLOW-AGING PROCESS</p>
<p><br>Medical researchers have made tremendous advancements in the field of aging and anti-aging. Today, we not only understand the phenomenon, but we have also successfully developed methods to slow down aging and live a long and disease-free life.</p>
<p>Many studies have highlighted that even though aging cannot be stopped, scientists are exploring the basic science behind aging (Gerontology) to understand various aspects and develop interventions. As a result of tremendous efforts in the space of gerontology, we now know for a fact that: Exercise and diet have a direct impact on life and health. Exercising daily and restricting certain diets, such as protein and those containing methionine, will slow age-related processes.</p>
<p>Over time, proteins aggregate in the form of plaques and tangles in the cells. Preventing protein aggregation can preserve health and increase the lifespan.</p>
<p>Men and women age differently. Exploring the underlying mechanism of aging in both sexes will help study and understand longevity better.</p>
<p>Researchers are exploring this field and provide promising answers that will add extra years to our life that we can spend with friends and family and enjoying fulfilling activities.</p>
<p>While aging is unavoidable, there are certain proven ways to slow down the process and add healthful years to life. However, with the information overload that exists today, figuring out what initiatives need to be taken to sustain your youthfulness can be extremely stressful and daunting.</p>
<p>SEVEN STEPS TO SLOW AGING &amp; PROMOTE YOUTHFULNESS</p>
<p>Here are seven steps, used by the Regenerative Medicine Expert Dr. Ross Carter. This will help you retain your youth and vitality.</p>
<p>1. GATHERING INFORMATION</p>
<p><br>The first step of an effective active-aging program comprises obtaining essential<br>and personalized health information to determine how well you are currently doing. Testing for significant factors such as nutrition, hydration, toxins, and stress helps prepare a customized anti-aging regime that keeps you feeling, looking, and performing better.</p>
<p>2. ADEQUATE SLEEP</p>
<p><br>Poor sleep is another major factor that hastens aging and disease. Most people are not getting the recommended daily sleep of 7-9 hours. Identifying and reversing the causative factors of poor sleep can play a huge part in boosting energy and recovery. In fact, sometimes simple things such as eliminating blue light from computers and televisions at night, reducing caffeine, and following a routine can dramatically improve quality of sleep and life.</p>
<p>3. IMPROVING MENTAL STATE</p>
<p>Psychological issues such as depression, stress and anxiety have often been associated with premature aging and a rapid decline in physiological health and function. However, people rarely register the importance of mental health, zeroing solely in on physical appearance. The active-aging methodology appearance. The active-aging methodology does the opposite; it focuses on managing and sustaining a positive mental state for optimal body functioning, which in turn helps keep up health and overall wellbeing. For superior mental health, one should consider adding daily rituals such as breath work, feeling grateful, and celebrating small achievements.</p>
<p><br>4. PERSONALIZED NUTRITION</p>
<p><br>In the past few years, customized nutrition has been developed to help protect our cells and their components from damage, extend their lifespan, and boost energy production. They do so by making up for any nutrients or minerals that are lacking from diet, hence promoting a healthy and active lifestyle. By utilizing epigenetics, or the expression of your genes, we can analyze metabolic biomarkers of cellular processes that are genetically, epigenetically, and environmentally altered. By assessing our ability to meet vital cellular functions, we can identify potential problem areas and minimize the effects even before they become health issues. Epigenetics allows scientists to identify exactly which nutrient you are deficient in and precisely what might be causing the deficiency. The information will help develop custom-made nutritional supplements created from specific vegetables, herbs, fruits, and spices, designed for your dietary needs.</p>
<p><br>5. ANTI-AGING DETOXIFICATION</p>
<p><br>Scientific data suggests that toxins, both environmental and endogenous, contribute majorly to molecular damage and physiological dysregulation, resulting in aging. Another important component of the 7-Step Program is detoxification that mainly focuses on eliminating toxins that speed up the internal and visual aging processes, therefore making you feel and look younger.</p>
<p>6. ADVANCED REGENERATIVE THERAPIES</p>
<p>Youth enhancing therapies such as PRP, stem cells, and exosomes are some of the treatments that the longevity program at HHI will include. These therapies trigger regeneration within the body and help reduce inflammation which keeps the body in a more youthful state.</p>
<p>When introduced into an aging body, regenerative therapy promotes self-renewal processes in the vital organs and tissues in addition to stimulating inactive stem cells. These processes enhance repair, boost immunity, and increase energy – aspects that help the body retain its vitality and youthfulness.</p>
<p>Stem-cell derived exosomes have also been utilized to repair aging cells. Their outstanding regenerative abilities influence cells to heal themselves and improve their strength and elasticity, subsequently slowing the onset of the aging process.</p>
<p>7. TRACKING<br>If you do not measure, you cannot manage. By utilizing the latest wearable tracking devices, we can manage and maintain our health and fitness, improve sleep, and find ways to recover from internal and external stress and injury. Tracking introduces feelings of accountability to the program and helps keep you motivated and informed on your progress and limitations.</p>
<p>A CUSTOMIZED ACTIVE-AGING PROGRAM, NOW OFFERED AT HIPPOCRATES Wellness — THE HIPPOCRATES LONGEVITY PROGRAM, IS BOUND TO ENHANCE YOUR HEALTH AND KEEP THE AGING PROCESS AT BAY. THE PROGRAM ENCOMPASSES THINGS THAT YOUR BODY NEEDS TO SLOW DOWN AND SUBSEQUENTLY DELAY THE PROCESS OF AGING.</p>

<strong><em>The Dawn of a New Age of Consciousness</em></strong>

Dear Friends,

As 2025 begins, my wife Anna Maria and I, who have had the honor to guide Hippocrates Wellness, the world-renowned pioneering institute of lifestyle medicine and advanced healthcare, wish you a year filled with vitality, hope, and transformation. This new year marks what we believe to be the dawn of a new era of consciousness, one where we recognize that the best healthcare is “<em>Self-Care,</em>” utilizing the foremost advanced, Western, and global practices.

As demonstrated by recent events, many of us feel completely disillusioned with the Global “healthcare” system. But this disillusionment also presents an opportunity, a chance to shift all of our focus from managing symptoms to

preventing illness and empowering ourselves with the tools for extraordinary health and longevity.

For 70 years, Hippocrates Wellness in West Palm Beach, Florida, has pioneered progressive medicine, liberating hundreds of thousands of lives worldwide. As directors and licensed nutritionists, Anna Maria and I along with our renowned medical team, from Harvard, MIT, Cambridge, &amp; Karolinska, continue to forge a proven direction in achieving an increased lifespan and a disease-free life. This is the new reality and future for a functioning global healthcare system.

Our 55-acre retreat in West Palm Beach, Florida, is a sanctuary for reversing illness and aging through advanced nutritional counseling, cutting edge technology, evidence-based therapies, luxuriating treatments, enlightening

lectures, and organic enzyme rich cuisine. This type of preventative medicine allows us not only to avoid illness, but to thrive physically, emotionally, and spiritually.

Together, we can build a healthier, more hopeful future. Come join us and begin anew at Hippocrates Wellness, the epicenter of the modern health and wellness revolution.

Yours in health,

___________________________________
